projects.content_zh: 木兰山古称建明山、青狮岭，传说中巾帼英雄花木兰生长于斯，因此而得名，山北麓有木兰祖庙、木兰将军庙及木兰将军墓。其山势峭拔，又有奇石松柏，自然环境优美，庙宇的修造始于隋唐，兴盛于明代，一度有七宫、八观、三十六殿的规模，是湖北道教名山之一。后因年久失修，大部分建筑被毁，现存主要建筑有木兰将军坊、木兰殿、金顶、玉皇阁牌坊和玉皇阁，近年又修复和重建了南天门、文昌宫、迎恩宫、斗姥宫、帝主宫等。以南天门为界，以上为道教建筑，以下为佛教建筑，两教在木兰山和睦相处，世代相传，形成了独特的木兰宗教文化。山中建筑依山就势，高低错落，多采用一种独特的'木庐干砌'法建造，即以木材为骨架，用大小不同的石板相间叠压，不用泥浆，形成独具一格的建筑风貌。木兰将军坊和木兰殿最早是唐代为表彰木兰将军而立，明代重建。木兰将军坊是一座四柱三楼的石牌坊，中门为拱券门洞，侧门由石块砌筑。横额书'忠孝勇节'四字，其下的两道额枋分别刻'双凤朝阳'和'二龙戏珠'，凤在上而龙在下，充分体现了世人的敬仰之情。石坊背面题有'唐木兰将军坊'六字。石坊之后为木兰殿，一层为石材墙体开拱券门，二层开木格子窗。殿内供奉三尊木兰将军像，分别着官服、铠甲和仕女装。木兰山最高处称为金顶，其上又有一座牌坊，高近7米，四柱三间，额枋正面书'金顶'，背面书'帝庭'，两旁有小字，左边是'大清光绪二十年'，右边是'宁波无名氏捐修'，建于明代，清代复修。牌坊后的金殿为现代重建，殿内供奉真武大帝和金童玉女、水火二将，是仿造武当山的金殿布置的。千尺峰上还有一组建筑，包括玉皇阁和玉皇阁牌坊。牌坊建于明代，四柱三楼石牌坊，正中开拱券门，正面书'第一天峰'四字，左右各有两字，分别为'日华''月映'。檐下置斗拱，正楼正脊为镂空雕刻。玉皇阁始建于唐朝，重建于明洪武二年（1369）。砖石结构，六边形平面，二层攒尖顶，每层檐下有石质斗拱，阁中供奉玉皇大帝。
projects.content_en: Mulan Mountain was anciently called Jianming Mountain and Qingshi Ridge; legend has it that the heroine Hua Mulan grew up here, hence the name. At the northern foot of the mountain are the Mulan Ancestral Temple, Mulan General Temple, and Mulan General's Tomb. With steep peaks, strange rocks, and pines and cypresses, the natural environment is beautiful. Temple construction began in the Sui and Tang dynasties and flourished in the Ming dynasty, once reaching the scale of seven palaces, eight temples, and thirty-six halls, making it one of Hubei's famous Daoist mountains. Later, due to long-term neglect, most buildings were destroyed; the main surviving buildings include the Mulan General Archway, Mulan Hall, Golden Summit, Jade Emperor Pavilion Archway, and Jade Emperor Pavilion. In recent years, the South Heaven Gate, Wenchang Palace, Ying'en Palace, Doumu Palace, and Dizhu Palace have been restored and rebuilt. With the South Heaven Gate as the boundary, above it are Daoist buildings and below it are Buddhist buildings; the two religions coexist harmoniously on Mulan Mountain, passed down through generations, forming a unique Mulan religious culture. The buildings in the mountain follow the terrain, staggered at different heights, mostly built using a unique 'mulu dry-stacking' method—using wood as the framework and stacking stone slabs of different sizes without mortar, forming a unique architectural style. The Mulan General Archway and Mulan Hall were first established in the Tang dynasty to honor General Mulan, rebuilt in the Ming dynasty. The Mulan General Archway is a four-column three-story stone archway, with the central gate an arched doorway and side gates built of stone blocks. The horizontal inscription reads 'Loyalty, Filial Piety, Bravery, Chastity'; below it, the two architraves are carved with 'Double Phoenixes Facing the Sun' and 'Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl,' with phoenixes above and dragons below, fully reflecting the world's admiration. The back of the stone archway is inscribed with 'Tang Mulan General Archway.' Behind the stone archway is Mulan Hall: the first story has stone walls with arched doors, and the second story has wooden lattice windows. The hall enshrines three statues of General Mulan, wearing official robes, armor, and women's attire respectively. The highest point of Mulan Mountain is called the Golden Summit, on which stands another archway, nearly 7 meters high, four columns and three bays. The front of the architrave reads 'Golden Summit,' the back reads 'Imperial Court,' with small characters on both sides: '20th year of Guangxu, Qing dynasty' on the left and 'Donated and repaired by an anonymous person from Ningbo' on the right; built in the Ming dynasty and restored in the Qing dynasty. The Golden Hall behind the archway is a modern reconstruction, enshrining the True Martial Emperor, Golden Boy and Jade Girl, and Water and Fire Generals, modeled after the Golden Hall on Wudang Mountain. On Qianchi Peak there is another group of buildings, including the Jade Emperor Pavilion and its archway. The archway was built in the Ming dynasty, a four-column three-story stone archway with an arched door in the center; the front reads 'First Heavenly Peak,' with two characters on each side—'Sun Glory' and 'Moon Reflection.' Bracket sets are placed under the eaves, and the main ridge of the central story is openwork carved. The Jade Emperor Pavilion was first built in the Tang dynasty and rebuilt in the 2nd year of Hongwu, Ming dynasty (1369). Brick-stone structure, hexagonal plan, two-story pyramidal roof, with stone bracket sets under each eave; the pavilion enshrines the Jade Emperor.

projects.name: 雨霖古建筑群
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 黄陂区木兰湖雨霖村
projects.address_en: Yulin Village, Mulan Lake, Huangpi District
projects.content_zh: 雨霖古建筑群位于黄陂区木兰湖雨霖村，是一处将湖北各地散落的古建筑搬迁复建而成的建筑群。这里汇集了来自湖北各地的明清古建筑，包括民居、祠堂、牌坊等多种类型。第一批复建的12栋建筑包括：一号馆（国民革命军第24师师部旧址）、二号馆（卢家老宅）、三号馆（阮和平老屋）、四号馆（阮士保老屋）、五号馆（廖氏官堂）、六号馆（庞氏老屋）、七号馆（舒家老屋）、八号馆（竹林旧宅）、九号馆（半部世家）、十号馆（陈献甲宗堂）、十一号馆（山陕会馆）、十二号馆（节孝坊）。其中，'半部世家'古建筑，原址阳新县白沙镇，建于清代，原屋主人赵启辉是北宋皇室后裔，老屋大门匾额上刻着'半部世家'，便出自赵匡胤'半部《论语》治天下'之说。老屋为一进天井院，硬山屋顶，正门上方有一根镂空雕刻的过梁，工艺非常精致。'竹林旧宅'原址通山县黄沙铺镇，建于清代初年，屋主的先祖为'竹林七贤'之一的阮籍。'山陕会馆'原址枣阳市鹿头镇，始建于明末。节孝坊是一座精美的石牌坊，建于清代，为表彰节妇而建，上面有精美的雕刻。
projects.content_en: The Yulin Ancient Building Complex is located in Yulin Village, Mulan Lake, Huangpi District. It is a complex formed by relocating and rebuilding ancient buildings scattered across various parts of Hubei. It gathers Ming and Qing ancient buildings from all over Hubei, including various types such as residences, ancestral halls, and memorial archways. The first batch of 12 rebuilt buildings includes: Hall 1 (former site of the 24th Division Headquarters of the National Revolutionary Army), Hall 2 (Lu Family Old House), Hall 3 (Ruan Heping Old House), Hall 4 (Ruan Shibao Old House), Hall 5 (Liao Official Hall), Hall 6 (Pang Family Old House), Hall 7 (Shu Family Old House), Hall 8 (Bamboo Forest Old Residence), Hall 9 (Half Ministry Family), Hall 10 (Chen Xianjia Ancestral Hall), Hall 11 (Shan-Shaan Guild Hall), and Hall 12 (Chastity and Filial Piety Archway). Among them, the 'Half Ministry Family' ancient building, originally at Baisha Town, Yangxin County, was built in the Qing dynasty. The original owner Zhao Qihui was a descendant of the Northern Song imperial family; the plaque on the old house's main gate is engraved with 'Half Ministry Family,' derived from Zhao Kuangyin's saying 'half of the Analects governs the world.' The old house is a one-courtyard residence with a gable roof; above the main gate is an openwork carved lintel, exquisitely crafted. The 'Bamboo Forest Old Residence,' originally at Huangshapu Town, Tongshan County, was built in the early Qing dynasty; the owner's ancestor was Ruan Ji, one of the 'Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove.' The 'Shan-Shaan Guild Hall,' originally at Lutou Town, Zaoyang City, was first built in the late Ming dynasty. The Chastity and Filial Piety Archway is an exquisite stone archway built in the Qing dynasty to honor a chaste widow, with exquisite carvings on it.

projects.name: 问津书院
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 新洲区旧街镇孔子河村孔子河畔
projects.address_en: By the Confucius River, Kongzihe Village, Jiujie Town, Xinzhou District
projects.content_zh: 《论语》中有一段，说到孔子带领弟子们周游列国，在楚国境内被一条大江拦住了去路。孔子派子路向不远处正在耕地的两位老人打听渡口。这两人正是在此隐居的高士长沮和桀溺，他们嘲笑子路说：孔子不是'生而知之'吗，哪里还需要问我们？当今天下就如这滔滔江水，你跟着孔子到处游历，还不如和我们一起做个隐士。子路没有办法，只好把原话告诉了孔子，孔子听后恍然叹道：人各有志，也只能各自坚持自己的选择了。'子路问津'的故事发生在哪里，如今不得而知。但问津书院历史悠久，相传西汉时期有农人耕地时掘得石碑一块，碑上以秦隶书写'子使子路问津处'，因此当时的淮南王刘安命人在此建碑亭，修文庙，设私学，供百姓瞻拜孔子，征召学士在此著书立说。自汉代至南宋末年，孔子庙得到了官府的多次拜谒和修缮，一代大儒朱熹还曾到此讲学。元初，江西庐陵名儒龙仁夫拒元不仕，效仿长沮、桀溺归隐山林，在此筑室讲学，时人称'孔子山庙学'或'龙仁夫书院'。元末明初，朱元璋与陈友谅在新洲一代大战，致使孔庙、书院毁于战火，后由地方官吏修复，并逐步受到官府的重视。万历年间，湖广巡抚熊尚文为书院题匾为'问津书院'。清代的问津书院渐渐成为官方科考取士之所，因而也得到了官方的保护和修复，并得到康熙皇帝御笔'万世师表'和嘉庆皇帝御笔'圣集大成'金匾。清中叶的问津书院坐北朝南，依山傍水，占地十余亩，有大成殿、讲堂、仪门、左右廊庑，前有文昌阁、魁星楼、藏书楼，还有孔叹桥、照壁，可谓文风鼎盛。经历清朝末年的动乱，大部分建筑倾塌，仅剩下大成殿、左右偏殿、孔叹桥，民国年间曾经修复并建有西洋风格的讲堂。大成殿为单檐硬山灰瓦顶，面阔五间，进深四间，穿斗式构架，内壁嵌重修孔庙碑8通，周围有'坐石'刻石、'孔子使子路问津处'石碑等。讲堂为二层歇山顶小楼，面阔三间，进深三间，二层有圆拱券外廊和栏杆，门窗亦为圆拱券，显示出一些西洋风味。书院前面的孔叹桥始建于明万历三十二年（1604），清咸丰元年（1851）重修，由东北至西南横跨在孔子河上。这座三孔石梁桥结构比较特殊，桥墩做梭形分水尖，可以减小流水对桥墩的冲击力，因而整个桥体十分稳固。
projects.content_en: In the Analects, there is a passage about Confucius leading his disciples traveling through various states, blocked by a great river within the territory of Chu. Confucius sent Zilu to ask two old men plowing nearby about the ferry crossing. These two were the reclusive scholars Chang Ju and Jie Ni, who mocked Zilu: 'Is not Confucius one who knows without learning? Why does he need to ask us? The world today is like this surging river; rather than following Confucius wandering everywhere, why not join us as recluses?' Zilu had no choice but to report their words to Confucius, who sighed in realization: 'People have different aspirations; each can only坚持 his own choice.' Where the story of 'Zilu asking about the ferry' took place is now unknown. But Wenjin Academy has a long history; legend has it that during the Western Han dynasty, a farmer digging in his fields unearthed a stone stele inscribed in Qin clerical script: 'The place where Zilu was sent to ask about the ferry.' Therefore, Liu An, the King of Huainan at the time, ordered a stele pavilion built here, a Confucian temple repaired, and a private school established, allowing common people to worship Confucius and summoning scholars to write and teach here. From the Han dynasty to the late Southern Song, the Confucius Temple received repeated official visits and repairs, and the great Confucian scholar Zhu Xi once lectured here. In the early Yuan dynasty, Long Renfu, a famous scholar from Luling, Jiangxi, refused to serve the Yuan and, following the example of Chang Ju and Jie Ni, retreated to the mountains and built a hall to lecture here; people called it the 'Confucius Mountain Temple School' or 'Long Renfu Academy.' At the end of the Yuan and beginning of the Ming, Zhu Yuanzhang and Chen Youliang fought a great battle around Xinzhou, destroying the Confucian temple and academy in the flames of war; they were later repaired by local officials and gradually received official attention. During the Wanli reign, Xiong Shangwen, the governor of Huguang, inscribed the plaque 'Wenjin Academy' for it. In the Qing dynasty, Wenjin Academy gradually became an official place for imperial examination candidates, thus receiving official protection and restoration, and was granted the golden plaques 'Teacher of Ten Thousand Generations' in the Kangxi emperor's own handwriting and 'Sage Collection Great Achievement' in the Jiaqing emperor's own handwriting. In the mid-Qing, Wenjin Academy faced south, nestled against mountains and water, covering over ten mu, with the Dacheng Hall, lecture hall, ritual gate, left and right corridors, and in front the Wenchang Pavilion, Kuixing Tower, Library Building, as well as the Confucius Sighing Bridge and screen wall—truly a flourishing place of literature. After the turmoil of the late Qing, most buildings collapsed, leaving only the Dacheng Hall, side halls, and Confucius Sighing Bridge; during the Republican period it was restored and a Western-style lecture hall built. The Dacheng Hall has a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, five bays wide and four bays deep, with a column-and-tie frame; its inner walls embed 8 steles recording the rebuilding of the Confucian temple, surrounded by 'Sitting Stone' carvings and the 'Place where Zilu was sent to ask about the ferry' stele. The lecture hall is a two-story small building with a hip-and-gable roof, three bays wide and three bays deep, with arched loggias and railings on the second story; doors and windows are also arched, showing some Western flavor. The Confucius Sighing Bridge in front of the academy was first built in the 32nd year of Wanli, Ming dynasty (1604), rebuilt in the 1st year of Xianfeng, Qing dynasty (1851), spanning the Confucius River from northeast to southwest. This three-hole stone beam bridge has a special structure: the piers are shaped like shuttles with water-dividing points, reducing the impact of flowing water on the piers, making the entire bridge very stable.

projects.name: 明楚王墓
projects.name_en: Ming Dynasty Tomb of Princes of Chu
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 江夏区龙泉乡龙泉山
projects.address_en: Longquan Mountain, Longquan Township, Jiangxia District
projects.type: 礼制建筑·木结构（多数已毁）
projects.content_zh: 明楚王墓是明代藩王的墓群，分布在龙泉山天马峰与玉屏峰形成的山坳之间，占地面积约760万平方米。明洪武三年（1370），明太祖朱元璋封第六子朱桢为楚王，藩武昌。朱桢生前将龙泉山定为'仙壤'，辟为寝山，并于洪武十四年（1381）开始营建茔园，设置陵卫及陵户看护王陵，'山内不许百姓行走，山外不许车马践踏'。此后的八位楚王也都埋葬于此，一直沿袭到明末。张献忠攻克武昌时，茔区遭到严重的破坏，清中叶后由当地百姓进行了修葺。九座楚王陵的总体布局和建筑依据明代王陵的规制，有内外垣、神道、金水桥、享殿和地宫等建筑，有'三龟九寝十二景'之称。地面上的木结构大部分已毁，仅存金水桥、台基、望柱栏板等石建筑和石构件。九陵中以朱桢的墓地昭园规模最大，保存也最好。昭园位于天马峰南麓，呈长方形，垣墙总长约1300米，设五门。正门有三个拱券门洞，进门依次为石桥、大殿、享殿和地宫。石桥拱券和享殿台基保存完好，而墓碑已毁。垣墙外左侧有一座碑亭，内有一座7米高的'楚昭王碑'，为明正统十二年（1447）所立，碑文记载朱桢生平。除昭园以外的八处茔园，宪园在昭园左侧，庄、愍、恭、靖、端、贺、康七茔园在玉屏峰北麓。除此以外，园区还有历代名人墓48座，共同构成宏大的古墓群。
projects.content_en: The Ming Dynasty Tombs of the Princes of Chu are a group of Ming dynasty vassal king tombs, distributed in the mountain valley formed by Tianma Peak and Yuping Peak of Longquan Mountain, covering about 7.6 million square meters. In the 3rd year of Hongwu, Ming dynasty (1370), the Hongwu Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang enfeoffed his sixth son Zhu Zhen as the Prince of Chu, with his fief at Wuchang. During his lifetime, Zhu Zhen designated Longquan Mountain as 'immortal soil,' converted it into a tomb mountain, and began building tomb gardens in the 14th year of Hongwu (1381), establishing tomb guards and tomb households to watch over the royal tombs: 'no common people may walk within the mountain, no horses or carts may trample outside the mountain.' The subsequent eight Princes of Chu were also all buried here, continuing until the late Ming. When Zhang Xianzhong captured Wuchang, the tomb area was severely damaged; after the mid-Qing, local people carried out repairs. The overall layout and buildings of the nine Chu prince tombs follow the regulations of Ming dynasty royal tombs, with inner and outer walls, spirit paths, Golden Water Bridges, offering halls, and underground palaces, known as 'three tortoises, nine tombs, twelve scenes.' Most above-ground wooden structures have been destroyed, leaving only stone buildings and components such as the Golden Water Bridges, platforms, and ornamental column railings. Among the nine tombs, the Zhaoyuan tomb of Zhu Zhen is the largest and best preserved. Zhaoyuan is located at the southern foot of Tianma Peak, rectangular in shape, with a total wall length of about 1,300 meters and five gates. The main gate has three arched doorways; entering the gate, one passes in sequence the stone bridge, main hall, offering hall, and underground palace. The stone bridge arches and offering hall platform are well preserved, while the tomb stele has been destroyed. Outside the wall on the left is a stele pavilion containing a 7-meter-high 'Chu Zhao King Stele,' erected in the 12th year of Zhengtong, Ming dynasty (1447), with an inscription recording Zhu Zhen's life. Besides Zhaoyuan, the other eight tomb gardens: Xianyuan is to the left of Zhaoyuan, and the seven tomb gardens of Zhuang, Min, Gong, Jing, Duan, He, and Kang are at the northern foot of Yuping Peak. In addition, the park contains 48 tombs of famous people of various dynasties, together forming a grand ancient tomb complex.

projects.name: 南桥
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 山坡乡贺站桥陈村六村大屋饶湾东北
projects.address_en: Northeast of Dawurao Bay, Liucun, Qiaozhanqiao Chen Village, Shanpo Township
projects.content_zh: 南桥始建于元代至正九年（1349年），是武汉市现存最早的，并且有确切年代可考的古桥。主体建筑是一座单孔半圆形石拱桥，长约37米，桥拱跨度近7米，桥面中间窄、两头宽，大概也是7米左右。桥拱两侧有'八'字形的挡水护坡，从底部向上逐渐收分，起到了支持河岸、保护桥身、减缓河水冲击的作用。桥身以红沙条石砌筑，用糯米石灰浆勾缝，桥面上铺大块青石板。桥拱券正中刻有'至正九年己丑春'题记，桥西头南面嵌一块写有'康熙三十六年'字样的青石碑，显示这一年南桥经历了一次较为重要的修缮。据考证，南桥由饶姓人东山公集资，带领当地人共同修建。据大屋饶村《饶氏宗谱》记载，南桥由本地的富户饶东山出资修建，是武昌南至咸宁、大冶路线的必经之处，因而当时这里有码头，也有不少居民，一度是十里八方一处热闹的场所，如今在桥的两端还能看到一些房屋的遗迹。《饶氏宗谱》中还记载了一段关于南桥和饶氏的故事，说明代的楚王府急用工料，想要拆桥取石，饶东山的后人陈情哀乞，力保南桥。此后南桥的历次修葺也多由饶氏出资出力，直到今天，大屋饶湾的村民也以饶姓为骄傲。除南桥以外，江夏区还保留了大量明清以来的石桥，有四十余座之多，大致可以分为石拱桥和平梁桥两种。这些古桥大多分布在较小的河流之上，以方便周边居民的出行，但随着岁月流逝，许多古桥渐渐失去功能，正在淡出人们的视野。
projects.content_en: South Bridge was first built in the 9th year of Zhizheng, Yuan dynasty (1349), and is the oldest surviving ancient bridge in Wuhan with a verifiable exact date. The main structure is a single-hole semicircular stone arch bridge, about 37 meters long, with an arch span of nearly 7 meters; the bridge deck is narrow in the middle and wide at both ends, also about 7 meters. On both sides of the arch are 'eight'-shaped water-retaining slope protections, gradually tapering from the bottom upward, serving to support the river banks, protect the bridge body, and slow the impact of river water. The bridge body is built of red sandstone blocks, with joints pointed using glutinous rice lime mortar, and the deck is paved with large bluestone slabs. The center of the arch is engraved with the inscription 'Spring of the Jichou year, 9th year of Zhizheng,' and a bluestone stele inscribed with '36th year of Kangxi' is embedded on the south side of the bridge's west end, indicating that South Bridge underwent a relatively important repair that year. According to research, South Bridge was built by a person surnamed Rao, Dongshan Gong, who raised funds and led local people in its construction. According to the 'Rao Family Genealogy' of Dawurao Village, South Bridge was funded by local wealthy merchant Rao Dongshan and was a necessary passage on the route from south Wuchang to Xianning and Daye; therefore there was a wharf here and many residents, once a bustling place for miles around. Today, traces of some houses can still be seen at both ends of the bridge. The 'Rao Family Genealogy' also records a story about South Bridge and the Rao family: during the Ming dynasty, the Chu Prince's Mansion urgently needed building materials and wanted to dismantle the bridge for its stone; Rao Dongshan's descendants pleaded earnestly, firmly protecting South Bridge. Since then, successive repairs of South Bridge have mostly been funded and carried out by the Rao family; to this day, the villagers of Dawurao Bay take pride in the Rao surname. Besides South Bridge, Jiangxia District also preserves over forty stone bridges from the Ming and Qing dynasties, roughly divided into stone arch bridges and flat beam bridges. Most of these ancient bridges are distributed over smaller rivers to facilitate travel for surrounding residents, but as time passes, many ancient bridges have gradually lost their function and are fading from people's view.

projects.name: 东坡赤壁
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 黄州区公园路11-1号
projects.address_en: No.11-1 Gongyuan Road, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 出黄冈古城西之汉川门，北面有一山陡峭如壁，山石颜色赤红，两汉时便有名为赤壁。西晋初年，龙骧将军蒯思为了纪念赤壁之战，始在山上建横江馆；唐代诗人杜牧、宋初散文家王禹偁先后被贬谪黄冈，赤壁之名日盛。北宋元丰三年（1080），苏轼因'乌台诗案'贬谪黄州。在黄州期间，苏轼处逆境而志存高远，遭挫折却大度豁达，每有闲情，常与友人泛舟赤壁下，赏明月、临清风、穿激流、荡碧波，抒怀壮志，写下了旷世奇作——前后《赤壁赋》和《念奴娇·赤壁怀古》。二赋一词灿若星斗，遂使黄州赤壁天下闻名。南宋末年，赤壁毁于兵燹，元、明、清三代多有修葺，现存建筑大多系同治七年（1868）重修。元明时期，因地方行政名称变动，曾以'黄州赤壁'称之，清康熙末年改名为'东坡赤壁'并沿用至今。赤壁矶东高西低，主要的建筑随山势而建，嵌于峭壁石矶之上，或临岩据险，或依山连岸，曲曲含方，小巧别致，以小径、院落相连，与地形结合浑然一体。主要的建筑物有二堂、三楼、二阁、一斋、九亭，又有一峰、一像，建筑与园林布局兼采南方园林之秀丽与官式风格之典雅庄重，亭台楼阁取名含蓄，温文尔雅，具有浓厚的人文色彩。苏轼在谪居黄州的四年多时间里，不仅创作了诗、词、文、赋数百篇，而且还留下了大量的书画作品，如《寒食诗帖》《月梅图》等。这些作品在明清时镌刻成碑，镶嵌在东坡赤壁的楼台亭阁之中。此外，这里还保存有苏轼晚期的一些书画作品，如谪居惠州时所作的《佛寿图》以及晚年书写的《临江仙·九十日春都过了》《行香子·清夜无尘》。这些书画碑刻总计139块，居古今名人个人书画碑刻之冠。苏轼与东坡赤壁在日本也有很高的知名度。1985年，日本著名的'东坡迷'山上次郎率'东坡参观访问团'来到东坡赤壁，出于对苏轼的景仰和对东坡赤壁的钟情，山上次郎慨然将珍藏的一卷《寒食帖》复制品捐赠给东坡赤壁管理处，这也是中国大陆唯一的一卷《寒食帖》珍品。1995年，又经山上次郎倡议，在东坡赤壁修建'中日友好之舍'，首次公开展出了这卷《寒食帖》的复制品。
projects.content_en: Exiting Hanchuan Gate west of the ancient Huangzhou city, to the north stands a mountain as steep as a wall, with reddish stone, known as Red Cliff since the Western Han dynasty. In the early Western Jin, General Kuai Si built the Hengjiang Pavilion on the mountain to commemorate the Battle of Red Cliff. Tang poet Du Mu and early Song prose writer Wang Yucheng were successively exiled to Huanggang, making Red Cliff increasingly famous. In the 3rd year of Yuanfeng, Northern Song (1080), Su Shi was exiled to Huangzhou due to the 'Wutai Poetry Case.' During his time in Huangzhou, Su Shi maintained high aspirations despite adversity, and was magnanimous and open-minded despite setbacks. In his leisure, he often boated with friends below Red Cliff, enjoying the bright moon, fresh breeze, rapids, and blue waves, expressing his ambitions, and writing masterpieces for the ages—the Former and Later 'Odes on the Red Cliff' and 'Niannujiao·Recalling the Past at Red Cliff.' These two odes and one ci poem shine like stars, making Huangzhou Red Cliff famous throughout the land. At the end of the Southern Song, Red Cliff was destroyed by war; it was repaired many times in the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties, and most existing buildings were rebuilt in the 7th year of Tongzhi (1868). During the Yuan and Ming, due to changes in local administrative names, it was called 'Huangzhou Red Cliff'; in the late Kangxi period of the Qing it was renamed 'Dongpo Red Cliff,' a name still used today. The Red Cliff rock is high in the east and low in the west; the main buildings follow the mountain's contours, embedded in the steep cliffs and rock projections, or perched on precipices, or connected to the banks, winding and containing squares, small and exquisite, connected by paths and courtyards, integrating seamlessly with the terrain. The main buildings include two halls, three towers, two pavilions, one study, and nine kiosks, plus one peak and one statue. The architecture and garden layout combine the elegance of southern gardens with the dignified formality of official style; the pavilions and towers have含蓄 names, gentle and refined, with a strong humanistic color. During his more than four years in exile in Huangzhou, Su Shi not only created hundreds of poems, ci, prose, and odes, but also left a large number of calligraphy and painting works, such as the 'Cold Food Poem Scroll' and 'Moon Plum Painting.' These works were engraved as steles in the Ming and Qing, embedded in the towers and pavilions of Dongpo Red Cliff. In addition, some of Su Shi's later calligraphy and painting works are preserved here, such as the 'Buddha Longevity Painting' made during his exile in Huizhou, and the 'Linjiangxian·Ninety Days of Spring Have Passed' and 'Xingxiangzi·Clear Night and Dustless' written in his later years. These calligraphy and painting steles total 139 pieces, ranking first among personal calligraphy and painting steles of famous people throughout history. Su Shi and Dongpo Red Cliff also have high recognition in Japan. In 1985, the famous Japanese 'Dongpo enthusiast' Kamiyama Jiro led a 'Dongpo Visit Delegation' to Dongpo Red Cliff. Out of admiration for Su Shi and affection for Dongpo Red Cliff, Kamiyama Jiro generously donated a replica of the treasured 'Cold Food Poem Scroll' to the Dongpo Red Cliff Management Office—also the only 'Cold Food Poem Scroll' treasure on the Chinese mainland. In 1995, at Kamiyama Jiro's initiative, a 'Sino-Japanese Friendship House' was built at Dongpo Red Cliff, publicly exhibiting this replica of the 'Cold Food Poem Scroll' for the first time.

projects.name: 二赋堂
projects.level: 风景建筑
projects.dynasty_en: Rebuilt in 7th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1868)
projects.address: 黄州区东坡赤壁内
projects.address_en: Inside Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 始建于清初，同治七年（1868）重建，以苏轼'赤壁二赋'得名。建筑坐北朝南，面阔三间，砖木结构，悬山小青瓦顶，'二赋堂'匾额为李鸿章题写。堂内空间以高3米的木屏分成前后室，正面刻清人程之桢楷书《前赤壁赋》，背面刻近代书法家李开铣书写《后赤壁赋》，前者豪迈俊逸，后者苍劲有力。
projects.content_en: First built in the early Qing, rebuilt in the 7th year of Tongzhi (1868), named after Su Shi's 'Two Odes on the Red Cliff.' The building faces south, three bays wide, brick-wood structure, with a gable roof of small gray tiles; the 'Erfu Hall' plaque was inscribed by Li Hongzhang. The interior space is divided into front and rear rooms by a 3-meter-high wooden screen; the front is engraved with the 'Former Ode on the Red Cliff' in regular script by Qing person Cheng Zhizhen, and the back is engraved with the 'Later Ode on the Red Cliff' written by modern calligrapher Li Kaixi—the former bold and elegant, the latter vigorous and powerful.

projects.name: 栖霞楼
projects.level: 风景建筑
projects.dynasty_en: Rebuilt in 1984 in Song dynasty style
projects.address: 黄州区东坡赤壁内
projects.address_en: Inside Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou District
highlights: 北宋黄州四大名楼之一
projects.content_zh: 北宋黄州四大名楼之一，苏轼赞为'郡中胜绝'。楼高四层，背山面江，落日时晚霞染红大江，映照楼身，如霞归栖，故名栖霞楼。原楼毁于宋末，明代重修，后又被毁。现有建筑为1984年仿宋代建筑样式重建的二层楼阁。
projects.content_en: One of the four famous towers of Huangzhou in the Northern Song, praised by Su Shi as 'the finest in the prefecture.' The tower is four stories high, backing the mountain and facing the river; at sunset, the evening glow dyes the great river red, reflecting on the tower body like rosy clouds alighting, hence the name Qixia (Rosy Clouds Resting) Tower. The original tower was destroyed at the end of the Song, rebuilt in the Ming, and later destroyed again. The existing building is a two-story tower rebuilt in 1984 in imitation of Song dynasty architectural style.

projects.name: 留仙阁
projects.level: 风景建筑
projects.address: 黄州区东坡赤壁内
projects.address_en: Inside Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 留仙之名取坡翁长留阁中之意，建于清光绪十年（1884）。阁内嵌有清代刘墉题跋的《东坡笠屐图》、清人杨守敬书写的《留仙阁记》和近代画家范家驹所作的《东坡游赤壁图》，前廊山墙上嵌有光绪十五年（1889）出土的苏轼手迹《乳母任氏墓志铭》，极为珍贵。
projects.content_en: The name Liuxian means 'the immortal (Su Shi) remains long in the pavilion'; built in the 10th year of Guangxu, Qing (1884). Inside the pavilion are embedded the 'Dongpo in Bamboo Hat and Sandals Painting' with colophon by Qing person Liu Yong, the 'Record of Liuxian Pavilion' written by Qing person Yang Shoujing, and the 'Dongpo Visiting Red Cliff Painting' by modern painter Fan Jiaju. On the front corridor gable wall is embedded Su Shi's handwritten 'Epitaph of Wet Nurse Ren,' unearthed in the 15th year of Guangxu (1889), extremely precious.

projects.name: 酹江亭
projects.name_en: Leijiang Pavilion (Libation to the River Pavilion)
projects.level: 风景建筑
projects.dynasty_en: Rebuilt in 7th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1868)
projects.address: 黄州区东坡赤壁内
projects.address_en: Inside Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou District
highlights: 康熙皇帝临摹赵孟頫书法
projects.content_zh: 面江临壁而建，始建于宋代，清同治七年（1868）重修，原名御书亭，后取《念奴娇·赤壁怀古》中'一樽还酹江月'之句，改名为酹江亭。亭中有历代名人的书画碑刻14块，其中包括康熙皇帝临摹元代书法家赵孟頫的《前赤壁赋》。
projects.content_en: Built facing the river and against the cliff, first built in the Song, rebuilt in the 7th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1868). Originally named Imperial Calligraphy Pavilion, later renamed Leijiang Pavilion taking the line 'a cup to the river and the moon' from 'Niannujiao·Recalling the Past at Red Cliff.' The pavilion contains 14 calligraphy and painting steles by famous people of various dynasties, including the 'Former Ode on the Red Cliff' copied by the Kangxi Emperor from Yuan dynasty calligrapher Zhao Mengfu.

projects.name: 坡仙亭
projects.level: 风景建筑
projects.dynasty_en: Rebuilt in 7th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1868)
projects.address: 黄州区东坡赤壁内
projects.address_en: Inside Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 坐落在赤壁矶头，清同治七年（1868）建成。亭内三面壁上嵌有历代名人书画碑刻26块，其中以苏轼亲笔草书的《念奴娇·赤壁怀古》词和别黄州时所作的《满庭芳·归去来兮》最令人称道，另有苏轼手绘的月梅图、寿星画像。如今亭下虽已死水微澜，但吟诵碑刻上的词句，遥想当年长江在脚下拍案而过，仍令人顿生豪迈之情。
projects.content_en: Located at the head of the Red Cliff rock, built in the 7th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1868). On the three walls inside the pavilion are embedded 26 calligraphy and painting steles by famous people of various dynasties, among which Su Shi's own cursive 'Niannujiao·Recalling the Past at Red Cliff' and the 'Mantingfang·Going Home' written when leaving Huangzhou are most praised, along with Su Shi's hand-painted moon plum painting and god of longevity portrait. Although the water below the pavilion is now stagnant with slight ripples, reciting the words on the steles and imagining the Yangtze River surging below in those days still evokes a sense of heroism.

projects.name: 睡仙亭
projects.level: 风景建筑
projects.address: 黄州区东坡赤壁内
projects.address_en: Inside Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou District
highlights: 平生睡足处，云梦泽南州
projects.content_zh: 沿着坡仙亭石阶向下，便来到睡仙亭。此亭面水而立，因杜牧'平生睡足处，云梦泽南州'而得名，相传当年苏轼同友人游赤壁时亦曾醉卧于此，亭内石床、石枕尚在。
projects.content_en: Heading down the stone steps from Poxian Pavilion, one arrives at Shuixian Pavilion. This pavilion stands facing the water, named after Du Mu's line 'the place where one sleeps fully in life, south of the Yunmeng Marsh.' Legend has it that when Su Shi visited Red Cliff with friends, he once slept drunk here; the stone bed and stone pillow inside the pavilion remain.

projects.name: 放龟亭
projects.level: 风景建筑
projects.dynasty_en: Rebuilt in 7th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1868)
projects.address: 黄州区东坡赤壁内
projects.address_en: Inside Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 从睡仙亭再向前是放龟亭，为清同治七年（1868）重建。放龟之事，见于《晋书·言宝传》，东晋晋大将毛宝戍守邾城时，其仆人将他买食的白龟放生于此，后得善报。明嘉靖二十八年（1549），黄州知府郭凤仪依据史书的记载，在赤壁矶头白龟渚凿一巨大白石龟，以彰显善恶有报的往事，亭名亦由此而得。
projects.content_en: Further forward from Shuixian Pavilion is Fanggui Pavilion, rebuilt in the 7th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1868). The story of releasing a turtle is found in the 'Book of Jin·Biography of Yan Bao.' When Eastern Jin general Mao Bao garrisoned Zhucheng, his servant released the white turtle he had bought for food here, and later received good retribution. In the 28th year of Jiajing, Ming (1549), Huangzhou prefect Guo Fengyi, based on historical records, carved a giant white stone turtle at White Turtle Shoal on the Red Cliff head, to highlight the story of good and evil receiving their due; the pavilion's name also derives from this.

projects.name: 问鹤亭
projects.level: 风景建筑
projects.address: 黄州区东坡赤壁内
projects.address_en: Inside Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 原名为'玩月台'，因位置高显，为赏月佳处。1922年扩建赤壁时，为彰显《后赤壁赋》中孤鹤化为道士与苏轼问答的韵事，始更名为问鹤亭。
projects.content_en: Originally named 'Moon-Playing Platform,' because of its high and prominent position, it was an excellent place for moon viewing. When Red Cliff was expanded in 1922, to highlight the anecdote in the 'Later Ode on the Red Cliff' where a lone crane transforms into a Daoist and converses with Su Shi, it was renamed Wenhe (Crane-Asking) Pavilion.

projects.name: 青云塔
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 黄州区赤壁街道办事处钵盂山
projects.address_en: Boyu Mountain, Chibi Subdistrict Office, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 位于黄州故城南门东侧，始建于明万历二年（1574）。清道光二十八年（1848）重建，光绪五年（1879）再次修复。塔身八角七层，仿木楼阁，外观朴素而不施雕饰，内部空心，可以沿石阶登临。第一层塔身侧面分别楷书八卦名，西北乾门门额嵌'全楚文峰'，东面巽门对面石壁上则书'青云直上'。可见青云塔虽毗邻安国寺，却非佛塔，而是一座风水塔，因而也称为文峰塔。
projects.content_en: Located east of the south gate of the ancient Huangzhou city, first built in the 2nd year of Wanli, Ming (1574). Rebuilt in the 28th year of Daoguang, Qing (1848), and repaired again in the 5th year of Guangxu (1879). The pagoda body is octagonal with seven stories, imitating a wooden multi-eaved tower, with a simple exterior without carvings; the interior is hollow and can be climbed via stone steps. On the sides of the first story body are the eight trigrams names in regular script respectively; the northwest Qian gate lintel is embedded with 'Literary Peak of All Chu,' and on the stone wall opposite the east Xun gate is written 'Rising Straight to the Blue Clouds.' It can be seen that although Qingyun Pagoda is adjacent to Anguo Temple, it is not a Buddhist pagoda but a feng shui pagoda, hence also called Wenfeng (Literary Peak) Pagoda.

projects.name: 文庙
projects.level: 市级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 黄州区考棚街黄冈实验学校院内
projects.address_en: Inside Huanggang Experimental School, Kaopeng Street, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 在明清两代的地方建筑中，由地方文庙和儒学共同构成的'官学'是一种重要的类型。黄州府试院（贡院）俗称为'黄州考棚'，是古代黄州主持科举考试的专门机构，也是平时本府秀才读书的地方。明朝以前，黄州考棚没有固定场所，每逢考试，考场就临时设在官宦大户人家。固定的考棚始建于清朝初年，当时有大堂、二堂，堂下建有诸多号舍。号舍即考场，由三面墙围合而成，大致为一米见方，无门，内有两块活动木板，白天作为考试用的桌椅，夜晚则拼合为床榻。诸多号舍以'千字文'顺序编号，每间供一位考生使用，排列整齐。经过清朝不断扩建，考棚具有了相当的规模。考棚的东侧为文庙，始建于明中期，清代重建，曾经有泮池、棂星门、大成门、名宦祀、乡贤祀、大殿、崇圣祀、明伦堂等建筑，现仅存大殿。大殿坐北朝南，重檐歇山屋顶，用黄琉璃瓦，具有明显的官式建筑风格，现在作为黄冈实验学校的图书馆使用。文庙正门前的考棚街因考棚而得名。每当考期来临，黄州府属下的各县考生，连同送考的家人、书童，纷纷在试院附近下榻备考。此时黄州城车水马龙、热闹异常，考棚街上有客栈、饭馆、日杂百货、文房四宝等生意十分兴隆，逐渐形成了一条繁华的街道。据统计，黄冈科举共有进士将近千人，其中著名的有程颢、程颐、李时珍、陈沆、董必武、黄侃、熊十力等。光绪三十年（1904），也就是科举制度废除的前一年，黄州府试院改为黄州府中学堂，是今天黄冈中学的前身，也是鄂东第一所中学。
projects.content_en: In local architecture of the Ming and Qing dynasties, the 'official school' composed of the local Confucian temple and the Confucian school was an important type. The Huangzhou Prefecture Examination Academy (tribute academy) was commonly called 'Huangzhou Examination Shed,' a specialized institution for hosting imperial examinations in ancient Huangzhou, and also a place for the prefecture's xiucai (cultivated talents) to study in ordinary times. Before the Ming, Huangzhou had no fixed examination venue; during examinations, the exam site was temporarily set up in the homes of wealthy officials. The fixed examination shed was first built in the early Qing, with a main hall and second hall, and many numbered cells below. The numbered cells were examination rooms, enclosed by three walls, roughly one meter square, without doors; inside were two movable wooden boards, used as desks and chairs for exams during the day, and joined together as a bed at night. The many cells were numbered in the order of the 'Thousand Character Classic,' each for one examinee, arranged neatly. Through continuous expansion in the Qing, the examination shed reached considerable scale. East of the examination shed was the Confucian temple, first built in the mid-Ming and rebuilt in the Qing. It once had buildings such as the Pan Pond, Lingxing Gate, Dacheng Gate, Official Worthies Shrine, Local Worthies Shrine, Main Hall, Chongsheng Shrine, and Minglun Hall; now only the Main Hall remains. The Main Hall faces south, with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof covered with yellow glazed tiles, with an obvious official architectural style, and is now used as the library of Huanggang Experimental School. Kaopeng (Examination Shed) Street in front of the Confucian temple is named after the examination shed. Whenever the examination period arrived, candidates from all counties under Huangzhou Prefecture, along with family members and servants accompanying them, stayed near the examination academy to prepare. At this time, Huangzhou city was bustling with traffic; Kaopeng Street had inns, restaurants, general merchandise, and the four treasures of the study (brush, ink, paper, inkstone), with very prosperous business, gradually forming a bustling street. According to statistics, Huangzhou had nearly a thousand jinshi (presented scholars) in the imperial examinations, among whom the famous include Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Li Shizhen, Chen Hang, Dong Biwu, Huang Kan, and Xiong Shili. In the 30th year of Guangxu (1904), the year before the abolition of the imperial examination system, the Huangzhou Prefecture Examination Academy was changed to the Huangzhou Prefecture Middle School, the predecessor of today's Huanggang High School and the first middle school in eastern Hubei.

projects.name: 中湾民居
projects.level: 市级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 黄州区考棚街黄冈实验学校院内
projects.address_en: Inside Huanggang Experimental School, Kaopeng Street, Huangzhou District
projects.content_zh: 百丈岩村坐落在团风县东北部的龙王山脚下，偏僻而路远。依山而上，在一个山坳口处，可见到一座白色大理石牌坊掩映在绿竹之中。牌坊为四柱三间，二重楼阁式，中门匾额阴刻'春秋万古'，额枋浮雕龙风、翠柏、麒麟等图案。牌坊之后原有林氏祠堂，不知毁于何年。百丈岩村按位置高低分为上湾、中湾和下湾，原林氏老屋也分布在这三湾之中，现存的中湾民居只是林氏家产的一小部分。据《林氏宗谱》和《黄冈县志》记载，林知堂在清道光年间曾任开封知府，据说从百丈岩村到黄州府约60公里的道路，均不通过他人的地盘，其田产之多令人咋舌。村中房屋曾多达两千余间，并修筑寨墙将三湾围在其中，寨内有花园，墙上有哨楼。村前的'春秋万古'牌坊，就是林氏女婿为老丈人祝寿所建。当地关于林氏发家的传说五花八门，...
projects.content_en: Baizhangyan Village is located at the foot of Longwang Mountain in the northeast of Tuanfeng County, remote and far from roads. Going up the mountain, at a mountain pass, one can see a white marble memorial archway half-hidden among green bamboos. The archway has four columns and three bays, in a two-story pavilion style; the central gate lintel is intaglio-carved with 'Eternal Through Spring and Autumn,' and the architrave has relief carvings of dragons and phoenixes, green cypresses, and qilin. Behind the archway originally stood the Lin Family Ancestral Hall, destroyed in an unknown year. Baizhangyan Village is divided by elevation into Upper Bay, Middle Bay, and Lower Bay; the original Lin family old houses were also distributed among these three bays, and the existing Zhongwan (Middle Bay) dwellings are only a small part of the Lin family property. According to the 'Lin Family Genealogy' and 'Huanggang County Annals,' Lin Zhitang served as prefect of Kaifeng during the Daoguang period of the Qing; it is said that the road from Baizhangyan Village to Huangzhou Prefecture, about 60 kilometers, did not pass through others' land, and the amount of his farmland was staggering. The village once had over 2,000 rooms, with fortress walls enclosing the three bays; inside the fortress there were gardens, and watchtowers on the walls. The 'Eternal Through Spring and Autumn' archway in front of the village was built by Lin's son-in-law for his father-in-law's birthday. Local legends about how the Lin family made their fortune are varied, ...

projects.name: 东岳庙
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 团风县总路咀镇东岳庙村东岳村
projects.address_en: Dongyue Village, Dongyue Temple Village, Zongluzui Town, Tuanfeng County
projects.content_zh: 东岳庙戏台始建于明洪武年间，明万历二年（1574）重修。现存最重要的建筑是山门对面的戏台，也叫万年台。戏台坐南朝北，距离山门约40米，戏台与山门间的广场可以容纳数千人。戏台平面呈'凸'字形，分前后台，面阔三间，进深两间，台高为2米。前台为重檐歇山灰瓦顶，后台为硬山灰瓦顶，两侧封火山墙。戏台主体为抬梁式构架，两山为穿斗式构架。前台檐下施如意斗拱装饰，台内原有八卦藻井，虽已毁坏，但轮廓依然可见。前后台之间用直棂木隔扇区分，两侧设有上下场门。前檐的正中，下层屋檐断开，中悬一块匾额，上书'春台'二字。戏台装饰精美，浮雕栩栩如生。额枋与雀替均雕刻龙凤花纹，雀替还雕刻花卉植物图案；斜撑是一条完整的游龙，阑额上则为对弈、饮酒、吟诗、作画等古代生活的场景。
projects.content_en: The Dongyue Temple stage was first built during the Hongwu period of the Ming, and rebuilt in the 2nd year of Wanli (1574). The most important surviving building is the stage opposite the mountain gate, also called the Wannian (Ten Thousand Year) Stage. The stage faces north, about 40 meters from the mountain gate; the square between the stage and gate can accommodate several thousand people. The stage plan is 'convex'-shaped, divided into front and back stages, three bays wide and two bays deep, with a stage height of 2 meters. The front stage has a double-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, the back stage has a gable gray-tile roof, with fire-sealing gable walls on both sides. The main body of the stage uses a post-and-lintel frame, with the two gables using a column-and-tie frame. Under the front eave are ruyi bracket set decorations; the stage originally had a Bagua caisson ceiling, which although destroyed, its outline is still visible. The front and back stages are separated by straight-lattice wooden partitions, with entrance and exit doors on both sides. In the center of the front eave, the lower eave is断开, with a plaque hanging in the middle inscribed with 'Spring Stage.' The stage is exquisitely decorated with lifelike reliefs. Both the architraves and spandrel brackets are carved with dragon and phoenix patterns; the spandrel brackets also carve floral and plant patterns; the diagonal brace is a complete swimming dragon, and the lintel depicts scenes of ancient life such as playing chess, drinking, reciting poetry, and painting.

projects.name: 柏子塔
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 麻城市阎家河镇柏子塔村九龙山上
projects.address_en: On Jiulong Mountain, Baizita Village, Yanjiahe Town, Macheng City
projects.content_zh: 柏子塔位于麻城市区东北10公里的九龙山上，塔下有九龙寺，又有柏子塔村。根据《黄州府志》记载：'九龙寺在县东北九龙山上，唐德宗四年虚应禅师建寺，有柏子塔，塔九级，覆以铁镬，镬侧一柏蟠根而生，故名。'唐德宗建中四年即公元783年，今天所见的柏子塔是一座六角仿木楼阁式砖塔，残高七层，近35米，为宋代重建。塔身采用双层套筒结构，从底层南门可以进入塔内，沿螺旋踏道登临塔顶。外观每层由塔身、斗拱、出檐和平座层组成，细致地模仿了木结构的做法，五层及以上的平座改为仰莲瓣形式。二层以上相间置拱券门和球纹格眼窗，墙身无其他装饰。各层收分严谨，形成挺拔的塔身轮廓，颇有古朴之风范。九龙山为当地地势最高的一处山岗，山体由红砂岩构成，由中心向四周蜿蜒伸展，如九条巨龙环绕盘旋。而柏子塔又高矗于中心平岗之上，周围起伏的丘陵一望无际，不可不谓形胜。《麻城县志》载，'每立秋日午，塔身无影'，'柏子秋荫'也成为麻城八景之一。
projects.content_en: Baizi Pagoda is located on Jiulong (Nine Dragons) Mountain, 10 kilometers northeast of Macheng city. Below the pagoda is Jiulong Temple, and there is also Baizita Village. According to the 'Huangzhou Prefecture Annals': 'Jiulong Temple is on Jiulong Mountain northeast of the county, built by Master Xuying in the 4th year of Tang Dezong; there is a Baizi Pagoda, nine stories, covered with an iron cauldron, with a cypress tree growing with coiled roots beside the cauldron, hence the name.' The 4th year of Jianzhong of Tang Dezong is 783 AD; the Baizi Pagoda seen today is a hexagonal imitation-wood multi-eaved brick pagoda, with a remaining height of seven stories, nearly 35 meters, rebuilt in the Song dynasty. The pagoda body uses a double-layer sleeve structure; one can enter the pagoda from the south gate on the ground floor and climb to the top via a spiral staircase. Externally, each story consists of the pagoda body, bracket sets, eaves, and a mezzanine level, meticulously imitating wooden structure practices; the mezzanines on the fifth story and above are changed to upward-facing lotus petal forms. Above the second story, arched doors and ball-pattern lattice windows are placed alternately, with no other decoration on the walls. Each story tapers rigorously, forming a tall and straight pagoda silhouette, with quite an ancient and simple style. Jiulong Mountain is the highest hill in the local area, composed of red sandstone, winding from the center to the surroundings like nine giant dragons coiling around. And Baizi Pagoda stands tall on the central flat hill, with the surrounding rolling hills stretching to the horizon—truly a scenic spot. The 'Macheng County Annals' records that 'at noon on the Start of Autumn day, the pagoda body has no shadow'; 'Baizi Autumn Shade' also became one of the Eight Scenes of Macheng.

projects.name: 五脑山庙
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 麻城市区西北5公里五脑山林场
projects.address_en: Wunao Mountain Forest Farm, 5 km northwest of Macheng city
projects.content_zh: 庙名为'帝主庙'，自宋代创立以来，一直是道教重要的活动场所，现存建筑于清嘉庆年间重修。庙门位于山脚，而建筑序列始于山腰，依山就势，中轴线上有静心亭、一天门、二天门和钟鼓楼、大殿（紫微宫），两侧又有玉清宫、斗姥殿、观音阁，以及凉亭、宿舍、厨房等附属建筑。中轴线上除静心亭外，多数建筑为清代原构，玉清宫亦为原构，其他建筑多为'文革'后整修重建。一天门为牌楼屋式门殿，牌楼部分表面在仿木结构的框架中，装点各式浮雕动物、人物形象和图案纹样，正中檐下还以砖砌出'敕封'匾的形象。浮雕动物和人物多呈白色，局部涂土黄色、青绿色，远观效果丰富而华丽。二天门与大殿一道组成两进天井式院落，大殿面阔三间，殿前两侧以麻石砌起两座小屋作为钟鼓楼，大殿梁架上布满丰富的木雕彩色人物，具有浓郁的世俗气息。每进房屋的封火山墙各不相同，形成十分丰富的天际线。周围茂林修竹，环境清幽，向南可以俯瞰整个麻城市区。五脑山庙所奉之帝主，又称福主、紫微侯、张七相公，是起源于麻城而后流传于整个鄂东地区的民间神祗，后来又随着黄州商人的脚步流传到鄂中、鄂西、四川等地。帝主在鄂东地区频频'显圣'，明清两代官方都有加封，也被称为'川楚御灾捍患之神'。
projects.content_en: The temple is named 'Dizhu Temple' (Emperor Lord Temple); since its founding in the Song dynasty, it has been an important Daoist activity venue. The existing buildings were rebuilt during the Jiaqing period of the Qing. The temple gate is at the foot of the mountain, while the building sequence begins at the mountainside, following the terrain. On the central axis are the Jingxin (Mind-Calming) Pavilion, First Heaven Gate, Second Heaven Gate, Bell and Drum Towers, and Main Hall (Ziwei Palace); on both sides are the Yuqing Palace, Doumu Hall, Guanyin Pavilion, as well as附属 buildings such as pavilions, dormitories, and kitchens. Except for the Jingxin Pavilion, most buildings on the central axis are original Qing structures; the Yuqing Palace is also original, while other buildings were mostly renovated and rebuilt after the Cultural Revolution. The First Heaven Gate is a memorial-arch-style gate hall; the surface of the memorial arch part, within an imitation-wood structure framework, is decorated with various relief animals, human figures, and patterns; directly under the central eave, a brick 'Imperially Bestowed' plaque形象 is also made. The relief animals and figures are mostly white, with parts painted earth yellow and blue-green, creating a rich and gorgeous effect from afar. The Second Heaven Gate and the Main Hall together form a two-courtyard layout; the Main Hall is three bays wide, with two small houses built of granite on both sides in front as bell and drum towers. The Main Hall's beam frame is covered with rich wood-carved colored figures, with a strong secular atmosphere. The fire-sealing gable walls of each courtyard's buildings are different, forming a very rich skyline. Surrounded by lush forests and tall bamboos, the environment is serene; looking south, one can overlook the entire Macheng urban area. The Dizhu (Emperor Lord) worshipped at Wunao Mountain Temple, also called Fuzhu (Blessing Lord), Ziwei Hou, or Zhang Qixianggong, is a folk deity originating in Macheng and later spreading throughout the eastern Hubei region, then following the footsteps of Huangzhou merchants to central Hubei, western Hubei, Sichuan, and other places. The Dizhu frequently 'manifested miracles' in eastern Hubei; both the Ming and Qing governments bestowed titles on him, and he was also called the 'God of Sichuan and Chu for Warding Off Disasters and Calamities.'

projects.name: 圣庙
projects.level: 市级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 麻城市陵园路48号
projects.address_en: No.48 Lingyuan Road, Macheng City
projects.content_zh: 即文庙、孔庙，始建于宋代，元末毁于兵燹，明洪武年间重建，明清两代多次重修。原位于市委机关院内，1994年迁建于现址。现仅存大成殿，坐北朝南，面阔五间，进深四间，重檐歇山青瓦顶。檐下施斗拱，额枋浮雕云龙，正面三间为隔扇门窗。1926年，中共麻城县委在此成立。
projects.content_en: Also called the Confucian Temple or Kong Temple, first built in the Song dynasty, destroyed by war at the end of the Yuan, rebuilt during the Hongwu period of the Ming, and repaired many times in the Ming and Qing. Originally located in the municipal party committee compound, it was relocated to the current site in 1994. Now only the Dacheng Hall remains, facing south, five bays wide and four bays deep, with a double-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof. Bracket sets are placed under the eaves; the architrave has relief carvings of cloud dragons; the front three bays have lattice doors and windows. In 1926, the Macheng County Committee of the Communist Party of China was established here.

projects.name: 玉皇阁经幢
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 麻城市宋埠镇朱冲村青山寨顶
projects.address_en: Top of Qingshan Village, Zhuchong Village, Songbu Town, Macheng City
projects.content_zh: 玉皇阁位于一处明末农民义军山寨的寨顶之上，当地人称'玉阁'，山上还保留有部分石质寨墙、寨门、哨所和生活水池等。根据碑文记载，玉皇阁始创于唐代，原有三重庙宇，现仅存三间牌楼式经幢，为明代中叶重建。经幢坐北朝南，为石材砌筑的仿木结构，分为上下两层。下层已经被水泥封住，不能见其原貌，上层保存较好，四角为浮雕方形盘龙石柱，正面本有两棵较细的圆形盘龙石柱，但西侧的一棵已丢失无存。原屋顶也应为石板，檐下斗拱出两跳，且第二跳计心，两侧的山墙上也有同样形制的斗拱和披檐。梁枋、槅扇、斗拱上，有大量人物、云龙、凤鸟、花卉等浮雕装饰，室内正面普拍枋上还雕刻有二人对弈的场景。玉皇阁经幢与普通的经幢有很大不同，反而更像是一座楼阁。它保留了经幢石质结构和造型繁复、讲究雕刻的特点，又忠实地模仿了木结构建筑的形式。而通身遍布的浮雕装饰则有很强的感染力，具有重要的历史价值和建筑艺术价值。
projects.content_en: Yuhuang Pavilion is located on the top of a mountain stronghold of a late-Ming peasant rebel army, locally called 'Yu Ge' (Jade Pavilion). Part of the stone fortress walls, gates, sentry posts, and living water pools remain on the mountain. According to stele records, Yuhuang Pavilion was first founded in the Tang dynasty, originally with three temple halls; now only a three-bay memorial-arch-style pillar (jingchuang) remains, rebuilt in the mid-Ming. The pillar faces north-south, is a stone-built imitation-wood structure, divided into upper and lower levels. The lower level has been sealed with cement, so its original appearance cannot be seen; the upper level is well preserved, with four corners as relief-carved square coiled-dragon stone columns. The front originally had two thinner circular coiled-dragon stone columns, but the western one has been lost. The original roof should also be stone slabs; under the eaves, bracket sets project two tiers, with the second tier counting the center; the gable walls on both sides also have bracket sets and eaves of the same type. On the beams, architraves, lattice windows, and bracket sets, there are大量 relief decorations of figures, cloud dragons, phoenix birds, and flowers; on the front interior pubai fang (plate architrave), a scene of two people playing chess is also carved. The Yuhuang Pavilion pillar is very different from ordinary pillars (jingchuang), instead more like a pavilion. It retains the stone structure and complex, carving-oriented characteristics of a pillar, while faithfully imitating the form of a wooden structure. The relief decorations covering the entire body have strong appeal, with important historical value and architectural artistic value.

projects.name: 王氏祠
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 麻城市黄土岗镇桐枧冲村
projects.address_en: Tongjianchong Village, Huangtugang Town, Macheng City
projects.content_zh: 坐落在风景优美的桐枧冲瀑布景区附近，背倚青山，始建于嘉庆年间。祠堂坐西朝东，硬山屋顶，砖木混合结构。王氏祠堂的保存状况较差，内部几乎全部坍塌，树木丛生，大门和两壁的过梁为仅存的木结构，梁枋雕刻细致精美，部分墙砖上还有'王氏祠'字样，表明是为建造祠堂而特别烧制的砖料。
projects.content_en: Located near the scenic Tongjianchong Waterfall, backed by green mountains, first built during the Jiaqing period. The ancestral hall faces east, with a gable roof and a brick-wood composite structure. The Wang's Ancestral Hall is in poor condition, with the interior almost entirely collapsed and overgrown with trees; the main gate and the lintels of both walls are the only surviving wooden structures, with exquisitely carved beams and architraves. Some wall bricks also bear the characters 'Wang's Ancestral Hall,' indicating they were specially fired for the construction of the hall.

projects.name: 雷氏祠
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 麻城市盐田河镇百亩堰村
projects.address_en: Baimu Village, Yantianhe Town, Macheng City
projects.content_zh: 始建于清嘉庆六年（1801），三进天井式院落，有朝门、厅堂和后堂，两侧对称布置厢房。外墙檐下彩画戏曲人物故事，题材丰富，画面也十分精美。朝门背面有一座石柱、石栏杆的戏楼，戏楼下是一道小巧的圆拱桥，跨越天井，通往正厅。正厅面阔五间，进深三间，是族人议事的场所，也称为议事厅。整个祠堂内共有20根石柱，其中以戏台前檐的两棵盘龙柱雕刻最为精致，而勾栏、裙板、副手、抱鼓等处也布满了石雕装饰，大门左右还置有石狮，整体雕刻风格精细繁缛、内容丰富多彩，是大别山地区保存十分完好、具有较高建设艺术价值的一座古祠堂。
projects.content_en: First built in the 6th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1801), a three-courtyard layout with a gate hall, main hall, and rear hall, with wing rooms symmetrically arranged on both sides. Under the exterior wall eaves are painted opera figure stories, with rich themes and very exquisite pictures. On the back of the gate hall is a stage with stone columns and stone railings; below the stage is a small circular arch bridge spanning the courtyard, leading to the main hall. The main hall is five bays wide and three bays deep, a place for clan members to discuss affairs, also called the Discussion Hall. The entire ancestral hall has 20 stone columns; among them, the two coiled-dragon columns at the front eave of the stage are the most exquisitely carved, while the railings, skirt boards, handrails, and drum-shaped stone supports are also covered with stone carvings. Stone lions are placed on both sides of the main gate. The overall carving style is fine and elaborate, with rich and colorful content; it is an ancient ancestral hall very well preserved in the Dabie Mountain area, with high architectural artistic value.

projects.name: 七里坪镇长胜街及民居
projects.name_en: Changsheng Street and Vernacular Buildings in Qiliping Town
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 红安县七里坪镇
projects.address_en: Qiliping Town, Hong'an County
projects.content_zh: 七里坪镇位于红安县北部，鄂、豫两省的交界处，大别山余脉天台山的南麓，是鄂、豫、皖三省交界处的重要贸易集散中心之一，在第二次国内革命战争时期则是鄂豫皖苏区政府所在地。镇中的长胜街原名为正街，始建于明末清初，后因当地百姓企盼太平军打胜仗，改名为长胜街。全长约400米，1949年后又续建了近300米，宽约7米。长胜街南北各有一座花岗砌成的城门，两侧房屋则清一色青砖黑瓦，相邻房屋共用山墙，墙头上扬，使得街道呈现出一种优美的韵律感。沿街共有128栋明清建筑，整体保存状况较好。住宅以前店后宅为主，一般为单开间或双开间，内有天井院。
projects.content_en: Qiliping Town is located in the north of Hong'an County, at the junction of Hubei and Henan provinces, at the southern foot of Tiantai Mountain, a branch of the Dabie Mountains. It is one of the important trade distribution centers at the junction of Hubei, Henan, and Anhui provinces, and during the Second Revolutionary Civil War period it was the seat of the Hubei-Henan-Anhui Soviet Area government. Changsheng Street in the town was originally called Zhengjie (Main Street), first built in the late Ming and early Qing, later renamed Changsheng (Long Victory) Street because local people hoped the Taiping Army would win battles. It has a total length of about 400 meters; after 1949, nearly 300 meters were added, with a width of about 7 meters. Changsheng Street has a granite city gate at each of its north and south ends; the houses on both sides are uniformly gray brick and black tile, with adjacent houses sharing gable walls and raised wall tops, giving the street a beautiful sense of rhythm. There are 128 Ming and Qing buildings along the street, in generally good condition. The residences are mainly front-shop-back-house types, generally single or double bay, with interior courtyards.

projects.name: 陡山吴氏祠
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 红安县八里湾镇陡山村
projects.address_en: Doushan Village, Baliwan Town, Hong'an County
projects.content_zh: 陡山村坐落在八里湾镇东北，群山环绕之中，村里还保留了不少年代久远的传统民居。吴氏祠始建于乾隆二十八年（1763），同治十年（1871）重建，光绪二十八年（1902）扩建，被誉为'鄂东第一祠'。这座规模宏大的祠堂坐北朝南，分为前后三进，总占地面积达到1200多平方米。祠堂中有戏楼、有拜殿、有寝殿，两侧有厢房，平面布局为两进四合院，经历了战火和'文化大革命'，保存非常完整。吴氏祠的入口为牌楼式，以青石为框架，红砂岩为格心，牌楼和木质门扇之间还有一个倾斜的角度，以使大门能够朝向正南。屋檐下施三层如意斗拱，斗拱下方又以彩画装饰，正立面显得宏伟而精致。正门背后是一个平面为'凸'字形的戏楼，名为'观乐楼'，分为前后台，后台与两侧的廊屋相连，前台向庭院中伸出，当心的屋面高起一些，形成重檐的视觉效果。戏台雕梁画栋，十分精彩，木雕多使用镂空雕刻，前檐两个翼角之下各有一只展翅欲飞的凤凰，凤凰身上每一根羽毛都清晰可见。台裙上的木雕则是一幅近9米长的'武汉三镇江景图'，以整段樟木雕琢而成，浮雕刻画大胆深入，层次感极强。画面上可以看到由长江、汉江分隔开的武汉三镇，城门、城楼、军营、商铺、码头、树木、船只等都历历在目，人物有学生、拜殿之后是存放祖先牌位的寝殿，后院的尺度较小，庭院中有一对石砌树坛，使得不大的院落中布满了树荫。后院的装饰相对朴素一些，但也很有特点：两侧厢房窗上书'渔、樵、耕、读'四字，都以龙凤随笔画盘旋而成，匠人的构思可谓精妙。而在前院戏台后台两侧的窗扇上，也可以看到类似的字形设计。根据文献记载，吴氏祠的最后一次修葺，主要归功于陡山村中在外做生意的吴氏兄弟，他们将数十年在外经营的所得，统统捐献给家乡作修建祠堂之用，请来的据说是当时最负盛名的肖家石匠班子和闻名两湖的'黄孝帮'木工班子。主人不惜重金，工匠也极尽所能，其砖、木、石雕在民间艺术中均属上乘之作。一幅武汉繁华的'江景图'出现在鄂东乡村，是在外漂泊经商的人们将外面的世界带回故乡；乡人则透过木雕来'目睹'武汉的繁华，想象外面的世界。除了个人的成就和家族的荣耀，也集中了那个时代的辛酸、苦难与希望。
projects.content_en: Doushan Village is located northeast of Baliwan Town, surrounded by mountains; the village still retains many traditional residences of great age. The Wu's Ancestral Hall was first built in the 28th year of Qianlong (1763), rebuilt in the 10th year of Tongzhi (1871), and expanded in the 28th year of Guangxu (1902), known as the 'No.1 Ancestral Hall of Eastern Hubei.' This grand-scale ancestral hall faces south, divided into three front-to-back sections, with a total area of over 1,200 square meters. The hall contains a stage, a worship hall, and a sleeping hall (for ancestral tablets), with wing rooms on both sides; the planar layout is two courtyards, having survived wars and the Cultural Revolution, very well preserved. The entrance of Wu's Ancestral Hall is a memorial-arch style, with bluestone as the frame and red sandstone as the lattice; there is also a tilted angle between the archway and the wooden door leaves, so that the main gate can face due south. Under the eaves are three layers of ruyi bracket sets, with painted decorations below the bracket sets, making the front facade grand and exquisite. Behind the main gate is a 'convex'-shaped stage called 'Guanyue Tower' (Music-Viewing Tower), divided into front and back stages; the back stage connects with the corridor rooms on both sides, and the front stage projects into the courtyard, with the central roof slightly raised, creating a double-eave visual effect. The stage is gorgeously decorated with carved beams and painted pillars, very splendid; the wood carvings mostly use openwork carving; under each of the two front eaves corners is a phoenix with wings spread ready to fly, with every feather on the phoenix clearly visible. The wood carving on the stage skirt is a nearly 9-meter-long 'Wuhan Three Towns River Scene,' carved from a whole section of camphor wood, with bold and deep relief carving and strong layering. On the画面, one can see the three towns of Wuhan separated by the Yangtze and Han rivers, with city gates, towers, military camps, shops, docks, trees, and boats all clearly visible; figures include students, ... Behind the worship hall is the sleeping hall for storing ancestral tablets; the backyard is smaller in scale, with a pair of stone tree altars in the courtyard, filling the small courtyard with tree shade. The decoration of the backyard is relatively plain but also distinctive: the windows of the side wing rooms are inscribed with the four characters 'fishing, woodcutting, plowing, reading,' all formed by dragons and phoenixes swirling in calligraphic strokes—the craftsman's构思 is truly ingenious. Similar character designs can also be seen on the window sashes on both sides of the stage backstage in the front courtyard. According to literature records, the last renovation of Wu's Ancestral Hall was mainly due to the Wu brothers of Doushan Village who did business away from home; they donated all their decades of earnings from business abroad to their hometown for building the ancestral hall, hiring what was said to be the most famous Xiao family stonemason team at the time and the renowned 'Huang-Xiao Gang' carpenter team of Hunan and Hubei. The owners spared no expense, and the craftsmen did their utmost; its brick, wood, and stone carvings are all top-grade in folk art. A 'River Scene' of prosperous Wuhan appearing in an eastern Hubei village is the result of people wandering and doing business away from home bringing the outside world back to their hometown; villagers then 'witness' Wuhan's prosperity through the wood carving, imagining the outside world. Beyond personal achievement and family glory, it also集中 the bitterness, suffering, and hope of that era.

projects.name: 双城塔
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 红安县七里坪镇柳林河村邹（周）家墩
projects.address_en: Zhoujiadun, Liulinhe Village, Qiliping Town, Hong'an County
projects.content_zh: 据《红安县志》记载，双城塔为元末农民起义领袖徐寿辉的部将邹普胜驻扎此地时所建。邹普胜是当地人，徐寿辉称帝后被封为太师，到明朝建立，隐姓埋名，自名为何野云，以给人相风水为生。塔建于元末，清同治十一年（1872）经过一次重要的重修，但基本保存了最初的形制。塔身六角十三层，仿木阁楼式，残高约35米，可以通过中心128步砖阶旋登塔顶。第一层东北面设拱券门，门内神龛曾供地藏王。第二层以上西向设佛龛，交错设拱形门及假窗，假窗有破子棂窗、菱形格子窗、蜂窝状窗等，每层各个不一。二层在塔身上隐刻勾栏而无平座，三四层有平座，五层以上既无勾栏，也无平座。各层腰檐、斗拱、平座均以特制砖件砌筑，斗拱每面5攒，形制古朴，制作精细；塔身整体苍秀秀丽柔和，虽为元塔，却很有宋代建筑的遗韵。双城塔是红安县十二景之一，又名大圣寺塔。据传此处原有一座香火旺盛的寺庙，庙中和尚养有猴之爱好，几经繁衍，猴儿经常盘绕于塔顶、各层檐壁和树枝上，因猴群让人联想到孙悟空，这座寺庙也就逐渐被称为大圣寺。
projects.content_en: According to the 'Hong'an County Annals,' Shuangcheng Pagoda was built when Zou Pusheng, a general under Xu Shouhui, leader of the late-Yuan peasant uprising, was stationed here. Zou Pusheng was a local; after Xu Shouhui declared himself emperor, Zou was enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor; when the Ming dynasty was established, he hid his identity, calling himself He Yeyun, making a living by feng shui divination. The pagoda was built at the end of the Yuan and underwent an important renovation in the 11th year of Tongzhi, Qing (1872), but basically preserved its original form. The pagoda body is hexagonal with thirteen stories, imitation-wood multi-eaved style, with a remaining height of about 35 meters; one can spiral-climb to the top via 128 brick steps in the center. On the northeast side of the first story is an arched door, and the shrine inside once enshrined Ksitigarbha. Above the second story, west-facing Buddhist niches are set, with arched doors and fake windows alternately; the fake windows include broken-lattice windows, diamond-grid windows, honeycomb windows, etc., varying from story to story. The second story has隐刻 railings on the pagoda body but no mezzanine; the third and fourth stories have mezzanines; above the fifth story there are neither railings nor mezzanines. The eaves, bracket sets, and mezzanines of each story are all built with specially made brick components; each face has 5 sets of bracket sets, with an ancient and simple form and fine workmanship. The overall pagoda body is elegant, graceful, and soft; although a Yuan pagoda, it strongly retains the charm of Song dynasty architecture. Shuangcheng Pagoda is one of the Twelve Scenes of Hong'an County, also known as Dasheng Temple Pagoda. Legend has it that there was originally a temple with thriving incense here; the monks in the temple had a hobby of raising monkeys, and after several generations of breeding, the monkeys often coiled around the pagoda top, eaves walls of various stories, and tree branches. Because the monkey group reminded people of Sun Wukong (the Monkey King), this temple gradually came to be called Dasheng (Great Sage) Temple.

projects.name: 抗日干部训练班旧址
projects.name_en: Historic Site of Anti-Japanese War Cadre Training Group
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 红安县七里坪镇盐店河村
projects.address_en: Yandianhe Village, Qiliping Town, Hong'an County
projects.content_zh: 原为秦氏祠，建于清道光年间，祠堂为三进五间，四合院式，硬山布瓦顶，砖木结构。每一进封火山墙的形状各不相同，形成丰富的轮廓。入口后退形成前廊，檐下有砖制斗拱装饰。曾为红二十八军抗日干部训练班旧址。
projects.content_en: Originally the Qin's Ancestral Hall, built during the Daoguang period of the Qing. The hall is three sections deep and five bays wide, in a courtyard layout, with a gable tile roof and brick-wood structure. The shape of the fire-sealing gable wall of each section is different, forming a rich silhouette. The entrance recedes to form a front porch, with brick bracket set decorations under the eaves. It was once the historic site of the Anti-Japanese War Cadre Training Group of the 28th Red Army.

projects.name: 桃花塔
projects.level: 县级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 红安县桃花乡桃花村东北
projects.address_en: Northeast of Taohua Village, Taohua Township, Hong'an County
projects.content_zh: 塔建于宋代，具体建造时间已不可考，是六角七层密檐式空心砖塔，残高近17米。塔基为条石砌成，塔身、塔顶为砖砌，层间叠涩出檐，檐下施砖雕斗拱。一、二层南面设圆拱形龛。每层六面正中嵌方形汉白玉匾，浮雕人物故事。塔南前约10米处原有桃花书院，毁于何时，亦已无从考证。塔下百余步的山洼里有桃花大寺，1930年被烧毁。
projects.content_en: The pagoda was built in the Song dynasty; the exact construction time can no longer be verified. It is a hexagonal seven-story dense-eave hollow brick pagoda, with a remaining height of nearly 17 meters. The pagoda base is built of dressed stone; the pagoda body and top are brick-built, with corbelled eaves between stories and brick-carved bracket sets under the eaves. On the south side of the first and second stories are round-arched niches. In the center of each of the six faces of each story is embedded a square white marble plaque with relief-carved figure stories. About 10 meters south of the pagoda there was originally Taohua Academy; when it was destroyed can no longer be verified. In the mountain hollow over a hundred steps below the pagoda was the Great Taohua Temple, burned down in 1930.

projects.name: 红安古桥
projects.level: 见各分点
projects.address: 见各分点
projects.address_en: See individual sites
projects.content_zh: 红安县境内河流众多，保存了明清以来的古桥四十余座，年代从明代中叶的嘉靖年间直到清末。其中比较重要的有永寿桥、高桥河桥。永寿桥是一座单孔石拱桥，长33米，宽6米，孔跨8米。位于上新集镇李氏畈村东北，建于明嘉靖元年（1522），东北至西南横跨在滠水中游的支流上。拱券为纵联砌置，桥面两侧设石望柱和栏板，由当地李氏家族兴建，现为湖北省文物保护单位。高桥河桥位于高桥河乡高桥河村，东北至西南向，横跨在倒水中游的支流上，原名高石桥，后逐渐称为高桥。桥建于清代乾隆年间，由当地吴氏捐资修建，此后屡有修复。桥长44.2米，宽5.35米，整体用石灰、糯米掺浆和条石砌筑而成。桥面呈八字形，中间窄，两端略宽，两侧设石望柱、栏板。桥墩平面呈六棱形，桥孔呈抛物线形，中孔高，东西两孔略低。桥孔的跨度也有所不同，中孔略大，而东西两孔略大。高桥河桥至今保存完好，仍然还发挥着交通作用，现为湖北省文物保护单位。其他古桥见下表：福德桥（明嘉靖十六年1537，七里坪镇福德桥村）、杨家山桥（明嘉靖年间，七里坪镇杨家山村下杨家山）、南门堰桥（明嘉靖年间，七里坪镇红坪村周家墩湾）、柳林河桥（明嘉靖年间，七里坪镇盐店河村柳林河湾）、河堰桥（明代天启年间，七里坪镇盐田河村罗庄）、罗堰畈桥（明代隆庆年间，七里坪镇盐田河村罗堰畈湾）、合心桥（明代嘉靖年间，檀树岗乡长冲村方家湾）、石堰嘴桥（明代隆庆年间，檀树岗乡余家畈村张家湾）、养明桥（明代万历年间，檀树岗乡熊家咀村十丈山）、涂家桥（明万历八年1580，觅儿寺镇尚古山村夏家岗）、黄石桥（明万历年间，觅儿寺镇尚古山村）、黄安桥（明万历四十三年1615，杏花乡李西村一村秦家墩湾）、姚八斗桥（明代崇祯年间，太平桥镇姚八斗村姚八斗湾）、栋津桥（始建于明崇祯年间，清光绪十四年1888重修，太平桥镇栋津村漂涂宏）。
projects.content_en: Hong'an County has numerous rivers, preserving over forty ancient bridges from the Ming and Qing dynasties, dating from the mid-Ming Jiajing period to the late Qing. Among the more important are Yongshou Bridge and Gaoqiaohe Bridge. Yongshou Bridge is a single-hole stone arch bridge, 33 meters long, 6 meters wide, with a span of 8 meters. Located northeast of Lishifan Village, Shangxinji Town, built in the 1st year of Jiajing, Ming (1522), spanning a tributary of the middle reaches of the She River from northeast to southwest. The arch券 is built in longitudinal connection; stone望柱 and railings are set on both sides of the bridge deck, built by the local Li family, now a Hubei Provincial Cultural Heritage Protection Unit. Gaoqiaohe Bridge is located in Gaoqiaohe Village, Gaoqiaohe Township, oriented northeast to southwest, spanning a tributary of the middle reaches of the Dao River; originally named Gaoshi Bridge, later gradually called Gaoqiao (High Bridge). The bridge was built during the Qianlong period of the Qing, funded by the local Wu family, and has been repeatedly repaired since. The bridge is 44.2 meters long and 5.35 meters wide,整体 built with lime, glutinous rice mortar, and dressed stone. The bridge deck is figure-eight shaped, narrow in the middle and slightly wider at both ends, with stone望柱 and railings on both sides. The bridge piers have a hexagonal plan; the bridge holes are parabolic, with the middle hole high and the east and west holes slightly lower. The spans of the bridge holes also differ, with the middle hole slightly larger and the east and west holes slightly larger. Gaoqiaohe Bridge is well preserved to this day and still serves a transportation function, now a Hubei Provincial Cultural Heritage Protection Unit. Other ancient bridges are listed in the table below: Fude Bridge (16th year of Jiajing, Ming 1537, Fudeqiao Village, Qiliping Town), Yangjiashan Bridge (Jiajing period, Ming, Lower Yangjiashan, Yangjiashan Village, Qiliping Town), Nanmen堰 Bridge (Jiajing period, Ming, Zhoujiadun Bay, Hongping Village, Qiliping Town), Liulinhe Bridge (Jiajing period, Ming, Liulinhe Bay, Yandianhe Village, Qiliping Town), Heyan Bridge (Tianqi period, Ming, Luozhuang, Yantianhe Village, Qiliping Town), Luoyanfan Bridge (Longqing period, Ming, Luoyanfan Bay, Yantianhe Village, Qiliping Town), Hexin Bridge (Jiajing period, Ming, Fangjiawan, Changchong Village, Tanshugang Township), Shiyanzui Bridge (Longqing period, Ming, Zhangjiawan, Yujiaban Village, Tanshugang Township), Yangming Bridge (Wanli period, Ming, Shizhang Mountain, Xiongjiazui Village, Tanshugang Township), Tujia Bridge (8th year of Wanli, Ming 1580, Xiajiagang, Shanggushan Village, Mi'ersi Town), Huangshi Bridge (Wanli period, Ming, Shanggushan Village, Mi'ersi Town), Huang'an Bridge (43rd year of Wanli, Ming 1615, Qinjiadun Bay, Yili Village, Xinghua Township), Yao Badou Bridge (Chongzhen period, Ming, Yao Badou Bay, Yao Badou Village, Taipingqiao Town), Dongjin Bridge (first built in Chongzhen period, Ming, rebuilt in 14th year of Guangxu, Qing 1888, Piaotuhong, Dongjin Village, Taipingqiao Town).

projects.name: 吴氏节孝祠
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 罗田县河铺镇古人墩村吴家塆
projects.address_en: Wujiawan, Gurenkun Village, Hepu Town, Luotian County
projects.content_zh: 据罗田《吴孝子宗谱》的记载，罗田吴氏的始祖吴季益为南宋遗民，南宋亡国后隐居于罗田独尊山，并归葬于此。吴氏长子大中在父墓侧建庐，为父守墓并侍奉母亲终老共十七年，其孝心远近闻名，乡里人皆颂，被元仁宗赐封'吴氏孝子'，建孝子牌坊并立碑纪念。大中八十二岁终，死后御葬独尊山下孝子里（今河铺镇古人墩），后世称'孝子坟'，大中后人也被称为'孝子坟吴氏'。吴氏节孝祠由石构的牌坊和祠堂共同组成。牌坊为四柱三间，宽5米，高6米，石上有龙凤浮雕。祠堂的正门也为四柱三间牌坊式，面阔三间，进深一间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，后壁嵌有石碑一块，上书'旌念孝殊之碑'。庄严古朴，保存现状较好。
projects.content_en: According to the 'Genealogy of the Wu Filial Son' of Luotian, the ancestor of the Luotian Wu family, Wu Jiyi, was a leftover subject of the Southern Song; after the fall of the Southern Song, he lived in seclusion at Duzun Mountain in Luotian and was buried here. Wu's eldest son Dazhong built a hut beside his father's tomb, guarding the tomb and serving his mother until her death for a total of seventeen years; his filial piety was known far and near, praised by all villagers, and was enfeoffed as 'Wu the Filial Son' by Emperor Renzong of Yuan, with a filial son memorial archway built and a stele erected to commemorate him. Dazhong died at the age of eighty-two, and was posthumously buried at Xiaozili (now Gurenkun, Hepu Town) below Duzun Mountain; later generations call it the 'Filial Son's Tomb,' and Dazhong's descendants are also called the 'Filial Son Tomb Wu family.' The Wu's Chastity and Piety Shrine consists of a stone memorial archway and a shrine. The archway has four columns and three bays, 5 meters wide and 6 meters high, with dragon and phoenix reliefs on the stone. The main gate of the shrine is also a four-column three-bay memorial-arch style, three bays wide and one bay deep, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof; a stone stele is embedded in the back wall, inscribed with 'Stele Commemorating Filial Piety.' Solemn and simple, in good preservation.

projects.name: 罗田胜利镇屯兵堡街及民居
projects.name_en: Tunbingpu Street and Vernacular Dwellings in Shengli Town, Luotian
projects.level: 县级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 罗田县胜利镇
projects.address_en: Shengli Town, Luotian County
projects.content_zh: 胜利镇是皖鄂边界、大别山南麓的一个小镇。据《罗田县志》记载，胜利镇原名屯兵铺，又称滕家堡，因明嘉靖二十二年（1543）间屯兵防寇设堡而得名。虽然地处偏僻而又兴于兵事，这座小镇却是大别山区重要的商旅要道和周边地区商品的集散地。位于镇中心的屯兵堡街始建于宋代，以青石铺成，沿街二百多户民居均为二层砖木混合结构，青砖黑瓦，多为前店、中厨、后宅，今天还保存着较好的明清街巷风貌。古街上最富盛名的建筑当属金凤楼。它坐东面西，始建于明嘉靖年间，相传是一位安徽富豪的女儿远嫁至此，捐献陪嫁的一对大金凤建起了此楼。清代咸丰年间因战事被毁，同治十二年（1873）重建，一进四重，中有天井，颇为壮观。1926年夏季，共产党员李梯云、肖方等受中共湖北省委指派，在金凤楼开办平民小学，成立'滕家堡青年协进会'，并秘密成立了罗田第一个共产党组织——中共罗田支部。1947年刘邓大军第六纵队进入滕家堡，司令部也设在金凤楼。
projects.content_en: Shengli Town is a small town on the Anhui-Hubei border, at the southern foot of the Dabie Mountains. According to the 'Luotian County Annals,' Shengli Town was originally called Tunbingpu (Troop Station), also known as Tengjiabao, named because troops were stationed and a fort built here to defend against bandits in the 22nd year of Jiajing, Ming (1543). Although located in a remote area and arising from military affairs, this small town was an important commercial travel route and commodity distribution center for the surrounding area in the Dabie Mountain region. Tunbingpu Street in the town center was first built in the Song dynasty, paved with bluestone; over 200 households along the street are all two-story brick-wood composite structures, with gray brick and black tile, mostly front-shop, middle-kitchen, back-residence types, and today still preserves a good Ming-Qing streetscape. The most famous building on the old street is the Jinfeng (Golden Phoenix) Tower. Facing west, it was first built during the Jiajing period of the Ming; legend has it that the daughter of an Anhui wealthy merchant married far away here and donated a pair of large golden phoenixes from her dowry to build this tower. It was destroyed by war during the Xianfeng period of the Qing and rebuilt in the 12th year of Tongzhi (1873), with four sections and a central courtyard, quite spectacular. In summer 1926, Communist Party members Li Tiyun, Xiao Fang, and others, assigned by the Hubei Provincial Committee of the CPC, opened a civilian primary school at Jinfeng Tower, established the 'Tengjiabao Youth Progressive Association,' and secretly established Luotian's first Communist Party organization—the Luotian Branch of the CPC. In 1947, the Sixth Column of the Liu-Deng Army entered Tengjiabao, and its headquarters was also set up at Jinfeng Tower.

projects.name: 新屋垸民居
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 罗田县九资河镇官基坪村三省垴山下
projects.address_en: Below Sanshengnao Mountain, Guanjiping Village, Jiuzhihe Town, Luotian County
projects.content_zh: 明朝末年，江西人罗有琦随大移民从南昌迁居到罗田。据《罗氏宗谱》记载，罗有琦刚来时一贫如洗，茅棚栖身，被本地人称为'客户'；后来勤俭持家，进而致富。明万历二十六年（1598），他招募鄂、豫、皖三省匠人，历时5年，为三个儿子在三省垴山脚下盖起了气势恢宏的大房子，鹤立于众多茅舍之中，当地人称'新屋垸'（'垸'是湖南湖北一带对挡水堤的称呼，也指堤所围住的地区），名称延续至今。四周曾遍种紫薇，又名紫薇山庄。新屋垸坐东北朝西南，依山傍水而建，南北长168米，东西宽48米，具有一些客家围龙屋建筑的特点。比注重风水朝向和山形水势的处理，负阴抱阳、避风纳气，山围水、水围垸、垸围院、院围屋。大院的门楼是新屋垸的装饰重点，门楼突起，门洞上方为条石过梁，梁上雕刻花卉、如意等吉祥纹样，檐下亦彩绘鸟兽图案。门楼内侧是戏台，院内正面及左右两侧各有大门，三个门各有一个生活组团，均有下堂屋、中堂屋、上堂屋，且都有精致的雕花装饰。各堂屋两侧布置房屋共99间，取'久'的谐音，象征富贵长久，寓意永远进取。新屋垸里共有32口天井，全部用花岗石砌成。每个组团和组团之间，各个部分均有走廊相连，既独立又相通。院内生活自成一统，只要不出院门就可以不带雨伞。在主体建筑左侧，还建有接官亭、舞凤楼、贡马楼，此外周边还有古松遮日、枫林护夏、紫薇高照、丹桂盈香、晨钟暮鼓、又水回澜等多处景观。
projects.content_en: At the end of the Ming dynasty, Jiangxi native Luo Youqi moved from Nanchang to Luotian during the great migration. According to the 'Luo Family Genealogy,' when Luo Youqi first arrived he was penniless, living in a thatched hut, called a 'guest household' by locals; later he was thrifty and hardworking, becoming wealthy. In the 26th year of Wanli, Ming (1598), he recruited craftsmen from Hubei, Henan, and Anhui provinces, and over 5 years built grand houses for his three sons at the foot of Sanshengnao Mountain, standing out among the many thatched huts; locals called it 'Xinwuyuan' ('yuan' is a term in Hunan and Hubei for a water-retaining embankment, also referring to the area enclosed by the embankment), a name延续 to this day. Crape myrtle was once planted all around, also known as Crape Myrtle Villa. Xinwuyuan faces southwest from the northeast, built against the mountain and by the water, 168 meters long north-south and 48 meters wide east-west, with some characteristics of Hakka enclosed dragon houses. It emphasizes feng shui orientation and the handling of mountain and water forms, embracing yin and holding yang, sheltering from wind and gathering qi, with mountains enclosing water, water enclosing the yuan, the yuan enclosing courtyards, and courtyards enclosing houses. The gate tower of the great courtyard is the decorative focus of Xinwuyuan; the gate tower projects, with a dressed-stone lintel above the doorway carved with auspicious patterns such as flowers and ruyi, and the eaves are also painted with bird and beast patterns. Inside the gate tower is a stage; on the front and left and right sides of the courtyard are each main gates, with three gates each having a living group, all with lower, middle, and upper halls, all with exquisite carved decorations. On both sides of each hall are arranged a total of 99 rooms, taking the homophone of 'long-lasting,' symbolizing lasting wealth and meaning eternal progress. Xinwuyuan has a total of 32 courtyards (tianjing), all built of granite. Between each group and each part, there are corridors connecting them, both independent and interconnected. Life inside the courtyard is self-contained; one need not bring an umbrella as long as one does not leave the courtyard gate. On the left side of the main building, there are also the Official-Receiving Pavilion, Dancing Phoenix Tower, and Tribute Horse Tower; in addition, the surroundings have many scenic spots such as ancient pines shading the sun, maple forests protecting from summer, crape myrtle shining high, osmanthus fragrance filling the air, morning bells and evening drums, and returning water ripples.

projects.name: 段氏宅
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 英山县南河镇灵芝村南400米
projects.address_en: 400 meters south of Lingzhi Village, Nanhe Town, Yingshan County
projects.content_zh: 段氏宅为清光绪年间候补知县段昭昀的府第和庄园，始建于光绪二十四年（1898），光绪二十八年（1902）由段润霖续建，又称为兴贤庄。《英山县志·附录补遗》中记载：'段昭昀，湖北候补知县。乐施好善，慷慨任事，捐田课三十担零二斗，筹建本姓兴贤庄；捐田课二担三角斗，以为高祖祁成公祀之。丙申岁饥，捐资赈恤。县主陆祥清赠以'惠济桑梓'匾额。'这位候补官爷对宗族产业的发展和饥荒之赈恤也是功不可没的。段氏宅是一处规模庞大的宅邸，坐北朝南，通面阔九间，有三路两进院落，中轴对称，建筑的占地面积将近1700平方米，如此之规模甚至超过了一些中小型的祠堂，不仅显示了雄厚的财力，与段氏候补知县的身份也不无关系。建筑本身为砖木混合结构，中路有门厅、前堂、后堂等建筑，建筑之间多以窄小的天井相隔。所有柱础都采用汉白玉石，西路第一进还保留着较为精美的室内装修，其他房间的木装修则所剩无几。两侧的院落为纵向建筑，前后各有封火山墙，每一进房屋的山墙又比院墙高出一些，从墙外看去，形成了一种优美的韵律感。外墙四周的檐下以凸出的砖饰来模仿斗拱，在斗拱以下又以彩画作为装饰。根据地方文献记载，南宋绍兴十八年（1148）金人南侵，江西饶州一支段姓族人北迁至安庆，再迁至蕲春，最后在山水环绕的英山土地肥沃的英山瓦寺前村定居，置田产、建屋基，在此创业，后来成为英山一脉名门。南宋咸淳六年（1270）英山县从蕲水县分出，首任英山知县即为段氏族人段朝立，现在南河镇上村东北，还留存有段朝立之墓。1931年，苏维埃英山县红四区政府在段氏宅成立，当时的红山县包括现在的罗田、英山、蕲春等九个县；1932年又成立了红山县苏维埃政府保卫局。1932年—1947年，红四军、红十五军、红二十五军、红二十七军，以及刘（伯承）邓（小平）大军挺进大别山时，多次在段氏府宿营并成立临时的战斗指挥部，段氏宅一度成为大别山区的红色舞台。新中国成立后曾改建为寄宿式的小学，师生的生活和学习全部在这座宽敞的老屋之中。它今天仍是南河镇原麻元小学的一部分，门前还有一大片麻元小学的蔬菜基地。
projects.content_en: Duan's Mansion was the residence and manor of Duan Zhaoyun, a candidate county magistrate during the Guangxu period of the Qing. First built in the 24th year of Guangxu (1898), continued by Duan Runlin in the 28th year of Guangxu (1902), also called Xingxian Manor. The 'Yingshan County Annals·Appendix Supplement' records: 'Duan Zhaoyun, Hubei candidate county magistrate. Generous and charitable,慷慨 in taking responsibility; donated 30 dan and 2 dou of farmland rent to build the Xingxian Manor for his surname; donated 2 dan and 3 jiao dou of farmland rent for the sacrifice of his great-great-grandfather Qicheng Gong. In the Bing申 year famine, he donated funds for relief. County magistrate Lu Xiangqing presented him with a plaque 'Benefiting the Hometown.'' This candidate official also made undeniable contributions to the development of clan property and famine relief. Duan's Mansion is a large-scale residence facing south, with a total width of nine bays, three routes and two courtyards, with central axis symmetry; the building covers nearly 1,700 square meters, a scale even exceeding some small and medium-sized ancestral halls, not only showing strong financial resources but also related to Duan's status as a candidate county magistrate. The building itself is a brick-wood composite structure; the central route has an entrance hall, front hall, rear hall, and other buildings, mostly separated by narrow courtyards (tianjing). All column bases use white marble; the first section of the west route still retains relatively exquisite interior decoration, while the wood decoration of other rooms is almost gone. The courtyards on both sides are longitudinal buildings, with fire-sealing gable walls at the front and back; the gable wall of each section's house is higher than the courtyard wall, creating a beautiful sense of rhythm when viewed from outside the wall. Under the eaves around the exterior walls, protruding brick decorations imitate bracket sets, with painted decorations below the bracket sets. According to local literature records, in the 18th year of Shaoxing, Southern Song (1148), when the Jin people invaded south, a branch of the Duan family from Raozhou, Jiangxi, migrated north to Anqing, then to Qichun, and finally settled in Wasiqian Village, Yingshan, with fertile land surrounded by mountains and water, purchasing farmland, building house foundations, and starting a business here, later becoming a prominent family in Yingshan. In the 6th year of Xianchun, Southern Song (1270), Yingshan County was separated from Qishui County, and the first county magistrate of Yingshan was Duan clan member Duan Chaoli; today, northeast of Shangcun, Nanhe Town, the tomb of Duan Chaoli still remains. In 1931, the Soviet Hongsi District Government of Yingshan County was established at Duan's Mansion; at that time, Hongshan County included nine counties such as present-day Luotian, Yingshan, and Qichun; in 1932, the Hongshan County Soviet Government Security Bureau was also established. From 1932 to 1947, the Fourth Red Army, Fifteenth Red Army, Twenty-fifth Red Army, Twenty-seventh Red Army, as well as when the Liu (Bocheng)-Deng (Xiaoping) Army marched into the Dabie Mountains, repeatedly camped at Duan's Mansion and established temporary battle command posts; Duan's Mansion once became a red stage in the Dabie Mountain region. After the founding of New China, it was converted into a boarding primary school, with teachers and students living and studying entirely in this spacious old house. Today it is still part of the former Mayuan Primary School in Nanhe Town, with a large vegetable base of Mayuan Primary School in front of the door.

projects.name: 李公桥
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 英山县杨柳湾镇杨树堰村
projects.address_en: Yangshuyan Village, Yangliwan Town, Yingshan County
projects.content_zh: 又名花桥，是一座单孔石拱桥，长16米，宽约4米。两侧桥头以砖木修建廊屋，以如意山墙封头；跨河的部分则为纯木结构，在栏杆处加设披檐，桥身显得空灵轻巧，与两侧厚重的砖墙形成对比，使整座桥的造型丰富起来。李公桥的始建年代已无处考证，县志记载清光绪八年（1882）曾遭洪水冲毁，第二年重修。廊桥梁上的记载称1917年石匠周大发、木匠吴道成和砌匠徐自发等人重修。离这座桥不远，可以看到新修的武英高速大桥，新旧桥交相辉映，福泽世代百姓。
projects.content_en: Also called Flower Bridge, it is a single-hole stone arch bridge, 16 meters long and about 4 meters wide. On both bridgeheads, corridor houses are built with brick and wood, capped with ruyi gable walls; the part spanning the river is pure wood structure, with additional eaves at the railings, making the bridge body appear light and airy, contrasting with the heavy brick walls on both sides and enriching the shape of the entire bridge. The original construction date of Ligong Bridge can no longer be verified; county annals record that it was destroyed by a flood in the 8th year of Guangxu, Qing (1882) and rebuilt the following year. Records on the corridor beams state that it was rebuilt in 1917 by stonemason Zhou Dafa, carpenter Wu Daocheng, and bricklayer Xu Zifa. Not far from this bridge, one can see the newly built Wuying Expressway Bridge; the old and new bridges enhance each other, blessing generations of people.

projects.name: 安家大屋
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
