projects.content_zh: 蒋家花园又名蒋家院民居，位于咸丰县甲马池镇新场村的新场村，今新场中学的校园里面。东距咸丰县城50公里，西距黔江城44公里，北面有太子山、鸡窝山。据记载，蒋家花园建于19世纪初，是由当地的富豪蒋克勤建造的。传说蒋家花园的建造缘于蒋克勤的母亲李氏款待了一位落魄的风水先生，先生为表达感激之情，向蒋母吐露了天机，由此蒋克勤开始架梁起屋，不吝所有的建造蒋家花园，蒋氏一族便由此发达。蒋克勤50多岁时被土匪杀死，蒋家花园渐渐衰败。蒋家花园是四合院与吊脚楼的完美结合，坐东北朝西南，全木结构，五天井抱中央四合院形制，三路单进四合院布局，有门厅、正屋、以及左右偏房。正中为进园大门，左右各有3间正屋，1间转角屋，东侧有一吊脚楼厢房向院坝伸出。单檐硬山灰瓦顶，抬
projects.content_en: Jiang's Mansion, also called Jiang Family Courtyard Residence, is located in Xinchang Village, Jiamachi Town, Xianfeng County, inside the campus of today's Xinchang Middle School. It is 50 kilometers east of Xianfeng County seat, 44 kilometers west of Qianjiang City, with Taizi Mountain and Jiwo Mountain to the north. According to records, Jiang's Mansion was built in the early 19th century by the local wealthy man Jiang Keqin. Legend has it that the construction of Jiang's Mansion originated from Jiang Keqin's mother, Li Shi, entertaining a down-and-out fengshui master; to express gratitude, the master revealed the secrets of heaven to Jiang's mother, and from then on Jiang Keqin began to set up beams and build houses, sparing no expense to build Jiang's Mansion, and the Jiang clan prospered from then on. Jiang Keqin was killed by bandits in his 50s, and Jiang's Mansion gradually declined. Jiang's Mansion is a perfect combination of a four-sided courtyard and a stilted building, facing southwest from northeast, of all-wooden structure, with a form of five courtyards embracing the central four-sided courtyard, and a layout of three routes of single-entry four-sided courtyards, with an entrance hall, main house, and left and right wing rooms. In the center is the entrance gate to the garden, with 3 main rooms and 1 corner room on each side; on the east side, there is a stilted wing room extending toward the courtyard. It has a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, with post-and-lintel

projects.name: 黄龙古建筑群
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 犟河入堵河口东北岸，黄龙镇
projects.address_en: Northeast bank of Jiang River estuary into Du River, Huanglong Town
projects.type: 商业与手工业建筑·砖石结构
projects.type_en: Commercial and Handicraft Building · Brick-Stone Structure
highlights: 黄龙镇始建于明末清初
坐落在汉江支流堵河下游与犟河交汇之处
逐渐成为堵河下游和鄂西北最大的港口集镇和交通枢纽
并在此后多次改建街道
全镇有前街、后街、上街、河街4条主要的街道
前街、后街与上街呈Y字形相交
又相继建成了武昌会馆、江西会馆、山陕会馆等
还有一座西方传教士修建的天主教堂
目前保存状况较好的有武昌会馆、黄州会馆
江西会馆仅余完整山墙
而山陕会馆则已难觅其踪
黄龙镇余氏家族对古镇的兴盛发展作出了重要的贡献
族中余隆庭、余正裔二人分别官至四川松潘知府和兵部侍郎的高位
镇上的64号民居即为余氏故宅
并且很有可能是当年的余氏宗祠
projects.content_zh: 黄龙镇始建于明末清初，坐落在汉江支流堵河下游与犟河交汇之处，随着商业的发展，逐渐成为堵河下游和鄂西北最大的港口集镇和交通枢纽，曾被人们誉为'小汉口'。清咸丰元年（1851），黄龙正式设镇，并在此后多次改建街道。全镇有前街、后街、上街、河街4条主要的街道，前街、后街与上街呈'Y'字形相交，交汇处是古镇的中心。咸丰七年（1857），黄州会馆落成后，又相继建成了武昌会馆、江西会馆、山陕会馆等，还有一座西方传教士修建的天主教堂。目前保存状况较好的有武昌会馆、黄州会馆，江西会馆仅余完整山墙，内部已是废墟，而山陕会馆则已难觅其踪。此外，黄龙镇余氏家族对古镇的兴盛发展作出了重要的贡献，族中余隆庭、余正裔二人分别官至四川松潘知府和兵部侍郎的高位，镇上的64号民居即为余氏故宅，并且很有可能是当年的余氏宗祠。
projects.content_en: Huanglong Town was first built in the late Ming and early Qing, located at the confluence of the lower Du River, a tributary of the Han River, and the Jiang River. With the development of commerce, it gradually became the largest port town and transportation hub in the lower Du River and northwestern Hubei, and was once hailed as 'Little Hankou.' In the 1st year of Xianfeng, Qing (1851), Huanglong was officially established as a town, and the streets were rebuilt many times thereafter. The whole town has 4 main streets: Front Street, Back Street, Upper Street, and River Street; Front Street, Back Street, and Upper Street intersect in a 'Y' shape, with the intersection being the center of the ancient town. In the 7th year of Xianfeng (1857), after the Huangzhou Guild Hall was completed, the Wuchang Guild Hall, Jiangxi Guild Hall, Shaanxi-Shanxi Guild Hall, etc. were successively built, and there was also a Catholic church built by Western missionaries. Currently, the Wuchang Guild Hall and Huangzhou Guild Hall are in relatively good preservation; the Jiangxi Guild Hall only has complete gable walls remaining, with the interior already in ruins, while the Shaanxi-Shanxi Guild Hall is hard to trace. In addition, the Yu family of Huanglong Town made important contributions to the prosperity and development of the ancient town; among the clan, Yu Longting and Yu Zhengyi respectively rose to the high positions of Songpan Prefect of Sichuan and Vice Minister of War; Residence No. 64 in the town is the former residence of the Yu family, and is very likely the former Yu Family Ancestral Hall.

projects.name: 武昌会馆
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 黄龙镇老街
projects.address_en: Old Street, Huanglong Town
highlights: 武昌会馆是黄龙镇会馆中规模最大且最有特色的一座
始建于清嘉庆二十四年
中轴线上有山门、戏楼、前殿、拜殿和正殿等建筑
现在戏楼和前殿的位置新建了6层的住宅楼
切断了山门与后面部分的联系
已经无法领略建筑原先的规模和气势了
武昌会馆的山门特别讲究
在街道上一眼可以看到明间两侧高耸的云形四级封火山墙
明间正面也采用云线轮廓以形成呼应
次间、尽间则为重檐灰瓦顶
已经较明显地改变了原貌
两种山墙都富有很强的韵律感
山门与拜殿之间的距离较远
可以想象当年戏楼和前殿的规模应该是比较宏大的
从西侧绕过新建的住宅楼
两侧以偏房与拜殿相连
院落结构更接近于北方四合院
正殿、拜殿均没有太多装饰
与山门相比显得简朴、粗犷
只有外墙的砖上写有古凸起鄂邑
因为这一处武昌会馆便成为沟通武汉与郧阳商业活动的重要媒介
projects.content_zh: 武昌会馆是黄龙镇会馆中规模最大且最有特色的一座，始建于清嘉庆二十四年（1819），坐北朝南，有三进院落，占地面积约1700平方米，中轴线上有山门、戏楼、前殿、拜殿和正殿等建筑，现在戏楼和前殿的位置新建了6层的住宅楼，切断了山门与后面部分的联系，已经无法领略建筑原先的规模和气势了。武昌会馆的山门特别讲究，面阔五间，进深三间，穿斗式结构，在街道上一眼可以看到明间两侧高耸的云形四级封火山墙，明间正面也采用云线轮廓以形成呼应，单檐灰瓦顶，次间、尽间则为重檐灰瓦顶，四段跌落马头山墙，右半边因有人居住，已经较明显地改变了原貌。中部云墙的曲线流畅，两端马头墙干净利落，两种山墙都富有很强的韵律感。山门与拜殿之间的距离较远，大约50米，可以想象当年戏楼和前殿的规模应该是比较宏大的。从西侧绕过新建的住宅楼，可以看到拜殿和正殿，拜殿面阔五间，进深三间，穿斗式结构，单檐硬山屋顶，中间为穿堂，两端设砖墙；后面的正殿面阔三间，抬梁式结构，也是单檐硬山，左右各有一个垛殿，两侧以偏房与拜殿相连，院落结构更接近于北方四合院，山墙为马头墙。正殿、拜殿均没有太多装饰，与山门相比显得简朴、粗犷，只有外墙的砖上写有古凸起'鄂邑'（一说为'鄂郡'）二字。明清时期的郧阳府，因为这一处武昌会馆便成为沟通武汉与郧阳商业活动的重要媒介。
projects.content_en: Wuchang Guild Hall is the largest and most distinctive one among the guild halls in Huanglong Town. It was first built in the 24th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1819), facing south, with three courtyards, covering an area of about 1,700 square meters; on the central axis there are buildings such as the mountain gate, opera tower, front hall, worship hall, and main hall. Now, at the location of the opera tower and front hall, a 6-story residential building has been newly built, cutting off the connection between the mountain gate and the rear part, so it is no longer possible to appreciate the original scale and momentum of the building. The mountain gate of Wuchang Guild Hall is particularly elaborate, five bays wide and three bays deep, of column-and-tie structure; from the street, one can at a glance see the towering cloud-shaped four-level fire-sealing gable walls on both sides of the central bay; the front of the central bay also adopts a cloud-line outline to form a response, with a single-eave gray-tile roof, while the secondary and end bays have double-eave gray-tile roofs, with four sections of stepped horse-head gable walls; the right half, because someone lives there, has relatively obviously changed from its original appearance. The curve of the central cloud wall is smooth, and the horse-head gable walls at both ends are clean and neat; both types of gable walls are full of strong rhythmic sense. The distance between the mountain gate and the worship hall is relatively far, about 50 meters; one can imagine that the scale of the opera tower and front hall in those days should have been relatively grand. Bypassing the newly built residential building from the west, one can see the worship hall and main hall; the worship hall is five bays wide and three bays deep, of column-and-tie structure, with a single-eave gable roof, with a passage in the middle and brick walls at both ends; the main hall behind is three bays wide, of post-and-lintel structure, also with a single-eave gable roof, with a side hall on each side, connected to the worship hall by wing rooms on both sides; the courtyard structure is closer to a northern courtyard house, with horse-head gable walls. Both the main hall and worship hall do not have much decoration, appearing simple and rough compared to the mountain gate; only on the bricks of the exterior wall are written the ancient raised characters 'E Yi' (some say 'E Jun'). In the Yunyang Prefecture of the Ming and Qing periods, this Wuchang Guild Hall became an important medium for communicating commercial activities between Wuhan and Yunyang.

projects.name: 黄州会馆
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 黄龙镇老街
projects.address_en: Old Street, Huanglong Town
highlights: 黄州会馆紧挨着武昌会馆的西侧
轴线与武昌会馆平行而规模稍小
会馆现仅存正殿一组院落
正中入口有砖木结构的门罩
院落中是一个小小的天井
第二进的正殿面阔五间
前檐做成较为精美的卷棚顶装饰
建筑的原有构件选料和工艺都较为考究
外墙的多处砖面上有突起的黄州二字
说明当时的会馆建筑十分重视使用专门的材料
projects.content_zh: 黄州会馆紧挨着武昌会馆的西侧，建于咸丰七年（1857），坐北朝南，轴线与武昌会馆平行而规模稍小。由于年久失修，会馆现仅存正殿一组院落，基本保持了原貌。前厅面阔三间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，正中入口有砖木结构的门罩，稍稍高于屋面，现以强调入口。院落中是一个小小的天井，约5米见方，现已被填平。第二进的正殿面阔五间，进深三间，前檐做成较为精美的卷棚顶装饰，明间的空间高耸，两侧设有夹层，用材粗糙，像是后期改建而成的。建筑的原有构件选料和工艺都较为考究，外墙的多处砖面上有突起的'黄州'二字，说明当时的会馆建筑十分重视使用专门的材料。
projects.content_en: Huangzhou Guild Hall is immediately adjacent to the west side of Wuchang Guild Hall, built in the 7th year of Xianfeng (1857), facing south, with its axis parallel to Wuchang Guild Hall but slightly smaller in scale. Due to long-term neglect and disrepair, the guild hall now only retains one group of courtyards of the main hall, basically maintaining its original appearance. The front hall is three bays wide, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof; at the central entrance there is a brick-wood structure door canopy, slightly higher than the roof surface, now to emphasize the entrance. In the courtyard is a small courtyard (tianjing), about 5 meters square, which has now been filled in. The main hall of the second entry is five bays wide and three bays deep; the front eave is made into a relatively exquisite curved-roof decoration; the space of the central bay is tall, with mezzanines on both sides, using rough materials, as if rebuilt in a later period. The original components of the building were relatively carefully selected in materials and craftsmanship; on multiple brick surfaces of the exterior wall, there are protruding characters 'Huangzhou,' indicating that the guild hall buildings at that time attached great importance to using specialized materials.

projects.name: 江西会馆
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 黄龙镇老街
projects.address_en: Old Street, Huanglong Town
highlights: 江西会馆位于黄龙镇西头
会馆保存较好的只有最外围的山墙
后部正殿现有村民居住
但仍可看出原会馆两进院落的结构
正殿为单檐硬山灰瓦顶
整体规模远小于武昌会馆
外墙上也多用有凸起江西字样的灰砖
当年沿堵河而来的商贾登岸后
首先看到的就是江西会馆
因此会馆前很可能有较为开敞的空间
projects.content_zh: 江西会馆位于黄龙镇西头，坐东朝西，面向堵河。会馆保存较好的只有最外围的山墙，前堂已不存，中部主体建筑已坍塌，后部正殿现有村民居住，也遭到了较大的改动，但仍可看出原会馆两进院落的结构。正殿为单檐硬山灰瓦顶，封火山墙，整体规模远小于武昌会馆，外墙上也多用有凸起'江西'字样的灰砖。可以推测，当年沿堵河而来的商贾登岸后，首先看到的就是江西会馆，因此会馆前很可能有较为开敞的空间。
projects.content_en: Jiangxi Guild Hall is located at the west end of Huanglong Town, facing west from east, facing the Du River. Only the outermost gable walls of the guild hall are relatively well-preserved; the front hall no longer exists, the central main building has collapsed, and the rear main hall is now inhabited by villagers, having also undergone major alterations, but the structure of the original two-entry courtyard of the guild hall can still be seen. The main hall has a single-eave gable gray-tile roof and fire-sealing gable walls, with an overall scale much smaller than Wuchang Guild Hall; the exterior walls also mostly use gray bricks with protruding characters 'Jiangxi.' It can be inferred that when merchants arriving along the Du River disembarked in those days, the first thing they saw was Jiangxi Guild Hall, so there was likely a relatively open space in front of the guild hall.

projects.name: 回龙寺
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当街办处西坪村
projects.address_en: Xiping Village, Wudang Subdistrict Office
highlights: 回龙寺始建于明弘治年间
寺院建在形似盘龙卧伏的山包上
寺旁有两口清澈见底的水井
马家河从寺前迂回流过
有山门、前殿、正殿和左右厢房
正面有前廊和木隔扇门窗
殿前场地上散落存放一些建筑构件和回龙寺清然和尚塔记碑
寺中仅有一位释仁慈师傅住持打理日常事务
年轻人又多皈依基督教
使得寺院的保护一直不能得到足够的重视
整个建筑的保存状况令人担忧
projects.content_zh: 回龙寺始建于明弘治年间，清乾隆年间重修。寺院建在形似盘龙卧伏的山包上，寺旁有两口清澈见底的水井，被称为'龙眼'，马家河从寺前迂回流过，似蛟龙回游，故名为回龙寺。寺院原有两进院落，有山门、前殿、正殿和左右厢房，建筑面积约1000平方米，现仅存正殿，面阔七间，进深三间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，混合式木结构。殿高二层，正面有前廊和木隔扇门窗，殿前场地上散落存放一些建筑构件和'回龙寺清然和尚塔记'碑。寺中仅有一位释仁慈师傅住持打理日常事务，而本地由于道教盛行，年轻人又多皈依基督教，使得寺院的保护一直不能得到足够的重视，整个建筑的保存状况令人担忧。
projects.content_en: Huilong (Returning Dragon) Temple was first built during the Hongzhi period of the Ming and rebuilt during the Qianlong period of the Qing. The temple is built on a hill shaped like a coiling dragon lying down; beside the temple there are two crystal-clear wells, called 'Dragon Eyes'; the Majia River flows circuitously in front of the temple, like a dragon swimming back, hence the name Huilong Temple. The temple originally had two courtyards, with a mountain gate, front hall, main hall, and left and right wing rooms, with a building area of about 1,000 square meters; now only the main hall remains, seven bays wide and three bays deep, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof and a mixed wooden structure. The hall is two stories high, with a front porch and wooden lattice doors and windows on the front; on the ground in front of the hall, some building components and the 'Huilong Temple Qingran Monk Pagoda Record' stele are scattered and stored. In the temple, only one Master Shi Renci abides to manage daily affairs; because Taoism prevails locally and young people mostly convert to Christianity, the protection of the temple has never received sufficient attention, and the preservation condition of the entire building is worrying.

projects.name: 大丰仓
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 郧阳区汉江二桥北，209国道东侧
projects.address_en: North of Hanjiang Second Bridge, east of National Highway 209, Yunyang District
highlights: 郧阳大丰仓的前身可以追溯到汉代设立的常平仓
丰年收购粮食以免谷贱伤农
歉年卖出以平抑物价的一种仓储制度
现有建筑始建于明成化十三年
改建于县城小西门内的高岗上
县守军将大丰仓梁柱拆下
清光绪七年秋在原址上重建
中华民国时期由于税收政策的改变
大丰仓被确定为国有粮仓
并在20世纪50年代初重新修缮
一度恢复了往昔的气势与功能
似乎在沉默中诉说着古老的故事
清光绪九年的新建大丰仓碑开篇说到
简单而亘古不变的道理
projects.content_zh: 郧阳大丰仓的前身可以追溯到汉代设立的'常平仓'，即由国家设立，丰年收购粮食以免谷贱伤农，歉年卖出以平抑物价的一种仓储制度。现有建筑始建于明成化十三年（1477），明万历四十一年（1613），大水入城，仓储被淹没，改建于县城小西门内的高岗上。清同治元年，为抵抗太平天国军，县守军将大丰仓梁柱拆下，堆码在城墙上，用作滚木以抵抗来犯，大丰仓因而废毁。清光绪七年（1881）秋在原址上重建，占地面积53亩。中华民国时期由于税收政策的改变，以征银取代征粮，大丰仓长年闲置；新中国成立后，大丰仓被确定为国有粮仓，并在20世纪50年代初重新修缮，新建砖木结构仓库5栋，一度恢复了往昔的气势与功能。大丰仓近看结构考究，远看气势恢弘，似乎在沉默中诉说着古老的故事。清光绪九年的'新建大丰仓'碑开篇说到：'为政之要莫过于保民，保民之要莫先于足食。'简单而亘古不变的道理，正如朴素的建筑，庄严而厚重，让人心生感动。
projects.content_en: The predecessor of Yunyang Dafeng Granary can be traced back to the 'Ever-Normal Granary' established in the Han Dynasty, a storage system established by the state to purchase grain in bumper years to avoid low grain prices harming farmers, and to sell grain in lean years to stabilize prices. The existing building was first built in the 13th year of Chenghua, Ming (1477); in the 41st year of Wanli, Ming (1613), a flood entered the city and the granary was submerged, so it was rebuilt on a high ridge inside the Small West Gate of the county seat. In the 1st year of Tongzhi, Qing, to resist the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom army, the county garrison dismantled the beams and columns of Dafeng Granary and stacked them on the city wall to use as rolling logs to resist the invaders, hence Dafeng Granary was destroyed. In the autumn of the 7th year of Guangxu, Qing (1881), it was rebuilt on the original site, covering an area of 53 mu. During the Republic of China period, due to changes in tax policy, silver tax replaced grain tax, and Dafeng Granary was idle for many years; after the founding of New China, Dafeng Granary was designated as a state-owned granary, and was re-renovated in the early 1950s, with 5 new brick-wood structure warehouses built, once restoring its former momentum and function. Dafeng Granary has an exquisite structure up close and a grand momentum from afar, as if telling ancient stories in silence. The preface of the 'Newly Built Dafeng Granary' stele of the 9th year of Guangxu, Qing says: 'The essence of governance is nothing more than protecting the people; the essence of protecting the people is nothing prior to having sufficient food.' A simple and eternally unchanged truth, just like the simple building, solemn and厚重, moving people's hearts.

projects.name: 徐大章老屋
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 五峰乡上塔村三组
projects.address_en: Group 3, Shangta Village, Wufeng Township
highlights: 房主徐大章曾在陕西耀州任州官
也有逐层跌落的马头墙
第一进院落东西窄而南北长
第二进后院的二楼则有四面相连的回廊
老屋外墙的石质窗户上有精致的夔龙窗格
格心为人物、麒麟等图案
院内的门窗、栏杆、斜撑、柱础等也均装饰有蝙蝠、花草等纹样
老屋曾被用作乡粮管所
现在则是6户村民的居所
除了门厅一侧被改建为砖房
院内的部分槅扇门丢失外
整体保存情况相对完好
projects.content_zh: 老屋建于清代，房主徐大章曾在陕西耀州任州官。房屋坐东朝西，二进三重天井院，各进均面阔五间，共有房屋23间，二层砖木混合结构，穿斗式梁架，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，山墙有人字形的，也有逐层跌落的马头墙。第一进院落东西窄而南北长，第二进后院的二楼则有四面相连的回廊。老屋外墙的石质窗户上有精致的夔龙窗格，格心为人物、麒麟等图案，院内的门窗、栏杆、斜撑、柱础等也均装饰有蝙蝠、花草等纹样。'大跃进'时期，老屋曾被用作乡粮管所，现在则是6户村民的居所，除了门厅一侧被改建为砖房，院内的部分槅扇门丢失外，整体保存情况相对完好。
projects.content_en: The old house was built in the Qing Dynasty; the owner Xu Dazhang once served as the prefect of Yaozhou in Shaanxi. The house faces west from east, with two entries and three courtyard (tianjing) compounds; each entry is five bays wide, with a total of 23 rooms, a two-story brick-wood mixed structure, column-and-tie beam frames, a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, and gable walls that are either herringbone-shaped or stepped horse-head gable walls. The first courtyard is narrow east-west and long north-south; the second floor of the second rear courtyard has corridors connected on all four sides. On the stone windows of the exterior wall of the old house, there are exquisite kui-dragon window lattices, with the lattice center featuring patterns of figures, kylins, etc.; the doors, windows, railings, diagonal braces, and column plinths in the courtyard are also decorated with patterns such as bats and flowers. During the 'Great Leap Forward' period, the old house was once used as the township grain management office; now it is the residence of 6 households of villagers; except that one side of the entrance hall has been converted into a brick house and some lattice doors in the courtyard have been lost, the overall preservation condition is relatively intact.

projects.name: 冻青古建筑
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位

projects.address_en: Dongqinggou Village, Hujiaying Town, south bank of Han River, entering the valley from Sancha Village

是湖北省迄今为止发现的规模最大、功能最完备、资料最完整
保存状况也较好的清代村落遗址
以及宗祠祠堂、影壁、寨堡和古道等
多数建筑建于清道光前期
杨泗庙建立在沟口山顶处
是从汉江边唯一能看到的建筑物
相传为水神杨泗将军而设
从前人们捕鱼或出门经商均依靠汉江
去杨泗庙焚香祷告是所有船只开船前必需的活动
projects.content_zh: 冻青古建筑坐落在汉江南岸，是湖北省迄今为止发现的规模最大、功能最完备、资料最完整，保存状况也较好的清代村落遗址，包括古民居8处，庙宇2处，以及宗祠祠堂、影壁、寨堡和古道等，共计14处，多数建筑建于清道光前期（1825—1830）。杨泗庙建立在沟口山顶处，是从汉江边唯一能看到的建筑物，相传为水神杨泗将军而设。从前人们捕鱼或出门经商均依靠汉江，去杨泗庙焚香祷告是所有船只开船前必需的活动。沿着山路进入山谷，
projects.content_en: The Dongqing ancient buildings are located on the south bank of the Han River, and are the largest, most functionally complete, most documentarily complete, and relatively well-preserved Qing Dynasty village site discovered so far in Hubei Province, including 8 ancient residences, 2 temples, as well as ancestral halls, screen walls, fortress, and ancient roads, totaling 14 places; most buildings were built in the early Daoguang period of the Qing (1825–1830). Yangsi Temple was built at the top of the mountain at the mouth of the gully, and is the only building visible from the Han River bank; legend has it that it was built for the water god General Yangsi. In the past, people fishing or going out to do business all relied on the Han River, and going to Yangsi Temple to burn incense and pray was a necessary activity before all ships set sail. projects.name: 武当山古建筑群
projects.name_en: Ancient Building Complex in the Wudang Mountains
projects.level: 世界文化遗产
projects.address: 武当山镇
projects.address_en: Wudangshan Town
highlights: 人间仙山天国三段规划
projects.content_zh: 武当山这座方圆八百里的名山，位于十堰丹江口市境内，东临襄阳，北临丹江口水库，又名太和山、仙室山。自唐代始建五龙祠开始，武当山一直是道教的重要福地。宋元以来，先后开五龙观为五龙观、五龙宫，又建紫霄宫和南岩天乙真庆宫，武当山逐渐形成了以真武崇拜为主要特征的武当道教，教统也已经有了相当的规模。根据道教经典记载，真武本为净乐国太子，入武当山修道，历四十二年而功成飞升，被玉帝封为北方之神和水神，武当山也因'非真武不足以当之'而得名。明初永乐年间，武当山迎来了一次史无前例的发展。1403年，燕王朱棣以'靖难'之名，从侄子建文帝手中夺取皇位。为使皇权名正言顺、天下归心，平息朱棣君篡位的舆论，这位起兵于北方的永乐皇帝宣称自己起兵'靖难'是得到了真武的旨意和保佑，是君权神授、天人感应。而另一方面，在敕建武当山的碑文中提到，以水神真武坐镇被认为是火相山的武当山，也有水火调和、天下既济的意思。大规模振兴武当山的工程始于永乐十年（1412），隆平侯张信、驸马都尉沐昕、工部右侍郎郭琎、礼部尚书金纯等率30万民夫进驻武当山，南方六省的钱粮赋税亦全部用于这项工程。历时十三年，终于建成了这一旷世的宗教建筑群：八宫、二观、三十六庵堂、七十二岩庙，共有33个建筑群，殿宇2万余间，还有70公里的石蹬道、39座桥梁和12座厅堂，总占地面积达到160万平方米，是明代时间最长、规模最大的国家工程。如此浩大的规模，武当山的自然环境却几乎没有遭到破坏：一方面是出于对神灵的敬重，皇帝下旨不准破坏山体、砍伐树木，所用木材全部从两湖、川陕等地征调，不动当地一草一木；另一方面依照道教重生、顺应自然的思想，所有建筑随山势地形展开，与自然景观达到了高度的和谐。1994年武当山古建筑群入选世界文化遗产名录时，来自世界的评委会专家也为武当山宏大的建筑规模与保存完整的自然风貌而赞叹。朱棣大修武当山，除了平息舆论以外，目的和意义也是多重的：一方面他封武当山为'大岳'，实际上是另一种形式的封禅，以标榜自己的文治武功；另一方面是为迁都北平、营建北京城进行练兵，后来紫禁城的兴建经过了长期准备、周密计划和充足的备料，但从施工到建成仅仅用了3年时间，便是在借鉴武当山经验的基础上得以实现的；还有一点是裁减军队，建文时期的降军几乎全部派往武当山修庙，客观上有利于社会的安定。此后明朝的新帝登基，无不效法祖制，对武当山许以各种特权，并直接委派内臣代表皇帝对武当山进行管理，嘉靖年间还进行过一次大规模的维修和扩建。终明朝一代，武当山一直是皇室庙和全国的道教活动中心，各大宫中常设坛打醮，祈求风调雨顺，江山永固。武当山的规划者以真武下凡修真得道飞升、显圣治世的故事为依据，将整个建筑群分为人间（人）、仙山（地）、天国（天）三个部分来规划，三段的长度比例为3:2:1，又暗合了老子'人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然'和'道生一，一生二，二生三，三生万物'的思想。在具体建筑的选址、造型上尊重原本的山形地貌，疏密相间、错落有致、巧妙借自然。人间部分自古均州至玄岳门，根据净乐太子诞生、生长成人、潜心向道的故事进行布局。这一段地势平缓，按照人力目力所及和情绪变化，3至5里有一组小型建筑，如紫阳庵、申府庵、晋府庵等；8至10里为一组大型建筑，如净乐宫、玄岳宫、兴隆观、迎恩宫、修真观等，其中位于古均州城内的净乐宫是这一部分规模最大的建筑。进入玄岳门一直到南岩，是仙山的范围。这一段穿插三个真武入山修道的故事，象征着修炼的三个境界。第一个故事是真武太子15岁受紫元君点化，赴太和山修炼，从玄岳门进山，先遇遇真宫、玉虚宫，修炼之初思凡下山，又遇上紫元君真幻化之磨针老妇点化，回心归山修炼，有回龙观、回心庵、磨针井、复真观等建筑群。第二个故事是太子越水过关，入仙境修炼，有龙泉观、天津桥、仙关、紫霄宫、太子洞等建筑。第三个故事讲太子修炼日久，有黑虎巡山、乌鸦报晓，紫元君扮成美女来引诱，太子拒绝美色，挂衣萝衣而飞升，建有黑虎庙、乌鸦庙、南岩宫等。
projects.content_en: Wudang Mountain, a famous mountain with a circumference of eight hundred li, is located in Danjiangkou City, Shiyan, bordering Xiangyang to the east and the Danjiangkou Reservoir to the north; it is also called Taihe Mountain and Xianshi Mountain. Since the construction of Wulong Temple began in the Tang Dynasty, Wudang Mountain has always been an important blessed land of Taoism. Since the Song and Yuan dynasties, Wulong Temple was successively developed into Wulong Temple and Wulong Palace, and Zixiao Palace and Nanyan Tianyi Zhenqing Palace were also built; Wudang Mountain gradually formed Wudang Taoism characterized by the worship of Zhenwu (Perfected Warrior), and its religious lineage had already reached a considerable scale. According to Taoist classics, Zhenwu was originally the crown prince of the Jingle Kingdom; he entered Wudang Mountain to cultivate the Tao, and after forty-two years achieved success and ascended to immortality; he was enfeoffed by the Jade Emperor as the god of the north and the god of water, and Wudang Mountain was named because 'none but Zhenwu is worthy to be matched with it.' In the early Ming Yongle period, Wudang Mountain ushered in an unprecedented development. In 1403, Prince Yan Zhu Di, under the name of 'Jingnan' (Pacifying the Disaster), seized the throne from his nephew, the Jianwen Emperor. To make the imperial power legitimate and win the submission of the world, and to quell the public opinion of Zhu Di usurping the throne, this Yongle Emperor, who raised troops in the north, declared that his raising troops for 'Jingnan' had received the will and blessing of Zhenwu, and was the divine right of kings and the interaction between heaven and man. On the other hand, in the inscription of the imperial construction of Wudang Mountain, it is mentioned that having the water god Zhenwu sit in Wudang Mountain, which was considered a fire-phase mountain, also had the meaning of harmonizing water and fire and bringing peace to the world. The large-scale project to revitalize Wudang Mountain began in the 10th year of Yongle (1412); Zhang Xin, Marquis of Longping, Mu Xin, Princess husband, Guo Jin, Right Vice Minister of Works, Jin Chun, Minister of Rites, and others led 300,000 laborers to station in Wudang Mountain, and the grain, money, and taxes of the six southern provinces were also all used for this project. After thirteen years, this unparalleled religious building complex was finally completed: eight palaces, two temples, thirty-six nunneries, seventy-two rock temples, with a total of 33 building groups, more than 20,000 halls, as well as 70 kilometers of stone stairways, 39 bridges, and 12 halls, with a total land area of 1.6 million square meters; it was the longest and largest national project of the Ming Dynasty. Despite such a vast scale, the natural environment of Wudang Mountain was almost undamaged: on the one hand, out of reverence for the gods, the emperor issued decrees not to damage the mountain body or cut down trees, and all timber used was requisitioned from Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi and other places, without touching a single plant or tree locally; on the other hand, in accordance with the Taoist thought of valuing life and conforming to nature, all buildings were arranged along the mountain terrain, achieving a high degree of harmony with the natural landscape. When the Ancient Building Complex in the Wudang Mountains was inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List in 1994, experts from the international jury also marveled at the grand architectural scale and the well-preserved natural landscape of Wudang Mountain. Zhu Di large-scale renovation of Wudang Mountain, besides quelling public opinion, had multiple purposes and meanings: on the one hand, he enfeoffed Wudang Mountain as 'Great Mountain,' which was actually another form of fengshan (heaven and earth sacrifice), to flaunt his civil and military achievements; on the other hand, it was training for moving the capital to Beiping and building the Beijing city; the later construction of the Forbidden City, after long-term preparation, careful planning, and sufficient preparation of materials, took only 3 years from construction to completion, which was achieved on the basis of drawing on the experience of Wudang Mountain; another point was to reduce the army, and almost all the surrendered troops from the Jianwen period were sent to Wudang Mountain to build temples, which objectively contributed to social stability. Thereafter, every new emperor of the Ming Dynasty, without exception, followed the ancestral system, granted various privileges to Wudang Mountain, and directly appointed eunuchs to manage Wudang Mountain on behalf of the emperor; during the Jiajing period, a large-scale maintenance and expansion was also carried out. Throughout the Ming Dynasty, Wudang Mountain was always the imperial temple and the national center of Taoist activities; major palaces regularly held altars and Taoist rituals to pray for favorable weather and eternal stability of the country. The planners of Wudang Mountain, based on the story of Zhenwu descending to earth, cultivating the Tao, achieving immortality, ascending, and manifesting holiness to govern the world, divided the entire building complex into three parts: the human world (human), the immortal mountain (earth), and the heavenly kingdom (heaven); the length ratio of the three sections is 3:2:1, which also暗合 Laozi 'human follows the earth, earth follows heaven, heaven follows the Tao, and the Tao follows nature' and 'the Tao gives birth to one, one gives birth to two, two gives birth to three, and three gives birth to all things.' In the site selection and modeling of specific buildings, the original mountain topography was respected, with疏密相间, staggered arrangement, and clever borrowing of nature. The human world part, from ancient Junzhou to Xuanyue Gate, was laid out according to the story of the birth, growth to adulthood, and devotion to the Tao of Crown Prince Jingle. This section has gentle terrain; according to the reach of human vision and emotional changes, there is a group of small buildings every 3 to 5 li, such as Ziyang Nunnery, Shenfu Nunnery, Jinfu Nunnery, etc.; every 8 to 10 li there is a group of large buildings, such as Jingle Palace, Xuanyue Palace, Xinglong Temple, Ying'en Palace, Xiuzhen Temple, etc., among which Jingle Palace, located in ancient Junzhou city, is the largest building in this section. From entering Xuanyue Gate all the way to Nanyan, it is the scope of the immortal mountain. This section interweaves three stories of Zhenwu entering the mountain to cultivate the Tao, symbolizing three realms of cultivation. The first story is that Crown Prince Zhenwu, at the age of 15, was enlightened by Ziyuan Zhenjun and went to Taihe Mountain to cultivate; entering the mountain from Xuanyue Gate, he first encountered Yuzhen Palace and Yuxu Palace; at the beginning of cultivation, he missed the mortal world and went down the mountain, then encountered the old woman grinding a needle, an incarnation of Ziyuan Zhenjun, who enlightened him, so he returned to the mountain to cultivate; there are building groups such as Huilong Temple, Huixin Nunnery, Needle Grinding Well, and Fuzhen Temple. The second story is that the prince crossed water and passed through gates to enter the immortal realm to cultivate; there are buildings such as Longquan Temple, Tianjin Bridge, Immortal Gate, Zixiao Palace, and Prince Cave. The third story tells that after the prince cultivated for a long time, there were black tigers patrolling the mountain and crows announcing dawn; Ziyuan Zhenjun disguised as a beauty to seduce him, but the prince refused the beauty, hung his clothes on a radish vine, and ascended to immortality; buildings such as Black Tiger Temple, Crow Temple, and Nanyan Palace were built.

projects.name: 遇真宫
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山镇东四公里
projects.address_en: 4 km east of Wudangshan Town
highlights: 武当山道场的序幕式建筑
香霭亲霞楼仙乐空中流
projects.content_zh: 遇真，即'渴望遇见传奇道人张三丰'之意。相传明洪武年间，张三丰在此筑庵，名会仙馆，永乐初年成祖数次下旨召见而皆不遇，于是筑此宫以寄托思慕之情，是八宫中渲染修仙、烘托武当山道场的序幕式建筑群。遇真宫位于武当山镇以东约4公里处，面对九龙山，背倚凤凰山，于永乐十年（1412）敕建，3年后竣工。建筑群分为中宫、东宫和西宫，中宫建有大宫门、龙虎殿、真仙殿等主要建筑，东西两宫有方丈、斋堂、厨堂、道房、仓库、浴堂等，初时共有97间，后扩大至396间，占地3万平方米。院落宽敞，幽雅静穆，在明朝就被誉为'香霭亲霞楼，仙乐空中流'的灵境。
projects.content_en: Yuzhen (Meeting the Perfected) means 'longing to meet the legendary Taoist Zhang Sanfeng.' Legend has it that during the Hongwu period of the Ming, Zhang Sanfeng built a nunnery here, named Huixian Hall (Meeting Immortals Hall); in the early Yongle period, the Chengzu Emperor issued decrees several times to summon him but never met him, so he built this palace to express his longing; it is the prologue-style building complex among the eight palaces that renders the atmosphere of cultivating immortality and sets off the Wudang Mountain Taoist site. Yuzhen Palace is located about 4 kilometers east of Wudangshan Town, facing Jiulong Mountain and backing onto Fenghuang (Phoenix) Mountain; it was imperially built in the 10th year of Yongle (1412) and completed 3 years later. The building complex is divided into the Central Palace, Eastern Palace, and Western Palace; the Central Palace has main buildings such as the Great Gate, Dragon-Tiger Hall, and Zhenxian (Perfect Immortal) Hall; the Eastern and Western Palaces have abbot quarters, vegetarian halls, kitchens, Taoist rooms, warehouses, bathhouses, etc.; initially there were 97 rooms in total, later expanded to 396 rooms, covering 30,000 square meters. The courtyards are spacious, elegant, quiet, and solemn; in the Ming Dynasty it was already hailed as a spiritual realm where 'incense mist caresses the rosy tower, and immortal music flows in the air.'

projects.name: 玉虚宫遗址
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山镇
projects.address_en: Wudangshan Town
projects.content_zh: 玉虚宫全称玄天玉虚宫，是武当山八宫中规模最大的建筑组群，也是明代大兴武当的大本营，因此又称老营宫。玉虚宫于明永乐十一年（1413）敕建，嘉靖三十一年（1552）扩建，占地约50万平方米。建筑坐南朝北，中轴对称，平面呈'凸'字形，按照周礼中'天子三朝五门'的形制布局，有外罗城、内罗城和紫禁城三道城墙。嘉靖年间扩建的部分由于兴建汉十铁路和武当山镇，格局已不存；永乐年间的建筑布局则保持较为完整，占地约12万平方米。主体建筑东西分为5路，中轴线上有龙虎殿、十方堂、玄帝殿和父母殿4座大殿，又有大宫门、二宫门、玉带桥、御碑亭2对，配殿、廊庑等。中路宫墙两侧以外各有夹墙复道，与北京故宫东西夹道的规制相同。东宫中有神厨、神库、浴堂、方丈、斋堂等，西宫则有钵堂、圜堂等，东宫以东、西宫以西则为道士生活区，共有建筑2200余间。玉虚宫大部分的主要建筑于清乾隆十年（1745）毁于火灾，1938年汉水上涨又毁去一部分木结构。现存建筑以大宫门保存最为完好，砖木结构，单檐歇山绿琉璃瓦顶，三道拱券门，下设须弥座台基，前有月台和望柱栏杆，两侧与琉璃八字墙相接，琉璃琼花图案圆润富丽。门内外各有御碑亭一对，分别是永乐和嘉靖年间的遗物，楼顶木结构已不存，亭内各有6米高的石碑一座，以赑屃负之，总重量达90吨。玉虚宫为武当山八宫中规模最大的建筑群，是皇帝封禅武当、祀天修崇醮典的总坛。在2012年之前，玉虚宫遗址虽荒芜凋敝，但依稀可见当年宏伟的规模；2007-2012经过5年间修复御碑亭、大宫门，复建玄帝殿等工程，今日的玉虚宫已经成为市民休闲的广场和孩子们嬉戏的乐园。特别是每年农历三月初三真武诞辰之日，玉虚宫前会举行盛大的'三月三庙会'，这一天张灯结彩、鼓乐喧天、人头攒动，依稀可以窥见当年热闹非凡的场面。
projects.content_en: Yuxu Palace, fully named Xuantian Yuxu Palace, is the largest building group among the eight palaces of Wudang Mountain, and was also the base camp for the large-scale development of Wudang in the Ming Dynasty, hence also called Laoying Palace. Yuxu Palace was imperially built in the 11th year of Yongle, Ming (1413), and expanded in the 31st year of Jiajing (1552), covering about 500,000 square meters. The buildings face north from south, with central axis symmetry, and the plane is 'convex'-shaped; laid out according to the form of 'three courts and five gates for the Son of Heaven' in the Rites of Zhou, there are three city walls: the Outer Luocheng, Inner Luocheng, and Forbidden City. The part expanded during the Jiajing period no longer retains its layout due to the construction of the Han-Shi Railway and Wudangshan Town; the building layout from the Yongle period is relatively well-preserved, covering about 120,000 square meters. The main buildings are divided into 5 routes east and west; on the central axis there are 4 great halls: Dragon-Tiger Hall, Shifang Hall, Xuandi (Dark Emperor) Hall, and Parents Hall, as well as the Great Gate, Second Gate, Jade Belt Bridge, 2 pairs of Imperial Stele Pavilions, side halls, and corridors. Beyond both sides of the central palace wall, there are enclosed passageways between walls, the same regulation as the east and west side passages of the Forbidden City in Beijing. In the Eastern Palace there are divine kitchens, divine warehouses, bathhouses, abbot quarters, vegetarian halls, etc.; in the Western Palace there are alms-bowl halls, meditation halls, etc.; east of the Eastern Palace and west of the Western Palace are the living areas for Taoists, with a total of more than 2,200 buildings. Most of the main buildings of Yuxu Palace were destroyed by fire in the 10th year of Qianlong, Qing (1745), and in 1938 the rising Han River destroyed another part of the wooden structure. Among the existing buildings, the Great Gate is the best preserved; it is of brick-wood structure, with a single-eave hip-and-gable green glazed tile roof, three arched gates, a xumizuo (Sumeru) pedestal below, a moon terrace and balustrade with望柱 in front, and both sides connect to glazed splayed walls, with rounded and rich glazed flower patterns. Inside and outside the gate there is a pair of Imperial Stele Pavilions each, relics of the Yongle and Jiajing periods respectively; the wooden structure of the pavilion roofs no longer exists, and inside each pavilion there is a 6-meter-high stele, carried by a bixi (mythical tortoise), with a total weight of 90 tons. Yuxu Palace is the largest building complex among the eight palaces of Wudang Mountain, and was the main altar for the emperor fengshan sacrifice at Wudang and the grand Taoist rituals for heaven. Before 2012, although the Yuxu Palace site was desolate and dilapidated, the grand scale of that year could still be faintly seen; from 2007 to 2012, after 5 years of projects restoring the Imperial Stele Pavilions and Great Gate and rebuilding the Xuandi Hall, today Yuxu Palace has become a square for citizens leisure and a playground for children. Especially on the 3rd day of the 3rd lunar month every year, the birthday of Zhenwu, a grand 'March 3rd Temple Fair' is held in front of Yuxu Palace; on this day, lanterns and colorful decorations are hung, drums and music fill the air, and crowds throng, faintly allowing a glimpse of the extraordinarily lively scene of that year.

projects.name: 紫霄宫
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山展旗峰南
projects.address_en: South of Zhanqi Peak, Wudang Mountain
highlights: 重檐歇山蓝绿色琉璃瓦
projects.content_zh: 紫霄宫是武当山古建筑群中保存最为完好的宫观，背靠形同旌旗的展旗峰，前有'之'字形流淌的溪流，自然环境清幽秀丽。始建于北宋宣和年间（1119-1125），元代曾经经扩修，明永乐十年（1412）重建，嘉靖三十一年（1552）扩建，清代多次修缮和增补。坐西北朝东南，占地面积约27.4万平方米。中轴线上有龙虎殿、御碑亭、十方堂、紫霄殿及父母殿几座重要建筑，此外还有钟鼓楼、焚帛炉、东西配殿，以及东西宫院、道房、神厨和南天门、威烈观等建筑。主体建筑紫霄殿为重檐歇山屋顶，覆蓝绿色琉璃瓦，黄色琉璃屋脊，面阔、进深均为五间，高约20米，抬梁式木结构，上檐施七踩单翘重昂斗拱，下檐为五踩重昂金溜金斗拱，菱花隔扇门窗，殿内有八角藻井，正中设高大的石雕须弥座，供奉真武及金童玉女。殿内雕梁画栋，造型端庄稳重，是武当山具有代表性的木结构大殿之一，也是明代初年官式做法的珍贵实例。1931年，贺龙领导的红三军军部和后方医院曾设于宫内，如今这里是山上最具人气的道观，也是武当山道教学会的所在地，博大精深的道教文化和保存完好的自然风貌，吸引了中外道教信徒来这里修行。
projects.content_en: Zixiao (Purple Cloud) Palace is the best-preserved palace among the ancient building complex of Wudang Mountain, backing onto Zhanqi (Flag-Bearing) Peak shaped like a banner, with a zigzag-flowing stream in front, and a serene and beautiful natural environment. It was first built during the Xuanhe period of the Northern Song (1119–1125), expanded during the Yuan Dynasty, rebuilt in the 10th year of Yongle, Ming (1412), expanded in the 31st year of Jiajing (1552), and repaired and supplemented many times during the Qing Dynasty. Facing southeast from northwest, it covers an area of about 274,000 square meters. On the central axis there are several important buildings: Dragon-Tiger Hall, Imperial Stele Pavilion, Shifang Hall, Zixiao Hall, and Parents Hall; in addition there are bell and drum towers, paper-burning furnace, east and west side halls, as well as east and west palace courtyards, Taoist rooms, divine kitchen, South Heaven Gate, and Weilie Temple. The main building, Zixiao Hall, has a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, covered with blue-green glazed tiles and a yellow glazed ridge; it is five bays wide and five bays deep, about 20 meters high, with a post-and-lintel wooden structure; the upper eave uses seven-step single-raised double-ang bracket sets, and the lower eave uses five-step double-ang golden sliding bracket sets; with lattice doors and windows, an octagonal caisson inside the hall, and a tall stone-carved xumizuo (Sumeru) pedestal in the center, enshrining Zhenwu and the Golden Boy and Jade Maiden. Inside the hall, carved beams and painted rafters create a dignified and steady shape; it is one of the representative wooden-structure great halls of Wudang Mountain and a precious example of official-style practices from the early Ming Dynasty. In 1931, the military headquarters and rear hospital of the Third Red Army led by He Long were once set up inside the palace; today it is the most popular Taoist temple on the mountain and the location of the Wudang Mountain Taoist Association. The profound Taoist culture and well-preserved natural landscape attract Taoist believers from home and abroad to come here to cultivate.

projects.name: 南岩宫
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山乌鸦岭
projects.address_en: Wuya Ridge, Wudang Mountain
projects.content_zh: 南岩宫是武当三十六岩中景致最为优美的地方，传说中真武大帝便是在此得道飞升的。始建于唐代，南宋后期被毁，元中统年间重修，延祐元年（1314）敕赐为'天乙真庆万寿宫'，明永乐十一年（1413）扩建北坡玄帝殿、龙虎殿、玉皇殿等规模较大的建筑，嘉靖年间又扩建至600余间。
projects.content_en: Nanyan (South Cliff) Palace is the most scenic place among the thirty-six cliffs of Wudang Mountain; legend has it that the Great Emperor Zhenwu attained the Tao and ascended to immortality here. It was first built in the Tang Dynasty, destroyed in the late Southern Song, rebuilt during the Zhongtong period of the Yuan, and in the 1st year of Yanyou (1314) was imperially granted the name 'Tianyi Zhenqing Wanshou Palace'; in the 11th year of Yongle, Ming (1413), large-scale buildings such as the Xuandi Hall, Dragon-Tiger Hall, and Jade Emperor Hall on the northern slope were expanded, and during the Jiajing period it was further expanded to more than 600 rooms.

projects.name: 太和宫
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山天柱峰
projects.address_en: Tianzhu Peak, Wudang Mountain
projects.content_zh: 太和宫位于武当山主峰——海拔1613米的天柱峰上，宋元时期即开始建设，大规模的兴建始于明永乐十年（1412）。太和宫的建筑也可分为两组，天柱峰南麓几座山丘之间的是太和宫，建筑顺着山腰蜿蜒，有朝圣门、斋堂、天云楼、皇经堂、转运殿、朝拜殿、太和殿、钟鼓楼和配殿等；另一组建筑在紫金城墙以内，沿天柱峰环绕而上，依次为南天门、灵官殿、配房、金殿、父母殿等，俗称'金顶'。总占地面积约5000平方米，其中紫金城内的面积约1600平方米。太和宫最南端的建筑名为转运殿，分内外殿。外殿建于明永乐年间，单檐歇山琉璃瓦顶，北面设山门；内殿为元大德十一年（1307）铸造的铜殿，平面大致为2.7米×2.7米的方形，单檐悬山顶，仿木结构，穿斗式构架。这座铜殿是我国最早的铜殿，由武昌等地的信士捐资，各个部件在武昌铸造完成后运至武当山，而后以榫卯拼接，置于金顶，永乐年间大修武当山时移至今天的位置。从转运殿向北进入太和宫门，前方的朝拜殿和左
projects.content_en: Taihe (Supreme Harmony) Palace is located on Tianzhu (Heavenly Pillar) Peak, the main peak of Wudang Mountain at an altitude of 1613 meters; construction began in the Song and Yuan periods, and large-scale construction started in the 10th year of Yongle, Ming (1412). The buildings of Taihe Palace can also be divided into two groups: between several hills at the southern foot of Tianzhu Peak is Taihe Palace, with buildings winding along the mountainside, including the Pilgrimage Gate, vegetarian hall, Tianyun Tower, Huangjing (Imperial Sutra) Hall, Transport Hall, Worship Hall, Taihe Hall, bell and drum towers, and side halls; the other group of buildings is inside the Zijin (Purple Gold) City wall, winding up along Tianzhu Peak, in order: South Heaven Gate, Lingguan Hall, side rooms, Golden Hall, Parents Hall, etc., commonly called 'Golden Summit.' The total land area is about 5,000 square meters, of which the area inside Zijin City is about 1,600 square meters. The southernmost building of Taihe Palace is named Transport Hall, divided into inner and outer halls. The outer hall was built in the Yongle period of the Ming, with a single-eave hip-and-gable glazed tile roof and a mountain gate on the north side; the inner hall is a bronze hall cast in the 11th year of Dade, Yuan (1307), with a plane roughly 2.7 meters × 2.7 meters square, a single-eave overhanging gable roof, imitating a wooden structure with a column-and-tie frame. This bronze hall is the earliest bronze hall in China; it was donated by believers from Wuchang and other places, with all parts cast in Wuchang and then transported to Wudang Mountain, then assembled with mortise and tenon joints and placed on the Golden Summit; during the major renovation of Wudang Mountain in the Yongle period, it was moved to its current location. From the Transport Hall northward into the Taihe Palace gate, the worship hall ahead and the left

projects.name: 元和观
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山镇东3公里
projects.address_en: 3 km east of Wudangshan Town
highlights: 进玄岳门之后的第一座道观
道教法庭和关押违反清规戒律的道人
永乐十年在元代遗址上重建
嘉靖三十年改建和增建
山门两侧带影壁和八字墙
大殿坐落在高大的台基上
projects.content_zh: 元和观是武当山进玄岳门之后的第一座道观。道教经典记载，玄武得道后曾掌管'元和迁校府'，元和观以此而得名。实际上，'迁'有放逐之意，而'校'则指刑具，因此元和观是武当道教处罚和关押违反清规戒律的道人的机构，是一座道教法庭和监狱。明永乐十年（1412）在元代遗址上重建，又敕建玄帝殿、山门、廊庑、东西方丈等44间，嘉靖三十年（1552）再次改建和增建，建筑规模比一般的道观大很多，仅次于遇真宫，现存大门、玄帝殿、配殿等37间。元和观布局紧凑，筑高墙厚，体现出与世隔绝的森严之气。山门为两侧带影壁和八字墙的歇山建筑，形制已如同宫殿，只是体量较小。大殿坐落在高大的台基上，面阔五间，进深三间，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，殿内山墙上还保存有宗教故事壁画。
projects.content_en: Yuanhe Temple is the first Taoist temple after entering Xuanyue Gate on Wudang Mountain. According to Taoist classics, after Xuanwu attained the Tao, he once administered the 'Yuanhe Qianjiao Mansion,' and Yuanhe Temple is named after this. In fact, 'Qian' means exile, and 'Jiao' refers to instruments of torture; therefore Yuanhe Temple was an institution of Wudang Taoism for punishing and imprisoning Taoists who violated the pure rules and commandments, a Taoist court and prison. It was rebuilt on the Yuan Dynasty site in the 10th year of Yongle, Ming (1412), and 44 rooms including the Xuandi Hall, mountain gate, corridors, and east and west abbot quarters were imperially built; in the 30th year of Jiajing (1552), it was again rebuilt and expanded, with a building scale much larger than ordinary Taoist temples, second only to Yuzhen Palace; currently 37 rooms including the gate, Xuandi Hall, and side halls remain. Yuanhe Temple has a compact layout with high thick walls, reflecting an air of strict isolation from the world. The mountain gate is a hip-and-gable building with screen walls and splayed walls on both sides, its form already like a palace, only smaller in volume. The main hall sits on a tall pedestal, five bays wide and three bays deep, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof; religious story murals are still preserved on the gable walls inside the hall.

projects.name: 复真观
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山太子坡
projects.address_en: Taizi Slope, Wudang Mountain
highlights: 净乐国太子15岁入山修炼
紫气元君化老妇用铁杵磨针点化
projects.content_zh: 俗称'太子坡'，是传说中净乐国太子15岁入武当山修炼时最初居住的地方。后来太子意志不坚，私自下山，在回家的路上遇到紫气元君幻化而成的老妇，用铁杵磨针点化，复又上山修炼，这组建筑因而得名复真观。始建于明永乐十二年（1414），嘉靖年间扩建，清康熙、乾隆年间4次重修。建筑群依山势展开，占地面积约1.6万平方米，有宫门、九曲黄河墙、龙虎殿、祖师殿、斗姆楼、藏经阁、皇经堂和五云楼等，共105间。其中，走进宫门后夹道随山势曲折，两侧的九曲黄河墙高低起伏，不见首尾，使人感到神秘而威严。而高达4层的五云楼则是武当山最高的建筑，室内一根立柱上穿插交叠十二根梁，被誉为'一柱十二梁'。
projects.content_en: Commonly called 'Taizi Slope' (Crown Prince Slope), it is the place where, according to legend, the crown prince of the Jingle Kingdom first lived when he entered Wudang Mountain to cultivate at the age of 15. Later, the crown prince's will was not firm and he secretly went down the mountain; on his way home, he met an old woman transformed by Ziyuan Zhenjun, who enlightened him by grinding an iron pestle into a needle, so he returned to the mountain to cultivate, hence this building group is named Fuzhen (Returning to Truth) Temple. It was first built in the 12th year of Yongle, Ming (1414), expanded during the Jiajing period, and rebuilt 4 times during the Kangxi and Qianlong periods of the Qing. The building group unfolds along the mountain terrain, covering about 16,000 square meters, with 105 rooms including the palace gate, Nine-Bend Yellow River Wall, Dragon-Tiger Hall, Patriarch Hall, Doumu Tower, Scripture Pavilion, Huangjing Hall, and Wuyun (Five Clouds) Tower. Among them, after entering the palace gate, the夹道 winds along the mountain terrain, and the Nine-Bend Yellow River Walls on both sides rise and fall, with neither beginning nor end visible, making people feel mysterious and solemn. The four-story Wuyun Tower is the tallest building on Wudang Mountain; inside, twelve beams are interlaced on one column, hailed as 'one column with twelve beams.'

projects.name: 治世玄岳牌坊
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山镇东6公里
projects.address_en: 6 km east of Wudangshan Town
highlights: 古均州城至武当山的官道与朝山进香的神道相接之处
四柱三间五楼仿木式样石牌坊
两面均镌刻嘉靖皇帝所题治世玄岳四个大字
脊上有鸱吻、宝瓶等装饰
鳌鱼、蟠龙、仙鹤、云水、水浪、如意、卷草和神仙人物图案
明代石雕中的上乘佳作
嘉靖皇帝修道成仙的愿望
projects.content_zh: '治世玄岳'牌坊，俗称玄岳门，位于古均州城至武当山的官道与朝山进香的神道相接之处，进入此门，便由人间进入仙山范围。始建于明嘉靖三十一年（1552），清乾隆二十年（1755）修缮。坐西朝东，四柱三间五楼仿木式样石牌坊，通高近12米。其中柱高6米有余，下有巨大的碌墩石。柱顶架龙门枋，明间嵌一块巨大的横匾，两面均镌刻嘉靖皇帝所题'治世玄岳'四个大字。石匾之上为又一道额枋，额枋上置六攒七踩斗拱，上承屋顶，屋脊上有鸱吻、宝瓶等装饰。两侧的次间、尽间分为两层，按照云板、额枋、斗拱、屋顶的顺序，依次架设。整个石坊的雕刻装饰异常华美，虽然匾额、斗拱等使用了皇家才能使用的规制，但雕刻题材却一反官式建筑中常见的龙凤狮子，而是鳌鱼、蟠龙、仙鹤、云水、水浪、如意、卷草和神仙人物图案，使得整个牌坊充满了神仙之气。线刻、浮雕、圆雕和透雕等技法使用娴熟，是明代石雕中的上乘佳作。治世玄岳石坊是明世宗嘉靖皇帝大修武当山的代表建筑，表达了嘉靖以道教治理天下的愿望。世宗崇信道教，在位时又多次逢凶化吉，为报答真武大帝的庇佑，按照明成祖的做法，成立了专门的指挥机构。施工之时恰逢郧阳、襄阳连年灾荒，朝廷转而以工代赈，不仅招募了大量廉价劳动力，节约了大批资金，也救济了灾民。工程历时1年零4个月，除了修建石坊，还维修了八宫和其所辖庙观的屋面，更换琉璃瓦，重做油漆彩绘，修补宫墙、台基、沟渠和神道、石桥等，并新增5座琉璃建筑。
projects.content_en: The 'Zhishi Xuanyue' (Governing the World, Mysterious Mountain) Archway, commonly called Xuanyue Gate, is located at the junction of the official road from ancient Junzhou city to Wudang Mountain and the sacred path for pilgrimages to the mountain; entering this gate, one moves from the human world into the scope of the immortal mountain. It was first built in the 31st year of Jiajing, Ming (1552), and repaired in the 20th year of Qianlong, Qing (1755). Facing east from west, it is a four-column three-bay five-story imitation-wood-style stone archway, with a total height of nearly 12 meters. The columns are more than 6 meters high, with huge lu-dun stones below. On top of the columns, longmen (dragon-gate) lintels are placed; in the central bay, a huge horizontal plaque is embedded, with the four large characters 'Zhishi Xuanyue' inscribed by the Jiajing Emperor on both sides. Above the stone plaque is another architrave; on the architrave, six sets of seven-step bracket sets are placed, supporting the roof; on the ridge there are decorations such as chiwen (dragon-like roof ornaments) and treasure vases. The secondary and end bays on both sides are divided into two stories, erected in sequence according to the order of cloud boards, architraves, bracket sets, and roofs. The carved decoration of the entire stone archway is extraordinarily gorgeous; although the plaque and bracket sets use regulations that only the imperial family could use, the carving themes, contrary to the dragon, phoenix, and lion commonly seen in official-style buildings, are patterns of mythical fish, coiling dragons, cranes, cloud-water, water waves, ruyi (auspicious), scrolling grass, and immortal figures, making the entire archway full of immortal atmosphere. Techniques such as line carving, relief carving, round carving, and openwork carving are used skillfully, making it a superior masterpiece of Ming stone carving. The Zhishi Xuanyue Stone Archway is a representative building of the Jiajing Emperor Shizong of Ming's large-scale renovation of Wudang Mountain, expressing Jiajing desire to govern the world through Taoism. Shizong believed in Taoism, and during his reign he repeatedly escaped danger; to repay the protection of the Great Emperor Zhenwu, following the practice of Emperor Chengzu of Ming, he established a special command organization. At the time of construction, it coincided with successive years of famine in Yunyang and Xiangyang; the court instead used work as relief, not only recruiting a large amount of cheap labor and saving a great deal of funds, but also relieving the disaster victims. The project lasted 1 year and 4 months; in addition to building the stone archway, it also repaired the roofs of the eight palaces and their subordinate temples, replaced glazed tiles, redid paint and colored drawings, repaired palace walls, pedestals, ditches, sacred paths, and stone bridges, and added 5 new glazed buildings.

projects.name: 琼台中观
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山金殿索道出口
projects.address_en: Exit of Golden Hall Cableway, Wudang Mountain
highlights: 清咸丰六年大部分毁于火
同治和光绪年间先后修复
projects.content_zh: 始建于元代，明崇祯九年（1636）重修，清咸丰六年（1856）大部分毁于火，同治和光绪年间先后修复。坐西南朝东北，占地面积约1.5万平方米，现存大殿、北配房、石殿等建筑，以及记载明清重修中观的石碑十余通。其中最重要的建筑为元代初年的石殿，殿高近4米，单檐歇山顶，殿内供奉石雕造像8尊。琼台三观曾经规模宏大，建筑之间亭桥相连，上观名为白玉龟台，中观叫紫岳琼台，下观为玉乐霄台。现上观仅存遗址，下观残存大殿和配殿13间。
projects.content_en: It was first built in the Yuan Dynasty, rebuilt in the 9th year of Chongzhen, Ming (1636), mostly destroyed by fire in the 6th year of Xianfeng, Qing (1856), and successively restored during the Tongzhi and Guangxu periods. Facing northeast from southwest, it covers about 15,000 square meters; existing buildings include the main hall, north side room, and stone hall, as well as more than ten stone steles recording the Ming and Qing restorations of the middle temple. The most important building is the stone hall of the early Yuan Dynasty, nearly 4 meters high, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, enshrining 8 stone-carved statues inside. The three Qiongtai temples were once large in scale, with pavilions and bridges connecting the buildings; the upper temple was named White Jade Tortoise Terrace, the middle temple was called Purple Mystic Qiongtai, and the lower temple was Jade Music Cloud Terrace. Now only ruins remain of the upper temple, while the lower temple has 13 remaining rooms of the main hall and side halls.

projects.name: 榔梅祠
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山乌鸦岭
projects.address_en: Wuya Ridge, Wudang Mountain
highlights: 榔梅是武当山独有的一种树
李时珍本草纲目记载榔梅只出均州太和山
徐霞客说榔梅开花时花色浮空映山绚丽
榔梅的果实也是明代的贡品
由武当山道士每年进献
榔梅祠正是因道士刘希将榔梅果进皇宫上而建
门额上嵌榔梅仙祠石匾
清代时武当山的榔梅树便完全绝迹
明代武当山作为贵重的礼物赠予齐云山
projects.content_zh: 榔梅是武当山独有的一种树，李时珍《本草纲目》记载：'榔梅，只出均州太和山。'徐霞客则说榔梅开花时'花色浮空，映山绚丽'。而榔梅的果实也是明代的贡品，由武当山道士每年进献，据传，榔梅祠正是因道士刘希将榔梅果进皇宫上而建。建于永乐十年（1412），占地面积1000平方米，有前殿、后殿和配殿，现存后殿为原物，其他建筑为1989年修复。后殿为单檐歇山灰瓦顶，四壁砖墙封砌，下有石雕须弥座。正面开拱券门，门额上嵌'榔梅仙祠'石匾。不知为何，到清代时武当山的榔梅树便完全绝迹，如今仅有几棵，是明代武当山作为贵重的礼物赠予齐云山，当代又从齐云山引回，栽种在榔梅祠旁的。
projects.content_en: Langmei (plum-apricot) is a tree unique to Wudang Mountain; Li Shizhen 'Compendium of Materia Medica' records: 'Langmei only grows in Taihe Mountain, Junzhou.' Xu Xiake said that when langmei blooms, 'the flower color floats in the air, reflecting the mountain gorgeously.' The fruit of langmei was also a tribute in the Ming Dynasty, offered annually by Wudang Mountain Taoists; according to legend, Langmei Shrine was built precisely because the Taoist Liu Xi presented langmei fruit to the imperial palace. It was built in the 10th year of Yongle (1412), covering 1,000 square meters, with a front hall, rear hall, and side halls; the existing rear hall is original, and the other buildings were restored in 1989. The rear hall has a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, with brick walls sealing all four sides and a stone-carved xumizuo (Sumeru) pedestal below. On the front, an arched gate is opened, with a stone plaque 'Langmei Immortal Shrine' embedded on the lintel. For unknown reasons, by the Qing Dynasty the langmei trees on Wudang Mountain had completely disappeared; today there are only a few, which Wudang Mountain gave as a precious gift to Qiyun Mountain in the Ming Dynasty, and were brought back from Qiyun Mountain in contemporary times and planted beside Langmei Shrine.

projects.name: 朝天宫
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山欢喜坡
projects.address_en: Huanxi Slope, Wudang Mountain
highlights: 明永乐十年敕建玄帝殿、配殿等17间
坐落在一组高耸的台基之上
projects.content_zh: 始建于元代，后屡建屡毁，明永乐十年（1412）敕建玄帝殿、配殿等17间，嘉靖年间扩建，清代、民国多次修补。现有山门、大殿、配殿等建筑。建筑群顺应地势，坐落在一组高耸的台基之上，被认为是人间与仙境的分界线。
projects.content_en: It was first built in the Yuan Dynasty, later repeatedly built and destroyed; in the 10th year of Yongle, Ming (1412), 17 rooms including the Xuandi Hall and side halls were imperially built, expanded during the Jiajing period, and repaired many times during the Qing and Republican periods. Existing buildings include the mountain gate, main hall, and side halls. The building group conforms to the terrain, sitting on a group of towering pedestals, and is considered the dividing line between the human world and the immortal realm.

projects.name: 一天门、二天门、三天门
projects.name_en: Chaotian Palace (First, Second, Third Heaven Gates)
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 武当山欢喜坡至天柱峰
projects.address_en: Huanxi Slope to Tianzhu Peak, Wudang Mountain
highlights: 三座天门中各存有从明至民国的石碑若干通
projects.content_zh: 这三座天门皆位于从朝天宫到太和宫的神道上，山势转折之处。始建于元代，明永乐年间重建，规制完全相同：砖石结构拱券门，通高近7米，单檐歇山顶，须弥座，檐下嵌石匾书写名称。三座天门中各存有从明至民国的石碑若干通。
projects.content_en: These three Heaven Gates are all located on the sacred path from Chaotian Palace to Taihe Palace, at the turning points of the mountain terrain. They were first built in the Yuan Dynasty and rebuilt during the Yongle period of the Ming, with completely identical regulations: brick-stone structure arched gates, with a total height of nearly 7 meters, single-eave hip-and-gable roofs, xumizuo (Sumeru) pedestals, and stone plaques embedded under the eaves writing their names. In each of the three Heaven Gates, several stone steles from the Ming to the Republican period are preserved.

projects.name: 饶氏庄园
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 浪河镇黄龙村水田畈
projects.address_en: Shuitianfan, Huanglong Village, Langhe Town
highlights: 武当峡谷第一漂景区附近
通过捐官拥有自己的军队
入口南侧四层的巨大碉楼
每面都有若干大小形状相同的孔洞
大门两侧云形马头山墙
山墙上雕刻五只蝙蝠寓意五福临门
镂雕莲花、凤凰、牡丹、缠枝花纹
第一进厅屋中斜撑采用镂空雕刻
黄杨木、银杏木等名贵材料
八仙过海、十八相送、刘海砍樵、曹冲称象、孔子讲学
文革时期被毛主语录纸糊起来
主院左下人居住的配院
小猴子拴马桩寓意马上封侯
主院右边仅以简单土墙围绕
解放初期农民扒院墙盖房
projects.content_zh: 位于'武当峡谷第一漂'景区附近，当地人称清末庄园。庄园的主人饶志义（1887-1926，一说饶宗义、饶崇义），18岁便开始做盐运生意，并逐步积攒了大量的财产，后来又通过捐官，拥有了自己的军队。乡里传说，饶志义在马背上行走10天，都不喝别人的水，不走别人的路。在修建这座庄园时，他考虑到正逢乱世，特意挑选了这样一个偏远隐蔽的地方，不易被发现且易守难攻，也使得庄园的建筑得以相对完好地保存到今天。整个建筑群坐西朝东，有两进两路院落，硬山灰瓦屋顶。一眼望去最显眼的便是入口南侧四层的巨大碉楼，每面都有若干大小形状相同的孔洞，用于监视和狙击；最上层还有一个开放的外廊，周围环绕以木制栏杆，屋顶为四角攒尖顶。若大胆推测一些，在入口北侧，与现状位置对称的地方，也应该有一座一样的碉楼，这样庄园的格局才算完整。继续向前来到大门，首先是一道栅门，打开栅门才是厚重的正门。门楼两侧是云形马头山墙，山墙上雕刻五只蝙蝠，寓意'五福临门'。大门背面上方还有一个小小的露台，作戏台太小无法攀登，若用于储藏，则裙板上雕饰之莲花、凤凰、牡丹、缠枝花纹又显得太过奢侈。大门和二门之间是一个前院，向左可以通向碉楼，而走进垂花门式的二门，进入主院之后可以看到，这样精美的木雕在院中比比皆是。第一进厅屋中的斜撑采用了镂空雕刻的技法，曲线造型显得浑厚有力；而主院中每一道梁枋上都刻满了人物故事，材料用名贵的黄杨木、银杏木等，题材则有八仙过海、十八相送、刘海砍樵、曹冲称象、孔子讲学等。这些珍贵的木雕在'文革'时被一位有心的老木匠用一种粗糙的皮纸糊起来，上面写上毛主席语录，因此才能完整地保存到今天。从主院向左是下人居住的配院，建筑形制类似而无任何装饰，显示出等级的区别。院中还存有一对雕刻有小猴子的拴马桩，寓意'马上封侯'。主院的右边仅仅以简单的土墙围绕起来，院内有一两棵高大的植物。据管理员介绍，这里曾经是庄园的花园，面积也比现在大一倍，因为解放初期农民扒院墙盖房而逐渐毁坏，后来为保护庄园才筑起这道院墙。据说为修建这座庄园，饶志义在汉口聘请设计师
projects.content_en: Located near the 'Wudang Gorge No. 1 Rafting' scenic area, locals call it the late Qing manor. The owner of the manor, Rao Zhiyi (1887–1926, some say Rao Zongyi, Rao Chongyi), started a salt transportation business at the age of 18 and gradually accumulated a large amount of property; later, through donating for an official position, he had his own army. Local legend says that when Rao Zhiyi traveled on horseback for 10 days, he would not drink others water or walk on others roads. When building this manor, considering that it was a chaotic era, he specially chose such a remote and hidden place, not easy to be discovered and easy to defend but difficult to attack, which also allowed the manor buildings to be relatively well-preserved to this day. The entire building complex faces east from west, with two entries and two routes of courtyards, and gable gray-tile roofs. At first glance, the most conspicuous is the huge four-story watchtower south of the entrance; each side has several holes of the same size and shape, used for surveillance and sniping; on the top floor there is also an open veranda, surrounded by wooden railings, with a four-corner pyramidal roof. If one boldly speculates, on the north side of the entrance, at a position symmetrical to the current situation, there should also be an identical watchtower, so that the layout of the manor would be complete. Continuing forward to the main gate, first there is a fence gate; opening the fence gate is the heavy main gate. On both sides of the gate tower are cloud-shaped horse-head gable walls, with five bats carved on the gable walls, meaning 'five blessings arriving at the door.' Above the back of the main gate there is also a small terrace; too small to climb as a stage, and if used for storage, the carved lotus, phoenix, peony, and scrolling flower patterns on the skirt boards seem too luxurious. Between the main gate and the second gate is a front courtyard, to the left leading to the watchtower; entering the second gate in the form of a chuihuamen (flower-hung gate), after entering the main courtyard one can see that such exquisite wood carvings are everywhere in the courtyard. The diagonal braces in the first entry hall use the openwork carving technique, with curvilinear shapes appearing vigorous and powerful; while every beam in the main courtyard is covered with figure stories, using precious materials such as boxwood and ginkgo wood, with themes such as the Eight Immortals Crossing the Sea, Eighteen Send-offs, Liu Hai Cutting Firewood, Cao Chong Weighing the Elephant, and Confucius Teaching. These precious wood carvings were pasted over with a rough tissue paper by a caring old carpenter during the Cultural Revolution, with Chairman Mao quotations written on it, thus they could be completely preserved to this day. To the left from the main courtyard is the auxiliary courtyard where servants lived, with similar architectural form but without any decoration, showing the difference in rank. In the courtyard there is also a pair of horse-tying posts carved with little monkeys, meaning 'immediately conferred as a marquis.' The right side of the main courtyard is merely surrounded by a simple earthen wall, with one or two tall plants in the courtyard. According to the administrator, this was once the garden of the manor, and its area was also twice as large as now; because farmers tore down the courtyard wall to build houses in the early days after liberation, it was gradually destroyed, and later this courtyard wall was built to protect the manor. It is said that to build this manor, Rao Zhiyi hired a designer in Hankou

projects.name: 龙山宝塔
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.dynasty_en: Completed in 32nd year of Guangxu, Qing (1907)
projects.address: 土台乡龙巢山，丹江口水库库区旁
projects.address_en: Longchao Mountain, Tuitai Township, beside Danjiangkou Reservoir area
highlights: 清光绪二十六年至三十二年
眺望丹江口水库、汉水与武当山
为振兴艺文名为文笔塔
均州八景中今天唯一还能看到的龙山烟雨
塔后不远处曾有玉皇庙和禹王庙今已毁
projects.content_zh: 又名文笔塔，建于清光绪二十六年（1900）至三十二年（1907），是一座砖砌筑楼阁式风水塔，六角三层，高约12米。通过室内的木楼梯可以登上顶层，眺望丹江口水库、汉水与武当山的湖光山色。塔之得名，相传为镇龙颈、免水患，故名龙山塔；又说因位于古均州城东南，为振兴艺文，名为文笔塔。宝塔立于龙巢山之上，每天天色转阴之时，便能看到古'均州八景'中今天唯一还能看到的'龙山烟雨'。塔后不远处曾有玉皇庙和禹王庙，今已毁。
projects.content_en: Also called Wenbi (Writing Brush) Pagoda, built from the 26th year (1900) to the 32nd year (1907) of Guangxu, Qing, it is a brick-built pavilion-style fengshui pagoda, hexagonal with three stories, about 12 meters high. Through the indoor wooden staircase, one can climb to the top floor and overlook the lake and mountain scenery of the Danjiangkou Reservoir, Han River, and Wudang Mountain. The name of the pagoda, according to legend, is to suppress the dragon neck and avoid flood disasters, hence named Longshan (Dragon Mountain) Pagoda; another saying is that because it is located southeast of ancient Junzhou city, to revitalize literature and art, it is named Wenbi Pagoda. The pagoda stands on Longchao Mountain; every day when the sky turns overcast, one can see 'Longshan Misty Rain,' the only one of the ancient 'Eight Scenes of Junzhou' that can still be seen today. Not far behind the pagoda there were once the Jade Emperor Temple and Yu the Great Temple, now destroyed.

projects.name: 大晟庵箭楼
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 关垭镇银洞山村庵前沟，一处废弃铁矿西北的山坡上
projects.address_en: Slope northwest of an abandoned iron mine, Anqiangou, Yindongshan Village, Guanya Town
highlights: 大晟庵建筑群是武当古建筑群的组成部分
原有山门、前殿、主殿、左右厢房和箭楼等
箭楼位于右侧厢房的后方
在整个建筑群中位置最高
与道家提倡的道法自然、天人合一、修身养性、与世无争等理念明显不同
箭楼是一座军事防御建筑
各个墙面上不规则地分布着八个窗户和数十个箭孔
站在顶层则能轻松俯瞰周围数百平方米
箭楼顶部正中梁上有大明正德元年立大清乾隆九年重修等墨书题记
武当山境内首次在道教建筑群中修建的军事防御设施
projects.content_zh: 大晟庵建筑群是武当古建筑群的组成部分，原有山门、前殿、主殿、左右厢房和箭楼等组成，现存左右厢房和箭楼，其他建筑仅存基址。厢房面阔三间，高两层，单檐硬山灰瓦顶，二层有外廊和栏杆，现作为居住建筑使用。箭楼位于右侧厢房的后方，在整个建筑群中位置最高。与道家提倡的'道法自然、天人合一''修身养性、与世无争'等理念明显不同的是，箭楼是一座军事防御建筑，高四层，墙厚70厘米，各个墙面上不规则地分布着八个窗户和数十个箭孔，站在顶层则能轻松俯瞰周围数百平方米，显示出良好的防御功能。箭楼顶部正中梁上有'大明正德元年立''大清乾隆九年重修'等墨书题记，以及红黑相间的太极图案。箭楼也是武当山境内首次在道教建筑群中修建的军事防御设施。
projects.content_en: The Dasheng Temple building complex is part of the Wudang ancient building complex; it originally consisted of a mountain gate, front hall, main hall, left and right wing rooms, and an archery tower, etc.; currently the left and right wing rooms and the archery tower remain, while only the foundations of other buildings survive. The wing rooms are three bays wide, two stories high, with single-eave gable gray-tile roofs; the second floor has verandas and railings, and is now used as residential buildings. The archery tower is located behind the right wing room, at the highest position in the entire building complex. Obviously different from the concepts advocated by Taoism such as 'the Tao follows nature, heaven and humanity are one' and 'cultivating oneself and living in peace with the world,' the archery tower is a military defensive building, four stories high, with walls 70 centimeters thick; eight windows and dozens of arrow holes are irregularly distributed on each wall surface; standing on the top floor, one can easily overlook several hundred square meters around, showing good defensive function. On the central beam at the top of the archery tower, there are ink inscriptions such as 'Erected in the 1st year of Zhengde, Ming' and 'Rebuilt in the 9th year of Qianlong, Qing,' as well as red-and-black Taiji patterns. The archery tower is also the first military defensive facility built in a Taoist building complex within Wudang Mountain.

projects.name: 上津古城
projects.level: 国家级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 上津镇西街
projects.address_en: West Street, Shangjin Town

在此改由汉江水路通往江南和岭南地区
驿道偏僻、艰险、设备简陋
安史之乱和唐末节度使反叛时期成为保障首都物资的重要道路
上津的兴衰与全国军事政治形势的局势变化密切相关

水路向西南可以通向安康、汉中

战时流民来到上津居住
会折一枝家乡的柳树带来以寄托思乡之情

城的平面是一个东西约30米、南北长约300米的狭长长方形
西南还有一座小西门以方便居民出入

是山陕商人祭祀关公、联谊乡情并从事商业活动的重要场所
projects.content_zh: 上津道是唐代从首都长安向东南，陆行至商州上津县（今上津镇），在此改由汉江水路通往江南和岭南地区的一条驿道。这条驿道偏僻、艰险，设备简陋，因此只有在中原战乱、主要驿道阻塞不通时才被开辟使用，故而在安史之乱和唐末节度使反叛的时期，成为保障首都物资的重要道路。历史上，上津的兴衰与全国军事政治形势的局势变化密切相关。三国时期，上津附近最早设平阳县，南北朝时期先后为上洛郡、上津郡，并成为省级政区上州的治所；而从隋代以后又降为上津县，并一直保持到明代，到清康熙年间再降为上津堡。这说明在分裂战乱时期，特别是南北对峙的政权以秦岭为界，汉江上游成为重要的争夺对象时，上津的军事地位便会凸显出来。上津在水陆交通方面的重要性，表现为从水路向西南可以通向安康、汉中，向东南通向襄阳、武汉，陆路向西北通往长安，东北通往洛阳。唐中宗李显被贬为庐陵王前往均州（今丹江口市均县镇）时，便是在这里下马乘船，因此古城西门的码头也被称为'天子渡口'。据说，战时流民来到上津居住，会折一枝家乡的柳树带来以寄托思乡之情，久而久之，上津柳树成荫，也被称为柳州城。今天的上津古城墙建于明嘉靖二年（1523），清嘉庆七年（1802）重修，2005年成为国家级文物保护单位之后，又经历了一次大规模的修葺。城的平面是一个东西约30米、南北长约300米的狭长长方形，石垒墙基，砖砌城墙，高近7米，外有护城河。有五座城门，东为'向郧'，西为'通汉'，南为'达楚'，北为'接秦'，西南还有一座小西门以方便居民出入。城中偏西有一条南北向的主街，西门至主街还有一条小街，另外在北门外还保留着一条石子路老街和两排旧时民居。在城外东北的小山丘上还有一座山陕会馆，也称为关帝庙，始建于清乾隆、嘉庆交际之时，现仅存正殿的一进天井院。平面为三开间，单檐硬山灰瓦，第一进卷棚顶。殿内供奉关帝，是山陕商人祭祀关公、联谊乡情并从事商业活动的重要场所。
projects.content_en: The Shangjin Road was a post road in the Tang Dynasty from the capital Chang'an southeastward, traveling by land to Shangjin County of Shangzhou (today Shangjin Town), where it changed to the Han River waterway to reach the Jiangnan and Lingnan regions. This post road was remote, dangerous, and poorly equipped, so it was only opened and used when the Central Plains was in chaos and the main post roads were blocked; hence, during the An Lushan Rebellion and the period of jiedushi (military governor) rebellion at the end of the Tang, it became an important road for ensuring supplies to the capital. Historically, the rise and fall of Shangjin was closely related to changes in the national military and political situation. During the Three Kingdoms period, Pingyang County was first established near Shangjin; during the Northern and Southern Dynasties, it successively became Shangluo Commandery and Shangjin Commandery, and became the seat of the provincial-level administrative region Shangzhou; from the Sui Dynasty onward, it was downgraded to Shangjin County and remained so until the Ming Dynasty, and in the Kangxi period of the Qing it was further downgraded to Shangjin Fort. This shows that during periods of division and war, especially when the opposing regimes of the north and south took the Qinling Mountains as the boundary and the upper Han River became an important object of contention, the military position of Shangjin would become prominent. The importance of Shangjin in water and land transportation is manifested in that by waterway it can lead southwest to Ankang and Hanzhong, southeast to Xiangyang and Wuhan; by land route it leads northwest to Chang'an and northeast to Luoyang. When Li Xian, Emperor Zhongzong of Tang, was demoted to Prince of Luling and went to Junzhou (today Junxian Town, Danjiangkou City), he dismounted and boarded a boat here, hence the dock at the west gate of the ancient city is also called 'Son of Heaven Ferry.' It is said that when war refugees came to live in Shangjin, they would bring a willow branch from their hometown to express their homesickness; over time, Shangjin became shaded with willows and was also called Liuzhou (Willow City). The current Shangjin ancient city wall was built in the 2nd year of Jiajing, Ming (1523), rebuilt in the 7th year of Jiaqing, Qing (1802), and after becoming a national cultural heritage protection unit in 2005, it underwent another large-scale renovation. The plane of the city is a narrow rectangle about 30 meters east-west and 300 meters north-south, with stone-built wall foundations and brick-built city walls, nearly 7 meters high, with a moat outside. There are five city gates: the east is 'Xiangyun' (toward Yun), the west is 'Tonghan' (to Han), the south is 'Dachu' (to Chu), the north is 'Jieqin' (connecting Qin), and there is also a small west gate in the southwest for the convenience of residents entering and exiting. In the city, slightly west of center, there is a north-south main street; from the west gate to the main street there is also a small street; in addition, outside the north gate, an old cobblestone street and two rows of old residences are preserved. On a small hill northeast of the city, there is also a Shaanxi-Shanxi Guild Hall, also called the Guandi Temple, built at the turn of the Qianlong and Jiaqing periods of the Qing; now only one entry of the courtyard of the main hall remains. Its plane is three bays wide, with a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, and the first entry has a curved roof. Inside the hall, Guandi is enshrined; it was an important place for Shaanxi-Shanxi merchants to sacrifice to Guan Gong, fellowship with fellow townspeople, and engage in commercial activities.

projects.name: 铁山寺宝塔
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 店子镇铁山寺村，301省道北侧
projects.address_en: Tieshansi Village, Dianzi Town, north side of Provincial Highway 301
highlights: 从上津镇继续向前沿着301省道继续行驶约45分钟
道路北侧山脚下的地方
边停车沿着田间小路跨过一条清澈的小溪
近距离地观察这座铁山寺塔
原本是一座六角十三级的楼阁式实心砖塔
由于山谷中泥沙的淤积
目前露出地面的仅有五层半
projects.content_zh: 从上津镇继续向前，沿着301省道继续行驶约45分钟，在道路北侧山脚下的地方，可以看到一座并不起眼的小塔。在边停车，沿着田间小路跨过一条清澈的小溪，穿过一片水稻田，就可以近距离地观察这座铁山寺塔了。塔建于明代，原本是一座六角十三级的楼阁式实心砖塔，由于山谷中泥沙的淤积，目前露出地面的仅有五层半，高约10米，逐层收分。塔刹也已毁坏，
projects.content_en: Continuing forward from Shangjin Town, driving along Provincial Highway 301 for about 45 minutes, at the foot of the mountain on the north side of the road, one can see an inconspicuous small pagoda. Parking by the roadside, crossing a clear stream along a field path, and passing through a rice paddy, one can observe this Tieshan Temple Pagoda up close. The pagoda was built in the Ming Dynasty; it was originally a hexagonal thirteen-story pavilion-style solid brick pagoda. Due to sedimentation in the valley, currently only five and a half stories are exposed above the ground, about 10 meters high, tapering story by story. The pagoda finial has also been destroyed,

projects.content_zh: 甘氏宗祠是十堰市规模最大，保存也相对完整的宗祠之一，主体建筑始建于乾隆十九年（1754），光绪十四年（1888）增修，是为了纪念清康熙年间族长甘继芳在与地方叛军的战斗中为国捐躯而兴建的。康熙十四年（1675），鄂西北守军响应吴三桂叛乱，竹溪扼守陕、鄂之间，因而成为叛军争夺的要点。当时的知县曹席珍由于县城没有城墙，率官民退守到城西30里的中峰寨，与甘继芳合力抗敌。早先明末动乱时期，甘继芳便带领乡民抵御流寇的滋扰，在10余年间多次将其击退。甘、曹二人在山中困守60天，敌人始终无法攻破。这时曹知县一个名为曹二的门役因为犯错受到责罚，便偷偷下山，与一个名叫'马蹶子'的叛军合伙，带领叛军从后山的绝壁攻入山寨，捉住了甘继芳和曹知县。甘继芳拒绝与叛军合作，慷慨赴死，年64岁；而曹知县则辗转逃至京城，甘继芳的事迹也因而得以流传，清政府为了褒奖忠义之士，赐匾3块，准立宗祠。建筑坐南朝北，中路为两进殿堂，有一个天井院；东侧为民国三年（1914）增建的官厅。整体由青砖砌筑，各个单体均为单檐硬山灰瓦顶。官厅面阔五间，屋脊两端上翘呈凹曲线，两侧山墙突出高起的墀头装饰；正中入口为高耸的三间仿木牌楼，中间匾额书'甘宗祠'，门前一对抱鼓石，两侧两扇雕花石窗。
projects.content_en: Gan's Ancestral Hall is one of the largest and relatively well-preserved ancestral halls in Shiyan City. The main building was first built in the 19th year of Qianlong, Qing (1754), and expanded in the 14th year of Guangxu (1888), built to commemorate the clan leader Gan Jifang who died for his country in battle against local rebel forces during the Kangxi period of the Qing. In the 14th year of Kangxi (1675), the garrison in northwestern Hubei responded to Wu Sangui rebellion; Zhuxi, guarding the pass between Shaanxi and Hubei, thus became a key point contested by the rebels. At that time, the county magistrate Cao Xizhen, because the county seat had no city wall, led officials and people to retreat to Zhongfeng Stockade 30 li west of the city, and joined forces with Gan Jifang to resist the enemy. Earlier, during the late Ming turmoil, Gan Jifang led villagers to resist the harassment of roving bandits, repelling them many times over more than 10 years. Gan and Cao were besieged in the mountain for 60 days, and the enemy was never able to break through. At this time, a servant of Magistrate Cao named Cao Er, because he had been punished for a mistake, secretly went down the mountain and partnered with a rebel named 'Majuzi,' leading the rebels to attack the stockade from the precipice at the back of the mountain, capturing Gan Jifang and Magistrate Cao. Gan Jifang refused to cooperate with the rebels and died heroically at the age of 64; while Magistrate Cao escaped to the capital after many twists and turns, and Gan Jifang deeds thus spread. The Qing government, to commend the loyal and righteous, bestowed 3 plaques and permitted the establishment of an ancestral hall. The building faces north from south, with the central route being two-entry halls and one courtyard; on the east side is the official hall added in the 3rd year of the Republic (1914). The whole is built of blue bricks, and each individual unit has a single-eave gable gray-tile roof. The official hall is five bays wide, with both ends of the ridge upturned in a concave curve, and the gable walls on both sides protrude with high chi tou (gable-end) decorations; the central entrance is a towering three-bay imitation-wood paifang, with the central plaque reading 'Gan Ancestral Hall,' a pair of drum-holding stones in front of the gate, and two carved stone windows on both sides.

projects.content_zh: 敖宗祠是十堰地区另一座典型的祠堂，外观和平面布局与甘氏宗祠相似而规模较小，为中路两进殿堂和一个天井院，左手有侧院，各个单体山墙的形状也与甘氏宗祠一致，不过由于进深较小，侧院的云形山墙已经简化成了一段圆弧。据族谱记载，敖宗祠始建于明朝，而现存建筑的修建年代应不早于清中期。祠堂石雕、砖雕、木雕工艺精致，特别是主人口的砖砌牌楼，四根盘龙石柱，大门上置竖匾，上书'敖宗祠'，石柱和匾额的四周都贴有各色瓷片。但可惜的是建筑内部已损毁殆尽，正殿坍圮，仅残余外部一层空壳。
projects.content_en: Ao's Ancestral Hall is another typical ancestral hall in the Shiyan area; its appearance and plane layout are similar to Gan's Ancestral Hall but smaller in scale, with the central route being two-entry halls and one courtyard, a side courtyard on the left, and the shape of each individual gable wall also consistent with Gan's Ancestral Hall; however, due to the smaller depth, the cloud-shaped gable wall of the side courtyard has been simplified into a circular arc. According to the genealogy, Ao's Ancestral Hall was first built in the Ming Dynasty, and the construction date of the existing building should not be earlier than the mid-Qing. The stone carving, brick carving, and wood carving craftsmanship of the ancestral hall are exquisite, especially the brick paifang at the main entrance, with four dragon-coiled stone columns; a vertical plaque is placed above the main gate, inscribed with 'Ao Ancestral Hall,' and various colored porcelain pieces are pasted around the stone columns and plaque. Unfortunately, the interior of the building has been completely destroyed, the main hall has collapsed, and only an outer one-story empty shell remains.

projects.name_en: Dacheng Hall of Temple of Confucius

highlights: 竹山文庙始建于明洪武十三年
projects.content_zh: 竹山文庙始建于明洪武十三年（1380），毁于明末，清初重建，清道光二十一年（1841）修缮，现仅存大成殿。大殿坐北朝南，面宽五间，重檐歇山灰瓦顶，砖木结构，抬梁式构架，屋顶高耸。三面有外廊，正面为槅扇门窗，方砖墁地。
projects.content_en: Zhushan Confucian Temple was first built in the 13th year of Hongwu, Ming (1380), destroyed in the late Ming, rebuilt in the early Qing, and repaired in the 21st year of Daoguang, Qing (1841); now only the Dacheng (Great Achievement) Hall remains. The main hall faces south, five bays wide, with a double-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, brick-wood structure, post-and-lintel frame, and a towering roof. It has exterior corridors on three sides, with lattice doors and windows on the front and square brick paving on the ground.

projects.content_zh: 上庸古建筑群包括三盛院和黄州会馆两组天井式四合院，是为配合潘口水电站的建设而分别从两处搬迁至此的。三盛院原先位于官渡河与泗河交汇的两河口，是一组有六路院落的超大型民居组群，于清朝嘉庆末年完工，有大小48个天井，房屋千余间，地跨竹山、竹溪两县，但因年久失修，搬迁前便已所剩无几。这一建筑群是王氏家族经商积累财富后在家乡建造的豪宅，'三盛'三字由慈禧太后亲笔题写，既是家族的名号，也用作商号，寓意人盛、地盛、财盛。六路院落分为北路三进，南三路三进，坐西朝东，呈'王'字形扩展布局。三盛院现存部分是搬迁前保存状况较好的两进天井院，作为民俗博物馆使用。建筑高两层，硬山灰瓦顶，檐下有一圈彩绘和彩塑装饰。各处门窗均有精美的石雕装饰，题材丰富、各不相同。大门上石匾书'紫气东来'四字；门楣浮雕人物生活场景，角部饰以历史人物，下侧为一对麒麟舞丝带、滚绣球；石门墩各个面上亦有花木、丝带、龙纹等雕刻装饰。此外，大门右侧的外墙上还有一对雕刻极精致的葡萄缠枝纹镂
projects.content_en: The Shangyong Ancient Building Complex includes two groups of courtyard-style quadrangles: the Sansheng Courtyard and the Huangzhou Guild Hall, which were relocated here from two places respectively to配合 the construction of the Pankou Hydropower Station. The Sansheng Courtyard was originally located at Lianghekou, where the Guandu River and Si River meet; it is a super-large residential building group with six routes of courtyards, completed in the late Jiaqing period of the Qing, with 48 courtyards of various sizes and more than a thousand rooms, spanning both Zhushan and Zhuxi counties; but due to long-term neglect and disrepair, little remained before relocation. This building complex was a mansion built by the Wang family after accumulating wealth through business in their hometown; the three characters 'Sansheng' were personally inscribed by Empress Dowager Cixi, serving both as the family name and as a trade name, meaning prosperity of people, land, and wealth. The six routes of courtyards are divided into the north route with three entries and the south three routes with three entries, facing east from west, in an expanded layout shaped like the character 'Wang' (king). The existing part of Sansheng Courtyard is the two-entry courtyard that was in relatively good preservation before relocation, used as a folk custom museum. The building is two stories high, with a gable gray-tile roof and a ring of painted and colored sculpture decorations under the eaves. Doors and windows everywhere have exquisite stone carving decorations, with rich and varied themes. On the stone plaque above the main gate are written the four characters 'Purple Qi Comes from the East'; the door lintel has relief sculptures of figure life scenes, with historical figures decorating the corners, and below is a pair of kylins dancing with ribbons and rolling embroidered balls; each face of the stone door piers also has carvings of flowers and trees, ribbons, dragon patterns, etc. In addition, on the exterior wall to the right of the main gate, there is also a pair of exquisitely carved grape-vine pattern openwork
