projects.content_zh: 相比于三盛院的名动一方，高家花屋位于更加偏僻的鄂陕边界，也正因地远难行，得以相对完好地保存到今天。这座前后有三进院落的大宅子坐北朝南，背山临渊，选址极佳。大门正对远处的最高峰，门高约12米，两侧有八字墙，门前是13级青石板台阶，如此气派的入口在一般的民居中很少见到，让人不禁联想到宏丽的宫殿或庙宇。据当地老人讲，高家花屋原有房间57间，除正房、粮仓外，还有吊酒房、当铺、钱庄等商业用房十几间，逢年过节，方圆100多公里内都有人上这儿来典当、拆借，是一座名副其实的豪宅。两百年之后，这些房屋中有48间幸存下来，而类似这样的花屋，户主高方在世时共建了9座，保存至今的是其中最豪华的一座。房屋刚盖了一半，高方便去世了，他的后代子孙又用了20年时间终于完工，至今当地仍然有民谣唱道：'高家盖房，三十年散板……'从花屋放眼望去，四周全是灰灰的大山，这样一座超级四合院是怎样建起来的呢？据说，高方与父亲高启元本要从武昌去西安，走到解家沟时人困马乏，看到草房，想到草房之内正是无雪之地，当即拆除草房安葬母亲，从此以后便财运不断。另一个传说是'豪赌兴家'，说高方做长工时虽然肯下力干活，却也因为食量大而被东家嫌弃，闲来无聊便去看赌博，结果逢赌必赢，堪称'赌王'。不过，从花屋的建造过程来看，这些传说也仅仅是耸人听闻，能够不惜巨大的人力物力在如此偏远的地方，建造这样一座颇有归隐意味的豪宅，又能开设粮铺、杂货铺、当铺，可见高方应是一个家底殷实又善于经营的人。
projects.content_en: Compared with the fame of Sansheng Courtyard, Gao Family Huawu (Ornamental House) is located at the more remote Hubei-Shaanxi border, and precisely because it is far and difficult to reach, it has been relatively well-preserved to this day. This large mansion with three courtyards front and back faces south, with mountains at its back and an abyss in front, with an excellent site selection. The main gate faces directly the highest peak in the distance; the gate is about 12 meters high, with splayed walls on both sides, and in front of the gate are 13 blue stone slab steps; such an imposing entrance is rarely seen in ordinary residences, making one不禁 think of magnificent palaces or temples. According to local elders, Gao Family Huawu originally had 57 rooms; besides the main house and granary, there were also more than ten commercial rooms such as wine distillery, pawnshop, and money shop; during festivals, people from within a radius of more than 100 kilometers would come here to pawn and borrow, making it a veritable mansion. Two hundred years later, 48 of these rooms survived; and similar ornamental houses, when the owner Gao Fang was alive, he built a total of 9, and the one preserved to this day is the most luxurious among them. When the house was only half built, Gao Fang passed away, and his descendants spent another 20 years finally completing it; to this day, there is still a folk ballad locally singing: 'The Gao family builds a house, thirty years of scattered boards...' Looking out from the ornamental house, all around are gray mountains; how was such a super quadrangle built? It is said that Gao Fang and his father Gao Qiyuan were originally going from Wuchang to Xi'an; when they reached Xiejiagou, both man and horse were exhausted; seeing a thatched house and thinking that inside the thatched house was a snow-free place, they immediately demolished the thatched house to bury their mother, and from then on their wealth continued to grow. Another legend is 'getting rich through extravagant gambling,' saying that when Gao Fang worked as a hired laborer, although he was willing to work hard, he was also disliked by his employer because of his large appetite; when bored, he went to watch gambling, and as a result won every bet, worthy of being called the 'King of Gamblers.' However, from the construction process of the ornamental house, these legends are merely sensational; being able to spare no expense in manpower and material resources to build such a mansion with a sense of seclusion in such a remote place, and also being able to open grain shops, grocery stores, and pawnshops, shows that Gao Fang should have been a person with a solid family background and good at business.

一说东汉方士费长房在此显圣
而种种说法之事迹均难以考证
projects.content_zh: 始建于乾隆十四年（1749），道光二年（1822）重修，现存一座武圣宫和两侧配殿，咸丰十年（1860）又在后山之巅增修金顶。整个建筑群依山面水，从山脚一侧的大门可以拾阶而上。武圣宫为二层楼阁，单檐歇山灰瓦屋顶，屋角翘起，戗脊上施以仙人走兽装饰。两座配殿均为五间二层楼，有外廊，而大殿前方的一座为砖木混合结构，单檐硬山屋顶，而后方的则以木结构为主，重檐硬山屋顶。'显圣'一名众说纷纭，从武圣宫来看，显圣者当为关羽；而一说修建此殿时鲁班曾显圣，一说东汉方士费长房在此显圣，而种种说法之事迹均难以考证。
projects.content_en: It was first built in the 14th year of Qianlong (1749), rebuilt in the 2nd year of Daoguang (1822); currently there is one Wusheng (Martial Sage) Palace and two side halls, and in the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860), a Golden Summit was additionally built on the top of the back mountain. The entire building complex leans against the mountain and faces the water; from the gate on one side at the foot of the mountain, one can climb up the steps. The Wusheng Palace is a two-story pavilion, with a single-eave hip-and-gable gray-tile roof, upturned roof corners, and immortal and animal decorations on the diagonal ridges. The two side halls are both five-bay two-story buildings with exterior corridors; the one in front of the main hall is of brick-wood mixed structure with a single-eave gable roof, while the one at the rear is mainly of wooden structure with a double-eave gable roof. The name 'Xiansheng' (Manifesting Sage) has various explanations; from the Wusheng Palace, the one who manifests sage should be Guan Yu; while one saying is that Lu Ban manifested sage when this hall was built, another saying is that the Eastern Han alchemist Fei Changfang manifested sage here, but the deeds of various sayings are all difficult to verify.

projects.name: 彭家祠堂
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 门古寺镇彭家湾村
projects.address_en: Pengjiawan Village, Mengusi Town
highlights: 落成后第三年在祠堂中开设族塾
1920年改为彭家湾私立民族小学
解放后改为彭家湾小学
新四军曾在此祠堂中办公
除了大门上方高耸起三间垂花柱式的牌楼和门前一对抱鼓石
并无多余的雕刻或彩画装饰
引人注目的是牌楼正中的匾额不书彭宗祠
彭氏曾有一位先祖在科举考试中取得不错的名次
因而彭氏在修建祠堂时得到了光绪皇帝恩准
彭氏宗族进京赶考被封为府案
彭氏家族要建祠堂荣耀祖德
并由皇帝亲笔书写圣宗祠镌于匾额之上
祠堂在中轴线上为两进三天井院
门窗、梁柱上各有祥瑞动物的木雕
墙上还绘有二十四孝壁画
虽然遭到了一定的破坏
匾上文字一直难以辨识
直到村民走访到曾在祠堂中教书的86岁退休教师张发祥
彭氏的母亲刘氏贤惠善良、教子有方
光绪皇帝派大学士李家驹书淑德延年赐赠
其中淑字因为是异体字
projects.content_zh: 建于清光绪二十九年（1903），落成后第三年在祠堂中开设族塾，1920年改为'彭家湾私立民族小学'，解放后改为彭家湾小学，新四军曾在此祠堂中办公。彭家祠堂外观朴素，除了大门上方高耸起三间垂花柱式的牌楼和门前一对抱鼓石，并无多余的雕刻或彩画装饰。引人注目的是牌楼正中的匾额不书'彭宗祠'，而是写着'圣宗祠'三字。据祠中的碑文记载，彭氏曾有一位先祖在科举考试中取得不错的名次，因而彭氏在修建祠堂时得到了光绪皇帝恩准，彭氏宗族进京赶考被封为府案，彭和忠考中县案。彭氏家族要建祠堂荣耀祖德，得到光绪皇帝恩准，并由皇帝亲笔书写'圣宗祠'镌于匾额之上。祠堂在中轴线上为两进三天井院，门窗、梁柱上各有祥瑞动物的木雕，墙上还绘有二十四孝壁画，虽然遭到了一定的破坏，但保存相对完好，实属不易。值得一提的是，祠中还有一块长4米，宽1.5米，厚4厘米的巨型木匾，匾上文字一直难以辨识，直到村民走访到曾在祠堂中教书的86岁退休教师张发祥，才破出文字的内容。原来，彭氏退休教师张发祥，彭氏的母亲刘氏贤惠善良、教子有方，光绪皇帝派大学士李家驹书'淑德延年'赐赠，其中'淑'字因为是异体字，困扰了专家们多年。
projects.content_en: It was built in the 29th year of Guangxu, Qing (1903); three years after completion, a clan school was opened in the ancestral hall; in 1920 it was changed to 'Pengjiawan Private Ethnic Primary School'; after liberation it was changed to Pengjiawan Primary School; the New Fourth Army once worked in this ancestral hall. Peng's Ancestral Hall has a simple appearance; except for the towering three-bay hanging-column-style paifang above the main gate and a pair of drum-holding stones in front of the gate, there is no多余 carving or painted decoration. What is striking is that the plaque in the center of the paifang does not read 'Peng Ancestral Hall,' but writes the three characters 'Sheng Ancestral Hall.' According to the inscriptions in the hall, one of the Peng ancestors achieved a good ranking in the imperial examinations, so when the Peng family built the ancestral hall, they received the approval of Emperor Guangxu; the Peng clan went to the capital to take the exam and was enfeoffed as fu an (prefectural case), and Peng Hezhong passed the county case. The Peng family wanted to build an ancestral hall to glorify the ancestral virtue, received the approval of Emperor Guangxu, and the emperor personally wrote 'Sheng Ancestral Hall' to be engraved on the plaque. The ancestral hall, on the central axis, is two entries with three courtyards; on the doors, windows, beams, and columns there are wood carvings of auspicious animals, and the walls are also painted with the Twenty-four Filial Piety murals; although they have suffered some damage, they are relatively well-preserved, which is really not easy. It is worth mentioning that there is also a giant wooden plaque in the hall, 4 meters long, 1.5 meters wide, and 4 centimeters thick; the text on the plaque had always been difficult to identify, until the villagers visited the 86-year-old retired teacher Zhang Faxiang who once taught in the ancestral hall, and then the content of the text was deciphered. It turned out that the mother of the Peng family, Liu Shi, was virtuous and kind, and good at teaching children; Emperor Guangxu sent the grand secretary Li Jiaju to write 'Shu De Yan Nian' (Virtuous Virtue Prolongs Years) as a gift; among them, the character 'Shu' (virtuous), because it was a variant character, puzzled experts for many years.

projects.name: 三闾书院
projects.level: 省级重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 阳日镇阳日大道22号
projects.address_en: No. 22, Yangri Avenue, Yangri Town
highlights: 时任湖北省学政的孙为曾为其题送冬雪春晖匾额
占地曾达到一千余平方米
建筑有门楼、大殿、东西耳房、东西厢房和斋房
大殿为单檐硬山灰瓦屋顶
面阔和进深均为三开间
脊檩两段分别书写三闾书院合众首士修建大清道光丁酉年九月吉旦
部分墙砖上还依稀可见武昌二字
据说大殿立柱为马桑树
马桑树被认为是无法成材的树种
因此用这种木料修建大殿
寄托了客居此地的武昌人望子成材的心愿
projects.content_zh: 又名武昌书院、武昌庙，始建于清道光十七年（1837），时任湖北省学政的孙为曾为其题送'冬雪春晖'匾额，至今悬于大殿檐下。书院坐北朝南，占地曾达到一千余平方米，建筑有门楼、大殿、东西耳房、东西厢房和斋房，现仅存大殿。大殿为单檐硬山灰瓦屋顶，面阔和进深均为三开间，正面有前廊，抬梁式木结构，脊檩两段分别书写'三闾书院合众首士修建''大清道光丁酉年九月吉旦'。屋脊有仙人走兽，山墙彩绘装饰，部分墙砖上还依稀可见'武昌'二字。据说大殿立柱为马桑树，而在鄂西一带，马桑树被认为是无法成材的树种，因此用这种木料修建大殿，寄托了客居此地的武昌人望子成材的心愿。
projects.content_en: Also called Wuchang Academy or Wuchang Temple, it was first built in the 17th year of Daoguang, Qing (1837); Sun Wei, then the education commissioner of Hubei Province, once presented it with a plaque inscribed 'Winter Snow and Spring Sunshine,' which still hangs under the eaves of the main hall today. The academy faces south, once covering more than a thousand square meters; the buildings included a gate tower, main hall, east and west side rooms, east and west wing rooms, and study rooms; now only the main hall remains. The main hall has a single-eave gable gray-tile roof, with both the width and depth being three bays, a front porch on the front, and a post-and-lintel wooden structure; the two sections of the ridge purlin are respectively inscribed with 'Sanlü Academy built by all the leading gentlemen' and 'Auspicious day of the 9th month of the Dingyou year of Daoguang, Qing.' The roof ridge has immortal and animal decorations, the gable walls have painted decorations, and on some wall bricks the two characters 'Wuchang' can still be faintly seen. It is said that the columns of the main hall are made of matang (coral) tree wood; in western Hubei, the matang tree is considered a tree species that cannot become useful timber, so using this kind of wood to build the main hall expressed the wish of the Wuchang people living here as guests for their children to become talented.
